definition_zh: 范围；领域；余地；视野；（观察）镜；作用域
definition_en: the area or range that something covers, the room available for action, or an instrument used for viewing
core_image: 一支镜筒对准远处的靶标，镜筒框住的那一片就是“范围”
scene: 项目启动会上，负责人在白板上画了一个大圆圈，把要做的事都写进去，圈外的事则标为不在范围内。他说：Let us agree on the scope first.
sceneCN: 这里 scope 是「项目所覆盖的范围」（第 1、8 个义项：主题广度与项目边界）；句意：我们先确定项目的范围。图中可辨识物件：白板、大圆圈、清单、马克笔。

pos.zh: 范围；领域；余地；视野；（观察）镜
仔细察看；摸底（非正式，多用于 scope out）

senses.title: The breadth a subject covers
senses.definition: the range of subjects, activities or information that something deals with or includes
senses.definitionCN: 某事物所涉及或包含的主题、活动或信息的范围
senses.example: The scope of the study was limited to coastal waters.
senses.exampleCN: 这项研究的范围限于近岸水域。
senses.why: Greek skopos was the mark a watcher aimed at. The mark does not cover the whole landscape; it fixes how much of it is in play. Scope begins as that bounded field.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 skopos 是观察者瞄准的那个标记。标记并不覆盖整片风景，它只确定有多大一片进入视野。scope 的起点正是这块有边界的场。

senses.title: Room left for action
senses.definition: the opportunity or space available for doing something more or doing it better
senses.definitionCN: 可以做得更多或做得更好的机会与空间
senses.example: There is still scope for improvement in the design.
senses.exampleCN: 这个设计仍有改进的余地。
senses.why: If the mark defines the field, the empty part of the field is free for movement. From 'how much is covered' the word slides to 'how much is left open'.
senses.whyCN: 如果标记划出了场地，场中空着的部分就可以活动。于是词义从“覆盖多少”滑向“还空着多少”。

senses.title: The reach of a rule or law
senses.titleCN: 规则或法律的效力范围
senses.definition: the range of cases, people or situations to which a rule, law, agreement or power applies
senses.definitionCN: 规则、法律、协议或权力所适用的案件、人或情境的范围
senses.example: The new tax falls outside the scope of this agreement.
senses.exampleCN: 这项新税不在本协议的适用范围之内。
senses.why: A law draws a line around itself exactly as a mark draws a circle. What lies inside the line is governed; what lies outside is not reached.
senses.whyCN: 法律给自己画了一条界线，正如标记画出一个圆圈。线内的受管辖，线外的够不着。

senses.title: One's field of activity or duty
senses.definition: the area of activity that a person, department or organization is responsible for
senses.definitionCN: 个人、部门或组织负责的活动领域
senses.example: Marketing is outside my scope; I only handle production.
senses.exampleCN: 营销不在我的职责范围内，我只负责生产。
senses.why: A person is assigned a portion of the whole field, and that portion becomes the boundary of their responsibility. Scope here is jurisdiction in everyday dress.
senses.whyCN: 一个人被分派到整块场地中的一部分，这一部分就成了其责任的边界。此义的 scope 就是日常说法里的“管辖范围”。

senses.title: The range of vision
senses.definition: the distance or area that can be seen, especially in literary description
senses.definitionCN: 能够看见的距离或区域，尤用于文学描写
senses.example: The tower came within the scope of the lookout's glass.
senses.exampleCN: 那座塔进入了瞭望手望远镜的视野。
senses.why: The oldest layer of skopos is watching. Before scope meant a rule's reach, it meant how far a pair of eyes could reach across open ground.
senses.whyCN: skopos 最古老的一层意思是“看”。在 scope 表示规则效力之前，它表示一双眼睛在开阔地面上能看多远。

senses.title: An instrument that lets you see
senses.definition: a device for viewing, especially one named with the suffix -scope, such as a microscope or endoscope
senses.definitionCN: 用于观察的器械，尤指以 -scope 结尾命名的仪器，如显微镜、内窥镜
senses.example: The clinic bought a new scope for examining joints.
senses.exampleCN: 诊所买了一台检查关节的新内窥镜。
senses.why: The suffix -scope turns skopos 'watcher' into 'instrument that watches'. The noun scope alone is a clipped form of microscope, telescope and similar devices.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -scope 把 skopos“观看者”变成“观看的器械”。单独使用的名词 scope 是 microscope、telescope 这类词的截短形式。

senses.title: Where a name is visible: programming scope
senses.titleCN: 名字可见的范围：编程作用域
senses.definition: in programming, the region of a program in which a declared name can be used
senses.definitionCN: 在编程中，一个已声明的名字可以被使用的程序区域
senses.example: A variable declared inside the loop has local scope.
senses.exampleCN: 在循环内部声明的变量具有局部作用域。
senses.why: A name is 'visible' only inside its own region, just as an object is visible only inside the field of the lens. Computing borrowed the optical metaphor almost unchanged.
senses.whyCN: 一个名字只在自己的区域内“可见”，正如物体只在镜头的视场内可见。计算机领域几乎原样借用了这个光学比喻。

senses.title: The agreed boundary of a project
senses.definition: in project management, the defined set of work and deliverables that a project will and will not include
senses.definitionCN: 项目管理中，一个项目将做与不做的既定工作与交付物集合
senses.example: The team agreed on the scope before signing the contract.
senses.exampleCN: 团队在签合同前先确定了项目范围。
senses.why: Modern management made the circle explicit: everything inside is scope, everything outside is out of scope. The Greek mark has become a contract line.
senses.whyCN: 现代管理把这个圆圈明确化了：圈内都是 scope，圈外都是 out of scope。希腊人的标记变成了合同上的界线。

senses.title: To look something over: the verb
senses.definition: to examine or assess something, especially quickly and informally, often in the phrase scope out
senses.definitionCN: 察看或评估某事物，尤指快速、非正式地，常用于短语 scope out
senses.example: They scoped the venue before the concert.
senses.exampleCN: 演出前他们先去察看了场地。
senses.why: The verb returns to the root's plain act of looking. To scope a place is to put it inside your field of vision before you act.
senses.whyCN: 动词回到了词根最朴素的“看”。scope 一个地方，就是在行动之前先把它放进自己的视野。

intro.en: Scope is a Greek word that travelled through Latin and Italian before it became English. Its core is skopos, 'a mark to aim at', and everything the word means grows from the idea of a bounded field held in view.
intro.cn: scope 是一个希腊词，经拉丁语和意大利语进入英语。核心是 skopos“瞄准的标记”，它的全部词义都从“被目光框住的一块场地”这个意象生长出来。

items.en: Skopos meant 'a watcher, one who looks out; a mark or target aimed at; an object of observation'. The double sense of person and target is already present in Homeric Greek.
items.cn: skopos 意为“观看者、瞭望者；瞄准的标记或靶子；观察的对象”。人与靶标这两重意思在荷马时代的希腊语中就已存在。

items.en: Skopos is explained as a metathesized form of PIE *spek-yo-, from the root *spek- 'to observe'. The same root gives Greek skeptesthai 'to look at, examine' and Latin haruspex 'entrail-inspector'.
items.cn: skopos 被解释为原始印欧语 *spek-yo- 的换位形式，出自词根 *spek-“观察”。同一词根也给出希腊语 skeptesthai“看、审视”和拉丁语 haruspex“肠卜师”。

items.en: Latin borrowed skopos as scopus, 'aim, purpose, object'. Roman writers used it mostly in the abstract sense of a goal one aims at rather than a physical target.
items.cn: 拉丁语把 skopos 借作 scopus，意为“目标、目的、对象”。罗马作家多用其抽象义，指人瞄准的目的，而不是实物靶子。

items.en: Italian scopo inherited both 'aim, purpose' and 'field of view'. It was the direct source of the English word, which is why English scope carries purpose and range at once.
items.cn: 意大利语 scopo 同时继承了“目的”与“视野范围”两义。它是英语词的直接来源，因此英语 scope 一身兼有“目的”与“范围”。

items.en: English first recorded scope in the 1530s meaning 'room to act, free play', and in the 1550s 'space to move in'. The classical sense 'a mark to shoot at' appears in the 1560s but is now obsolete.
items.cn: 英语最早在 16 世纪 30 年代记录 scope，意为“行动余地、自由活动”；16 世纪 50 年代又指“可移动的空间”。古典义“射击瞄准的标记”在 16 世纪 60 年代出现，现已废弃。

items.en: Intellectual range is recorded from c. 1600 and spatial extent from the 1590s; 'sphere of activity' from 1830. The instrument sense (1872) is a clipping of telescope and microscope. The verb dates from 1807, and the slang 'look at, examine' (scope out) from 1985. Programming and project-management senses are 20th-century extensions.
items.cn: “智力所及的范围”自 1600 年前后有记录，“空间广度”自 16 世纪 90 年代起，“活动领域”自 1830 年起。仪器义（1872）是 telescope 与 microscope 的截短。动词始于 1807 年，俚语义“察看、摸底”（scope out）始于 1985 年。编程与项目管理义都是 20 世纪的延伸。

note.en: The first group collects words that look or sound close to scope; the second collects words that share part of its meaning. Form first, then sense.
note.cn: 第一组收集与 scope 形音相近的词，第二组收集与它部分同义的词。先看形音，再看词义。

entries.definition: a deep shovel, or an exclusive news story. It differs from scope by the final consonant and by its image of digging.
entries.definitionCN: 深口铲；独家新闻。它与 scope 只差末尾辅音，意象是“挖”。

entries.definition: a surface that rises or falls at an angle. It shares the -ope ending but comes from a different root meaning 'slant'.
entries.definitionCN: 斜面；坡度。它同样以 -ope 结尾，但词根不同，意为“倾斜”。

entries.definition: the act of defining or examining a range; the present participle and verbal noun of scope. It is not a separate root word.
entries.definitionCN: 界定或察看范围的行为；scope 的现在分词与动名词。它不是独立的词根词。

entries.definition: the extent of variation or coverage between limits. It is more quantitative than scope and often names a measured spread.
entries.definitionCN: 变化或覆盖的幅度。它比 scope 更偏量化，常指可测量的跨度。

entries.definition: the size or degree to which something extends. It measures how far something reaches rather than what it includes.
entries.definitionCN: 某物延伸的大小或程度。它衡量伸得多远，而不是包含什么。

entries.definition: the scope of someone's authority or responsibility. It is formal and almost always tied to an office or a law.
entries.definitionCN: 某人的职权或责任范围。它是正式用语，几乎总与职位或法律绑定。

entries.definition: freedom to act within limits, or distance north or south of the equator. Only the first sense overlaps with scope as 'room to act'.
entries.definitionCN: 在限度内的行动自由；纬度。只有第一个义项与 scope 的“余地”重叠。

normalIntro.en: Concrete images first: a target, a lens, a circle drawn on a whiteboard. Each image pins one cluster of senses.
normalIntro.cn: 先给具体画面：靶标、镜头、白板上画的圆圈。每个画面固定一组义项。

normal.en: A marksman's target defines a field: everything he can hit is in scope, everything else is out of scope.
normal.cn: 射手的目标划出一块场地：打得中的都在 scope 内，其余都在 scope 外。

normal.en: A telescope's -scope is a watcher: the tube frames exactly the patch of sky you are allowed to see.
normal.cn: 望远镜的 -scope 就是“观看者”：镜筒框住的正是你能看见的那一小片天空。

normal.en: Scope for improvement is the empty space inside the circle: the work is bounded, but not filled.
normal.cn: scope for improvement 就是圆圈里的空白：工作有边界，但还没填满。

normal.en: A project's scope is a circle on a whiteboard; anything outside the line is politely called out of scope.
normal.cn: 项目范围就是白板上的一个圆圈；线外的东西被客气地称为 out of scope。

normal.en: A variable's scope is the region where its name is visible, like an object visible only through one window.
normal.cn: 变量的作用域就是它的名字可见的区域，就像只能透过某一扇窗看见的物体。

abstract.en: Hold one schema: MARK → FIELD → BOUNDARY → ROOM. Every sense of scope is one of these four stops.
abstract.cn: 记住一个图式：标记 → 场地 → 边界 → 余地。scope 的每个义项都是这四个站点之一。

abstract.en: Follow the root chain: Greek skopos → Latin scopus → Italian scopo → English scope. The meaning narrows from 'watcher' to 'field watched'.
abstract.cn: 沿词根链走：希腊 skopos → 拉丁 scopus → 意大利 scopo → 英语 scope。词义从“观看者”收窄为“被观看的场地”。

abstract.en: Contrast pairs: scope (range) vs scoop (shovel); scope (view) vs slope (slant). One letter, a different image.
abstract.cn: 对照记忆：scope（范围）对 scoop（铲子）；scope（视野）对 slope（斜面）。差一个字母，换一幅图。

examples.en: The scope of the investigation was widened to include the whole supply chain.
examples.cn: 调查范围被扩大到整条供应链。

examples.en: This job gives me plenty of scope for using my own judgment.
examples.cn: 这份工作给了我很大的自主判断空间。

examples.en: Anything beyond the scope of the treaty must be negotiated separately.
examples.cn: 超出条约范围的事项必须另行谈判。

dict_mnemonic.text: “四阔普”——四（处）阔（大）的普（及面）→ 铺开多大就是多大范围 → scope 范围、余地

root: 源自希腊语 skopos“观看者、瞄准的靶标”，经拉丁语 scopus 与意大利语 scopo 进入英语，核心是“目光对准并被框住的那一片”。

sensesIntro.en: One image runs through all nine senses: a mark held in view, and the bounded field around it. Breadth of a subject, room to act, reach of a law, a person's duties, the range of vision, a viewing instrument, a name's region in code, a project's agreed boundary, and the act of looking something over are nine ways of drawing that same circle.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项共用一幅画面：一个被目光锁定的标记，以及它周围那块有边界的场地。主题广度、行动余地、法律效力、个人职责、视野所及、观察仪器、代码中名字的可见区域、项目约定的边界，以及亲自察看，都是同一个圆圈的九种画法。

core.en: A target held in view: the bounded field that a gaze, a rule or a plan can cover.
core.cn: 一个被目光锁定的靶标：目光、规则或计划所能覆盖的那块有边界的场地。

branches.en: COVERAGE: what a subject, a rule or a job includes. The circle is drawn from the outside.
branches.cn: 覆盖：一个主题、一条规则或一份职责包含什么。圆圈从外面画定。

branches.en: ROOM TO ACT: the unfilled part of the circle, which is what opportunity feels like.
branches.cn: 行动余地：圆圈里尚未填满的部分，也就是“机会”的感觉。

branches.en: SEEING: the literal field of vision and the instruments that extend it.
branches.cn: 看见：字面上的视场，以及延伸视场的仪器。

branches.en: TECHNICAL BOUNDARY: the region where a name works, and the work a project promises to do.
branches.cn: 技术边界：名字生效的区域，以及项目承诺完成的工作。

branches.en: EXAMINING: the verb returns to plain looking, the root act behind all the nouns.
branches.cn: 察看：动词回到最朴素的“看”，也就是所有名词义背后的词根动作。

intro.en: Scope is a free root in English and also the second element of many instruments. The items below separate the Greek root, the combining suffix and the ordinary English endings.
intro.cn: scope 在英语中既是自由词根，也是许多仪器名的第二成分。下列条目把希腊词根、组合后缀和普通英语词尾分开。

latinIntro.en: Latin took the Greek root as scopus. The Latin forms matter because Italian and then English passed through them.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语把希腊词根借作 scopus。这些拉丁形式很关键，因为意大利语和英语都经由它们传来。

items.meaning: field of view; range; room to act
items.example: The scope of the study was narrow.
items.exampleCN: 这项研究的范围很窄。

items.meaning: an instrument for viewing very small things
items.meaningCN: 显微镜（观看微小之物的仪器）
items.example: The cells were visible under the microscope.
items.exampleCN: 这些细胞在显微镜下可见。

items.meaning: an instrument for viewing distant objects
items.meaningCN: 望远镜（观看远处之物的仪器）
items.example: They pointed the telescope at the moon.
items.exampleCN: 他们把望远镜对准月亮。

items.meaning: an instrument for viewing around or over an obstacle
items.meaningCN: 潜望镜（绕过障碍观察的仪器）
items.example: The submarine raised its periscope.
items.exampleCN: 潜艇升起了潜望镜。

items.meaning: an instrument for viewing the inside of a body
items.meaningCN: 内窥镜（观察体内情况的仪器）
items.example: The doctor used an endoscope to inspect the stomach.
items.exampleCN: 医生用内窥镜检查胃部。

items.meaning: a chart of the sky at a particular hour, used in astrology
items.meaningCN: 星象图；占星用的出生时刻天宫图
items.example: She read her horoscope in the morning paper.
items.exampleCN: 她在晨报上读了自己的星座运势。

items.meaning: an instrument for viewing or detecting
items.meaningCN: 表示“观看或探测仪器”的后缀
items.example: Stethoscope, oscilloscope and kaleidoscope all end in -scope.
items.exampleCN: 听诊器、示波器和万花筒都以 -scope 结尾。

items.meaning: relating to viewing or to a scope
items.meaningCN: 与观察或某种镜相关的
items.example: The scopic image was blurry at the edges.
items.exampleCN: 镜下的图像边缘模糊。

items.meaning: examined; also fitted with a scope
items.meaningCN: 已察看过；也指装有瞄准镜的
items.example: They scoped the hall before booking it.
items.exampleCN: 订场地前他们先去看过。

items.meaning: the act of defining or surveying a range
items.meaningCN: 界定或勘察范围的行为
items.example: Scoping the project took two full days.
items.exampleCN: 界定项目范围花了整整两天。

Greek verb, same family as skopos

definition_zh: 部分；章节；部门；截面；阶层；地块；声部；切开；条款
definition_en: a part cut or divided off from a whole, whether of a text, an organization, a surface or a document
core_image: 一把刀把一个整体切开，切下来的那一块就是 section
scene: 图书馆里，管理员把一本厚杂志拆开，指着目录说：Read the first section, then answer the questions.
sceneCN: 这里 section 是「书刊的章节」（第 2 个义项：文本被切分出的部分）；句意：先读第一节，然后回答问题。图中可辨识物件：杂志、目录页、书签、管理员。

pos.zh: 部分；章节；部门；截面；阶层；地块
把……切开；将……分段

collocations.zh: 逐节地；一部分一部分地

derivatives.zh: 分段的；局部的；由可拼合部分组成的

senses.title: A part cut off from a whole
senses.definition: one of the parts into which something is divided, especially a distinct and separable part
senses.definitionCN: 某物被分成的部分之一，尤指清晰可分开的部分
senses.example: Divide the cake into eight equal sections.
senses.exampleCN: 把蛋糕分成八等份。
senses.why: Latin secare means 'to cut'. Sectio is 'a cutting', and the section is literally the piece that the knife has separated from the rest.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 secare 意为“切”。sectio 是“一次切割”，而 section 字面上就是刀从整体上分开的那一块。

senses.title: A division of a text
senses.definition: a distinct part of a book, newspaper, report or piece of writing
senses.definitionCN: 书、报纸、报告或文章中清晰独立的一部分
senses.example: The report has three sections: background, findings and recommendations.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告分三节：背景、发现与建议。
senses.why: A book is a long whole that readers need cut into manageable pieces. Each chapter or section is a cut that lets the reader rest and resume.
senses.whyCN: 一本书是需要被切成可处理小块的漫长整体。每一章、每一节都是一刀，让读者能停下来再继续。

senses.title: A unit inside an organization
senses.definition: a separate department or unit within a larger organization
senses.definitionCN: 较大组织内部独立的部门或单位
senses.example: She works in the section that handles foreign orders.
senses.exampleCN: 她在负责海外订单的那个部门工作。
senses.why: An organization divides its work the way a body divides its labour. Each section is a piece cut out and given its own task.
senses.whyCN: 组织分派工作的方式，就像身体分工一样。每个 section 都是被切出来、赋予独立任务的一块。

senses.title: A surface exposed by cutting
senses.definition: the surface that appears when a solid is cut through, or a diagram showing that surface
senses.definitionCN: 固体被切开后出现的面，或表示该面的图
senses.example: The diagram shows a cross-section of the human heart.
senses.exampleCN: 这幅图展示了人类心脏的横截面。
senses.why: Cut a solid and the cut itself becomes visible. What was hidden inside is now a flat section, which is why anatomy and engineering use the word for slices.
senses.whyCN: 把固体切开，切口本身就变得可见。原本藏在内部的东西成了平面上的 section，故解剖学与工程学都用这个词表示切片。

senses.title: A slice of the population
senses.definition: a group of people seen as one distinct part of a larger society or population
senses.definitionCN: 被视为较大社会或人口中独特一部分的一群人
senses.example: The survey reached every section of society.
senses.exampleCN: 这项调查触及了社会的各个阶层。
senses.why: Society is treated as a whole that can be cut vertically. Each class or group is a slice, and a cross-section is a sample that cuts across all slices.
senses.whyCN: 社会被当作一个可以纵向切开的整体。每个阶层或群体都是一片，而 cross-section 则是横切所有层次的样本。

senses.title: A measured piece of land
senses.definition: in land surveying, a fixed unit of area, especially one square mile in the US system
senses.definitionCN: 土地测量中的固定面积单位，尤指美国制中的一平方英里
senses.example: The farm covers four sections of prairie.
senses.exampleCN: 这个农场占地四块草原地段。
senses.why: Settlers cut the open land into numbered squares. A section is a piece marked off by survey lines, a cut made on the map rather than in the soil.
senses.whyCN: 拓荒者把开阔土地切成编号方块。section 是被测量线划出的一块，是在地图上而非土壤上做的切割。

senses.title: A group of instruments
senses.definition: a group of instruments or players within an orchestra or band, such as the string section
senses.definitionCN: 管弦乐团或乐队中的一组乐器或演奏者，如弦乐组
senses.example: The brass section entered a bar early.
senses.exampleCN: 铜管组早了一小节进入。
senses.why: An orchestra is divided by families of sound. Each section is cut off from the rest by timbre and given its own line in the score.
senses.whyCN: 管弦乐团按音色家族划分。每个 section 因音色而从其余部分切出，并在总谱中拥有自己的声部线。

senses.title: To cut into pieces: the verb
senses.definition: to cut something into sections, especially in biology or medicine
senses.definitionCN: 把某物切成段或片，尤用于生物学或医学
senses.example: The tissue was sectioned and stained for the microscope.
senses.exampleCN: 组织被切片并染色以便显微镜观察。
senses.why: The verb is the root action itself: to section is to perform secare, to make the cuts that produce sections.
senses.whyCN: 动词就是词根动作本身：to section 就是执行 secare，做出产生各个 section 的那些切割。

senses.title: A numbered division of a legal text
senses.definition: a numbered subdivision of a statute, contract or legal code
senses.definitionCN: 法规、合同或法典中编号的细分条文
senses.example: Under section 12, the tenant must give written notice.
senses.exampleCN: 根据第 12 条，承租人必须发出书面通知。
senses.why: Law cuts its text into numbered pieces so that each rule can be cited alone. A section is the smallest citable cut.
senses.whyCN: 法律把文本切成编号的小块，好让每条规则都能单独引用。section 就是可引用的最小切割单位。

intro.en: Section is a straight Latin word: sectio 'a cutting', from secare 'to cut'. Every sense, from a book chapter to a land parcel, is a piece produced by some kind of cut.
intro.cn: section 是一个直系的拉丁词：sectio“切割”，来自 secare“切”。从书的章节到地块，每个义项都是某种切割产生的一块。

items.en: Secare meant 'to cut, cut off, divide'. It is one of the basic Latin verbs of separation and is unrelated to sequi 'to follow'.
items.cn: secare 意为“切、切下、分割”。它是拉丁语中最基本的“分离”动词之一，与 sequi“跟随”无关。

items.en: Sectio (genitive sectionis) meant 'a cutting, a cut, a division'. It named both the act of cutting and the part produced.
items.cn: sectio（属格 sectionis）意为“切割、切口、划分”。它同时指切割的动作与切出来的部分。

items.en: A different derivative, sector, meant 'a cutter', from the same secare. It later became the geometric and business 'sector' - same knife, different ending.
items.cn: 同一词根的另一个派生词 sector 意为“切割者”。它后来变成几何与商业上的“扇形、部门”——同一把刀，不同词尾。

items.en: English took section from Old French section in the early 15th century, first in the general sense of a division or a portion cut off.
items.cn: 英语于 15 世纪早期从古法语 section 借入，最初是“分割”或“切下的一部分”的一般义。

items.en: The sense 'part of a book or writing' is recorded from the 1530s. The anatomical sense 'slice of a solid body' follows in the 1570s as dissection became a science.
items.cn: “书或文章的一部分”这一义项于 16 世纪 30 年代有记录。随着解剖成为一门科学，解剖学上“固体切片”的义项在 16 世纪 70 年代跟进。

items.en: The organizational sense develops in the 19th century, and the land-survey sense comes from the US grid system. The verb 'to cut into sections' is a 19th-century back-formation from the noun.
items.cn: 组织“部门”义在 19 世纪发展出来，土地测量义来自美国的方格测量制。动词“切成段”是 19 世纪由名词逆构而成。

note.en: The look-alike group is dangerous because sect, section and sector all descend from secare but mean different things. The near-meaning group compares words for parts.
note.cn: 形近组需要警惕：sect、section、sector 都出自 secare，但意思不同。近义组比较各种表示“部分”的词。

entries.definition: a period of activity or a formal meeting. It comes from sedere 'to sit', not from secare 'to cut'.
entries.definitionCN: 一段活动时间；正式会议。它出自 sedere“坐”，不是 secare“切”。

entries.definition: a part of a circle between two radii, or a distinct branch of an economy. It comes from secare through sector 'cutter', and is not interchangeable with section.
entries.definitionCN: 两条半径之间的扇形；经济中的一个部门。它经 sector“切割者”出自 secare，不能与 section 互换。

entries.definition: a small religious group that has separated from a larger one. It is the bare Latin stem, literally 'a cut-off group'.
entries.definitionCN: 从更大团体中分离出来的小宗教派别。它是光秃秃的拉丁词干，字面就是“被切出去的一群”。

entries.definition: a piece of a whole. It is the broadest word and carries no image of cutting.
entries.definitionCN: 整体中的一部分。它是最宽泛的词，不带“切”的意象。

entries.definition: the act of separating something into parts, or one of the parts so made. It stresses the separating process more than section does.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物分成部分的行为，或分出的部分之一。它比 section 更强调分离的过程。

entries.definition: one of several pieces into which a line or a whole is naturally divided. It usually suggests pieces in a row.
entries.definitionCN: 线或整体自然分成的若干段之一。它通常暗示一段接一段排列。

entries.definition: a main division of a book. It is narrower than section and used mainly for books, not for reports or newspapers.
entries.definitionCN: 书的主要划分单位。它比 section 窄，主要用于书籍，不用于报告或报纸。

normalIntro.en: Concrete pictures for a word about cutting: a knife, a cake, a book, a microscope slide, a survey map.
normalIntro.cn: 用具体画面记一个关于“切”的词：刀、蛋糕、书、显微镜切片、测量地图。

normal.en: Cut a cake into eight pieces: each piece is a section, and secare is the knife.
normal.cn: 把蛋糕切成八块：每块都是一个 section，而 secare 就是那把刀。

normal.en: A book is cut into sections so the reader can stop at a clean edge.
normal.cn: 书被切成一个个 section，好让读者在干净的边缘处停下。

normal.en: A cross-section is what you see after slicing a solid: the hidden inside becomes a flat picture.
normal.cn: cross-section 是切开固体后看到的东西：藏着的内部变成了平面图。

normal.en: A company is a body with sections, each doing one job, like organs in an anatomy diagram.
normal.cn: 公司像一个被分成多个 section 的身体，每块各司其职，如同解剖图上的器官。

normal.en: A legal section is a numbered cut in a statute: cite the cut, not the whole animal.
normal.cn: 法律条款是法条上一道编号的切口：引用那道切口，而不是整只动物。

abstract.en: One schema: CUT → PIECE → PART OF TEXT → UNIT OF ORGANIZATION → SLICE OF SOCIETY.
abstract.cn: 一个图式：切 → 一块 → 文本的一部分 → 组织单位 → 社会的一层。

abstract.en: Root check: section, sector, sect, dissect, insect all share secare 'cut'. Session does not; it sits.
abstract.cn: 词根检查：section、sector、sect、dissect、insect 都共享 secare“切”。session 不属于此列，它是“坐”。

abstract.en: Contrast: a section is what is cut off; a session is a sitting; a sector is a cutter turned into a slice of a circle.
abstract.cn: 对照：section 是被切下来的东西；session 是一次“坐”；sector 是“切割者”转成的圆的一片。

examples.en: Each section of the bridge was built on land and then lifted into place.
examples.cn: 桥的每一段都先在陆上建造，再吊装到位。

examples.en: The newspaper's science section appears on Tuesdays.
examples.cn: 报纸的科学版在周二出版。

examples.en: Please read the safety section before operating the machine.
examples.cn: 操作机器前请先阅读安全条款部分。

dict_mnemonic.text: “塞克神”——塞（进）克（服）神（秘）的一刀，切开后每一块 → section 部分、章节

root: 源自拉丁语 secare“切”，经 sectio“切割”进入英语；核心是“被刀切开的一块”。同根的 sector、sect、dissect、insect 都共享这把刀，而 session 不属于此列。

sensesIntro.en: Section is a cut made visible. Cut a cake and you get a piece; cut a book and you get a chapter; cut an organization and you get a department; cut a solid and you get a cross-section; cut a population and you get a class. The verb simply performs the cut.
sensesIntro.cn: section 是一道看得见的切口。切开蛋糕得到一块，切开书得到一章，切开组织得到部门，切开固体得到截面，切开人群得到阶层。动词则是在执行这道切割。

core.en: A piece separated from a whole by a cut, real or imagined.
core.cn: 被真实或想象中的一刀从整体分开的一块。

chain: SLICE OF A SURFACE OR POPULATION

branches.en: PART OF A WHOLE: the plain piece, the chapter, and the citable legal clause.
branches.cn: 整体的一部分：最普通的一块、书的一章、可引用的法律条款。

branches.en: HUMAN DIVISIONS: a department cut out of an organization, a class cut out of society.
branches.cn: 人的划分：从组织切出的部门，从社会切出的阶层。

branches.en: THE CUT ITSELF: the exposed surface of a sliced solid, and the verb that makes the slice.
branches.cn: 切口本身：被切开固体的暴露面，以及做出切片的动词。

branches.en: LAND: a parcel marked off by survey lines, a cut drawn on a map.
branches.cn: 土地：被测量线划出的一块，是画在地图上的切口。

branches.en: SOUND: an orchestral family cut off from the rest by its timbre.
branches.cn: 声音：因音色而从其余部分切出的乐团声部。

intro.en: The sec- family is large and easy to confuse. The items below keep the 'cut' idea visible in each word.
intro.cn: sec- 词族庞大且易混。下列条目让每个词里的“切”义保持可见。

latinIntro.en: Latin has three useful forms: the verb secare, the noun sectio, and the participle sectus 'cut'. English builds on all three.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语有三个有用形式：动词 secare、名词 sectio、分词 sectus“被切的”。英语三者都用。

items.meaning: a cutting; a part cut off
items.example: The first section of the book is short.
items.exampleCN: 这本书的第一节很短。

items.example: Students dissect a frog in biology class.
items.exampleCN: 学生在生物课上解剖青蛙。

items.meaningCN: 昆虫（字面“被切成段的身体”）
items.example: An insect has three body parts.
items.exampleCN: 昆虫的身体分三部分。

items.meaning: a cutter; then a slice of a circle or economy
items.meaningCN: 切割者；后指扇形、经济部门
items.example: The service sector employs most of the city.
items.exampleCN: 服务业雇用了这座城市的大部分人。

items.meaning: a smaller division inside a section
items.example: See subsection 4.2 for the details.
items.exampleCN: 细节见 4.2 小节。

items.meaning: a slice across a solid; a representative sample
items.example: The cross-section shows layers of rock.
items.exampleCN: 横截面显示出岩层。

items.meaning: relating to a section; made of sections
items.meaningCN: 分段的；局部的；拼合式的
items.example: They bought a sectional sofa.
items.exampleCN: 他们买了一张组合沙发。

items.meaning: strong loyalty to one's own region or group
items.example: Sectionalism divided the country before the war.
items.exampleCN: 战前地方主义分裂了这个国家。

items.meaning: a group cut off from a larger body
items.meaningCN: 从大团体中切出的派别
items.example: The sect broke away in the 16th century.
items.exampleCN: 该派别在 16 世纪分离出去。

items.meaning: the process of cutting into slices
items.example: Sectioning the tissue took an hour.
items.exampleCN: 组织切片花了一小时。

definition_zh: 部门；行业；扇形；区域；防区；扇区
definition_en: a distinct part cut out of a larger whole, especially a branch of an economy or a pie-shaped piece of a circle
core_image: 一个圆被两条半径切成一片，那一片就是 sector
scene: 经济学课堂上，老师在圆饼图上把服务业涂成一大片。The service sector takes about sixty per cent of the chart, and the teacher said that this was the largest piece of the economy.
sceneCN: 这里 sector 是「经济中的一个部门」（第 1 个义项：经济被分成的不同部分之一）；句意：服务业部门占了图表约六成，老师说这是经济里最大的一块。图中可辨识物件：圆饼图、彩色扇形、百分比标签。

pos.zh: 部门；行业；扇形；区域；扇区
把……分成扇形／区域

senses.title: A branch of an economy
senses.definition: one of the distinct parts into which an economy is divided, such as agriculture, manufacturing or services
senses.definitionCN: 经济被分成的不同部分之一，如农业、制造业或服务业
senses.example: Tourism is the island's largest sector.
senses.exampleCN: 旅游业是该岛最大的产业部门。
senses.why: The image is a pie cut into slices. Each industry is one slice of the whole economy, and the word for a slice is sector.
senses.whyCN: 画面是一个被切成片的饼。每个行业都是整体经济中的一片，而表示“一片”的词就是 sector。

senses.title: A pie-shaped part of a circle
senses.definition: in geometry, the region enclosed by two radii of a circle and the arc between them
senses.definitionCN: 几何中，由圆的两条半径及它们之间的弧围成的区域
senses.example: The area of a sector equals half the radius times the arc length.
senses.exampleCN: 扇形的面积等于半径乘以弧长的一半。
senses.why: This is the oldest surviving sense. Late Latin sector translated Greek tomeus 'a cutter' for exactly this shape, because the slice looks as if a knife had cut it from the circle.
senses.whyCN: 这是现存最古老的义项。晚期拉丁语 sector 用“切割者”来翻译希腊语 tomeus，正因为这一片看起来像被刀从圆上切下来的。

senses.title: Public or private ownership
senses.definition: the part of a country's economy owned or controlled by the state, or by private individuals and companies
senses.definitionCN: 一国经济中由国家控制的部分，或由私人与公司控制的部分
senses.example: Half the workforce is employed in the public sector.
senses.exampleCN: 一半的劳动力受雇于公共部门。
senses.why: Ownership cuts the economy along a different line. Instead of agriculture versus industry, the slice is now defined by who holds it: the state or private owners.
senses.whyCN: 所有制沿另一条线把经济切开。此时的切片不再按农业与工业划分，而按“谁持有”来定：国家还是私人。

senses.title: A piece of a military front
senses.definition: a defined part of a battle front or area of operations assigned to a particular unit
senses.definitionCN: 分配给某一部队的防线或作战区域中的特定一段
senses.example: The battalion was ordered to hold its sector until dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 该营奉命坚守其防区直到天亮。
senses.why: A headquarters sits at the centre and draws a circle around itself; the front is then cut into sectors like slices of that circle. This WWI image gave the modern 'area' sense.
senses.whyCN: 指挥部位于中心并向四周画一个圆；防线于是像圆的切片一样被分成若干 sector。这个一战时期的意象催生了现代的“区域”义。

senses.title: A defined area of a place
senses.definition: a distinct area of a city, region or other space, often defined for administration or operations
senses.definitionCN: 城市、地区或其他空间中被划出的独立区域，常为管理或行动而设
senses.example: Aid was delivered to the worst-hit sectors of the city.
senses.exampleCN: 救援物资被送到该市受灾最重的几个区域。
senses.why: Once a front could be sliced, any space could be. The word generalized from military maps to maps of cities and disaster zones.
senses.whyCN: 既然防线可以被切片，任何空间都可以。这个词从军事地图推广到了城市与灾区地图。

senses.title: A slice of a disk: computing
senses.definition: one of the wedge-shaped divisions of a track on a magnetic disk or other storage medium
senses.definitionCN: 磁盘或其他存储介质上一条磁道中被划分出的楔形区域之一
senses.example: The file was written to a damaged sector of the disk.
senses.exampleCN: 该文件被写入了磁盘上一个损坏的扇区。
senses.why: A disk is literally a circle, and storage is laid out in wedges. Computing kept the geometric meaning whole: a sector of a platter is a sector of a circle.
senses.whyCN: 磁盘本身就是个圆，存储按楔形排布。计算机领域完整保留了几何义：盘片上的一块就是圆的一个扇形。

senses.title: A sphere of activity
senses.definition: a distinct area of social or economic activity, such as the voluntary sector or the informal sector
senses.definitionCN: 社会或经济活动中一个独立的领域，如志愿部门或非正规部门
senses.example: Charities form a large part of the voluntary sector.
senses.exampleCN: 慈善机构构成志愿部门的很大一部分。
senses.why: The pie is no longer the whole economy but the whole of social activity, cut by function. Each kind of work becomes a slice with its own rules.
senses.whyCN: 此时的饼不再是整个经济，而是整个社会活动，并按功能切开。每类工作成为一片，各有自己的规则。

senses.title: A cutter: the old literal sense
senses.definition: in classical Latin, a cutter or one who cuts; now surviving only in etymology and in historical writing
senses.definitionCN: 古典拉丁语中指切割者或从事切割的人；今仅存于词源说明与历史文本
senses.example: The Latin noun sector once meant simply 'a cutter'.
senses.exampleCN: 拉丁名词 sector 曾经只表示“切割者”。
senses.why: Sector is an agent noun from secare, so its oldest meaning is a person or tool that cuts. The shape sense came later, when the cutter's product was named after the cutter.
senses.whyCN: sector 是 secare 的施事名词，最古老的含义是“切割的人或工具”。形状义后来才出现，即用切割者来命名其产物。

senses.title: To divide into sectors
senses.definition: to divide an area, disk or field into sectors
senses.definitionCN: 把一片区域、磁盘或场地划分为若干扇形区
senses.example: The map was sectored into six patrol zones.
senses.exampleCN: 地图被划分为六个巡逻区。
senses.why: The verb simply applies the noun's cut: to sector a space is to draw the radii and make the slices explicit.
senses.whyCN: 动词只是执行名词的那一刀：sector 一个空间，就是画出半径，让各个切片显形。

intro.en: Sector is Latin for 'cutter', but English borrowed it first as a geometry term for the slice of a circle that a cutter would make. Economy, military and computing senses all radiate from that pie-shaped slice.
intro.cn: sector 在拉丁语里是“切割者”，但英语首先借它作几何术语，指切割者从圆上切下的那一片。经济、军事与计算机义都从这片扇形辐射出来。

items.en: Secare 'to cut' goes back to PIE *sek- 'to cut', the root behind section, sect, dissect, insect and segment. The 'cut' image is the deepest layer of sector.
items.cn: secare“切”追溯到原始印欧语 *sek-“切”，也是 section、sect、dissect、insect、segment 的词根。“切”的意象是 sector 最深的一层。

items.en: Classical Latin sector meant 'a cutter, one who cuts', an agent noun from sectus, the past participle of secare. Late Latin also used it to translate Greek tomeus 'cutter' for a section of a circle.
items.cn: 古典拉丁语 sector 意为“切割者、切割的人”，是 secare 的分词 sectus 构成的施事名词。晚期拉丁语也用它翻译希腊语 tomeus“切割者”，指圆的一段。

items.en: English adopted sector in the 1560s specifically as the geometry term: the region between two radii and their arc. It came through Late Latin sector 'section of a circle', which had translated Archimedes' Greek.
items.cn: 英语在 16 世纪 60 年代借入 sector，专门作几何术语：两条半径与它们所夹弧之间的区域。它经由晚期拉丁语 sector“圆的一段”传来，后者曾用于翻译阿基米德的希腊文。

items.en: By 1715 sector was applied to any figure shaped like that slice, not only a true circle sector. The shape, rather than the geometry, now defined the word.
items.cn: 到 1715 年，sector 已用于任何形状像这种切片的图形，不再限于真正的圆扇形。定义这个词的变成了形状，而不是几何条件。

items.en: A WWI sense 'part of a front' (1916), imagined as a circle centred on headquarters, generalized by 1920 to 'area, division'. The economic sense 'branch of an economy' is recorded by 1937.
items.cn: 一战时期出现“防线的一段”义（1916），其意象是以指挥部为圆心的圆；到 1920 年泛化为“区域、分区”。经济义“经济中的一个部门”于 1937 年有记录。

items.en: The verb 'divide into sectors' dates from 1884. Disk sectors in computing and 'public/private sector' in politics are 20th-century developments of the same slice.
items.cn: 动词“划分为扇形区”始于 1884 年。计算机中的磁盘扇区与政治中的“公私部门”都是同一片扇形在 20 世纪的延伸。

note.en: Section, sect and sector all come from secare, so the look-alike group must be read carefully. The near-meaning group compares other words for a part.
note.cn: section、sect、sector 都出自 secare，形近组必须仔细区分。近义组比较其他表示“部分”的词。

entries.definition: a part cut off from a whole, such as a chapter, a department or a cross-section. It names the piece, not a branch of the economy.
entries.definitionCN: 从整体切下的一部分，如章节、部门或截面。它指切下的那块，不指经济分支。

entries.definition: a small religious group separated from a larger one. It is the bare Latin stem, not the agent noun.
entries.definitionCN: 从更大团体分离出的小宗教派别。它是光秃秃的拉丁词干，不是施事名词。

entries.definition: the adjective from sector, meaning 'relating to a sector or sectors'. It is not a noun and cannot replace sector.
entries.definitionCN: sector 派生的形容词，意为“与部门或扇形相关的”。它不是名词，不能替代 sector。

entries.definition: one of the parts into which something is naturally divided, especially a line or a fruit. It is more concrete than sector.
entries.definitionCN: 某物自然分成的部分之一，尤指线段或果实。它比 sector 更具体。

entries.definition: a part of a larger organization or whole. It is broader and does not carry a pie-shaped image.
entries.definitionCN: 较大组织或整体中的一部分。它更宽泛，不带扇形意象。

entries.definition: a local office of a company, or a division of a subject. It suggests something growing out from a trunk rather than a slice.
entries.definitionCN: 公司的分支机构，或学科的分支。它暗示从主干生长出来，而不是从圆上切下。

entries.definition: an area with a particular purpose or character. It overlaps with sector in the military and city senses but has no root image of cutting.
entries.definitionCN: 有特定用途或特征的区域。它在军事与城市义上与 sector 重叠，但没有“切”的词根意象。

normalIntro.en: Pictures for sector: a pie, a tank front, a gramophone record, a city map. Each picture holds one group of senses.
normalIntro.cn: sector 的画面：饼图、坦克防线、黑胶唱片、城市地图。每幅画托住一组义项。

normal.en: Draw a pie and cut it into slices: each industry is one sector of the economy.
normal.cn: 画一个饼并切成片：每个行业都是经济的一个 sector。

normal.en: A sector of a circle is exactly a pie slice made with a compass.
normal.cn: 圆的一个 sector 就是用圆规画出的饼图切片。

normal.en: A WWI headquarters sits at the centre and assigns each unit a slice of the front: its sector.
normal.cn: 一战指挥部坐在圆心，给每个部队分一片防线：这就是它的 sector。

normal.en: A hard disk is a stack of circles; data is stored in wedges called sectors.
normal.cn: 硬盘是一叠圆盘；数据存在称为 sector 的楔形块里。

normal.en: The old Latin sector was the cutter himself; only later did the slice take his name.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 sector 本指切割者本人；后来那片切片才借用了他的名字。

abstract.en: One schema: CUT → CUTTER → PIE SLICE → SHARE OF A WHOLE. Every sense stops at one of these four.
abstract.cn: 一个图式：切 → 切割者 → 扇形片 → 整体中的一份。每个义项都停在这四站之一。

abstract.en: Root check: sector, section, sect share secare 'cut'. Do not confuse them with sequence, which follows sequi.
abstract.cn: 词根检查：sector、section、sect 共享 secare“切”。不要与 sequence 混，后者跟随 sequi。

abstract.en: Contrast triple: section = the cut piece; sector = the slice with a shape; sect = the group cut away.
abstract.cn: 三词对照：section 是切下的块；sector 是有形状的扇形；sect 是被切出去的一群人。

examples.en: The government plans to open the energy sector to private investment.
examples.cn: 政府计划向私人投资开放能源部门。

examples.en: Each sector of the circle was coloured differently in the chart.
examples.cn: 图表中圆的每个扇形都被涂成不同颜色。

examples.en: The rescue team searched sector by sector through the rubble.
examples.cn: 救援队一片一片地搜遍了废墟。

dict_mnemonic.text: “赛克特”——赛（过）克（服）特（别）大的一片，像切开的饼 → sector 部门、扇形

root: 源自拉丁语 secare“切”；sector 本是“切割者”，晚期拉丁语用它指“圆被切下的一片”，英语 1560 年代借入作几何扇形，后扩展为经济部门、区域与磁盘扇区。

sensesIntro.en: Sector is one slice of a larger whole. The oldest slice is geometric: two radii cut a pie from a circle. From that shape come the economic sector (a slice of the economy), the public/private sector (a slice by ownership), the military sector (a slice of a front), the city sector (a slice of space), the disk sector (a wedge of a platter) and the sphere of activity. The old literal 'cutter' survives only as etymology, and the verb draws the slices.
sensesIntro.cn: sector 是更大整体中的一片。最古老的一片是几何的：两条半径从圆上切下一块饼。经济部门（经济的一片）、公私部门（按所有权切的一片）、军事防区（防线的一片）、城市区域（空间的一片）、磁盘扇区（盘片上的一块）以及活动领域，都从这一形状而来。古老的实义“切割者”只留在词源里，而动词则是在画这些切片。

core.en: One slice cut from a round whole, later any distinct slice of an economy, a front or a space.
core.cn: 从圆形整体上切下的一片，后来指经济、防线或空间中任何独立的一片。

branches.en: GEOMETRIC SLICES: a sector of a circle, and a wedge-shaped sector of a disk.
branches.cn: 几何切片：圆的一个扇形，以及磁盘上的楔形扇区。

branches.en: ECONOMIC AND SOCIAL SPHERES: industry branches, ownership halves, and fields of activity.
branches.cn: 经济与社会领域：产业分支、按所有制切的两半、活动领域。

branches.en: TERRITORY: a slice of a battle front, and a defined area of a city or region.
branches.cn: 地域：防线的一段，以及城市或地区中被划定的区域。

branches.en: THE CUTTER: the classical Latin sense, now only etymological.
branches.cn: 切割者：古典拉丁语义，今仅存于词源。

branches.en: THE ACT OF DIVIDING: the verb that turns a space into sectors.
branches.cn: 划分动作：把空间切成扇区的动词。

intro.en: Sector sits inside the large sec- 'cut' family. The items below show which ending produces which kind of word.
intro.cn: sector 属于庞大的 sec-“切”词族。下列条目展示不同词尾造出哪类词。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies secare 'cut', sector 'cutter', sectio 'a cutting' and sectus 'cut'. English uses all four.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供 secare“切”、sector“切割者”、sectio“切割”、sectus“被切的”。英语四者都用。

items.meaning: cutter; later a slice of a circle or economy
items.meaningCN: 切割者；后指圆或经济的一片
items.example: The service sector grew fastest.
items.exampleCN: 服务业部门增长最快。

items.meaning: a cutting; a part cut off
items.example: Read the next section carefully.
items.exampleCN: 仔细阅读下一节。

items.meaning: a group cut off from a larger body
items.meaningCN: 从大团体中切出的派别
items.example: The sect separated from the main church.
items.exampleCN: 该派别从主教会分离出去。

items.meaning: to cut into two equal parts
items.example: The line bisects the angle.
items.exampleCN: 这条线平分该角。

items.example: They trisected the field for three crops.
items.exampleCN: 他们把田分成三块种三种作物。

items.example: The class dissected an owl pellet.
items.exampleCN: 全班解剖了一个猫头鹰食团。

items.example: The two roads intersect near the bridge.
items.exampleCN: 两条路在桥附近相交。

items.example: Sectoral policies differ by industry.
items.exampleCN: 各部门政策因行业而异。

items.meaning: of or like a sector; adapted for cutting
items.example: The insect has sectorial mouthparts.
items.exampleCN: 这种昆虫有适于切割的口器。

items.meaning: the act of dividing into sectors
items.example: Sectoring the disk took several minutes.
items.exampleCN: 给磁盘划分扇区花了几分钟。

latinEntries.meaning: a cutter; a section of a circle

definition_zh: 安全的；牢固的；确定的；安心的；获得；使安全；系牢；保障
definition_en: free from danger or care, firmly fixed, certain, or to make something safe and certain to keep
core_image: 一扇上好锁的门：里面的人不必再操心，外面的人进不来
scene: 银行金库里，职员把门关上、转动锁轮，红灯变绿。屏幕上显示：The vault is now secure.
sceneCN: 这里 secure 是「安全、受保护」（第 1、4 个义项：免于危险与免于未授权进入）；句意：金库现在安全了。图中可辨识物件：金库门、锁轮、指示灯、监控屏。

pos.zh: 安全的；牢固的；确定的；无忧的
使安全；系牢；获得；保障

forms.label: 比较级（更多用 more 构成）
最高级（更多用 most 构成）

derivatives.zh: 不安全的；缺乏安全感的
证券化（把资产打包成可交易证券）

senses.title: Safe from danger or harm
senses.definition: protected from danger, attack, loss or harm
senses.definitionCN: 受到保护，不会遭遇危险、攻击、损失或伤害
senses.example: Keep your passport in a secure place.
senses.exampleCN: 把护照放在安全的地方。
senses.why: Latin securus is se- 'free from' + cura 'care'. A secure place is one you need not worry about, because nothing there can be lost or attacked.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 securus 由 se-“免于”加 cura“忧虑”构成。安全的地方就是一个不必为它操心的地方，因为那里没有什么会丢失或受攻击。

senses.title: Firmly fixed in place
senses.definition: firmly attached, fastened or held so that it cannot move or come loose
senses.definitionCN: 牢牢附着、系住或固定，不会移动或松脱
senses.example: Make sure the ladder is secure before you climb.
senses.exampleCN: 爬梯子前先确认它牢靠。
senses.why: Something firmly fixed gives no grounds for care either: it will not slip, so it cannot surprise you. The 1841 mechanical sense grew out of 'affording confidence'.
senses.whyCN: 牢固固定的东西同样让人不必操心：它不会滑脱，也就不会给你意外。1841 年的机械义正是由“令人放心”发展而来。

senses.title: Free from care: confident and untroubled
senses.definition: feeling safe and free from anxiety; confident about the future
senses.definitionCN: 感到安全、没有焦虑；对未来有信心
senses.example: She felt secure in the knowledge that her family was safe.
senses.exampleCN: 知道家人平安，她感到安心。
senses.why: This is the original 1530s sense: 'without care or fear'. The modern word has moved toward 'protected', but the inner state of not worrying is still visible.
senses.whyCN: 这是 16 世纪 30 年代的原义：“无忧、无惧”。现代词义已偏向“受保护”，但“内心不担忧”的状态仍然可见。

senses.title: Protected from unauthorised access
senses.definition: protected against being entered, intercepted, copied or used by someone without permission
senses.definitionCN: 受到保护，未经许可者无法进入、截取、复制或使用
senses.example: Use a secure connection when you send the file.
senses.exampleCN: 发送文件时请使用安全连接。
senses.why: A locked door keeps out the wrong person as well as the wrong danger. Digital security extends 'free from care' to data that others might take.
senses.whyCN: 上锁的门既挡住危险，也挡住不该进来的人。数字安全把“免于忧虑”扩展到可能被他人拿走的数据。

senses.title: Financially safe
senses.definition: having enough money or income to live without fear of loss or hardship
senses.definitionCN: 拥有足够的钱或收入，不必担心损失或困窘
senses.example: A steady salary made him feel financially secure.
senses.exampleCN: 稳定的薪水让他有了经济安全感。
senses.why: Money is the modern form of care. If income cannot vanish, the mind is free from its most common worry, so 'secure' applies to finances almost naturally.
senses.whyCN: 金钱是现代形式的“忧”。如果收入不会凭空消失，心就从最普遍的忧虑中解放出来，所以 secure 几乎自然地用于财务。

senses.title: To make something safe
senses.definition: to protect something from danger, loss or attack
senses.definitionCN: 保护某物免受危险、损失或攻击
senses.example: The company hired guards to secure the building.
senses.exampleCN: 公司雇了保安来保护大楼。
senses.why: The verb turns the adjective into an action: to secure is to remove the care, to make the thing such that no worry is needed.
senses.whyCN: 动词把形容词变成动作：to secure 就是消除忧虑，让事物变成不必操心的状态。

senses.title: To fasten or tie down
senses.definition: to fasten something firmly so that it cannot move
senses.definitionCN: 把某物牢牢系住，使其不能移动
senses.example: Secure the boat to the dock before the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 暴风雨来临前把船系牢在码头上。
senses.why: Physical fastening is the concrete version of making safe. Tie the rope and the boat can no longer drift into danger.
senses.whyCN: 物理上的系缚是“使安全”的具体版本。把绳子系好，船就不会漂向危险。

senses.title: To obtain and keep
senses.definition: to succeed in getting something, especially after effort or competition
senses.definitionCN: 尤指经过努力或竞争后成功得到某物
senses.example: They secured the contract after months of talks.
senses.exampleCN: 经过数月谈判，他们拿到了合同。
senses.why: This 1743 sense adds 'hold' to 'get': what you secure is not merely obtained but made safe from rivals. The grip is part of the meaning.
senses.whyCN: 1743 年出现的这一义项在“得到”之外加了“握住”：secured 的东西不仅到手，还从对手那里保住了。抓握本身就是词义的一部分。

senses.title: To guarantee an outcome
senses.definition: to make something certain to happen or certain to be won
senses.definitionCN: 使某事必定发生或必定获胜
senses.example: Her second goal secured the victory.
senses.exampleCN: 她的第二个进球锁定了胜局。
senses.why: If an outcome is secure, no rival can take it away. Certainty here is safety applied to the future: the result can no longer change.
senses.whyCN: 如果结果 secure，就没有对手能把它拿走。这里的“确定”是把安全应用于未来：结果不再会改变。

intro.en: Secure is built from two Latin pieces: se- 'free from' and cura 'care'. Its earliest English sense was 'without care or fear', and modern meanings of safety, firmness and certainty all grow from that freedom from worry.
intro.cn: secure 由两个拉丁成分构成：se-“免于”与 cura“忧虑”。它最早的英语义是“无忧无惧”，现代的安全、牢固与确定等义都从“免于操心”生长出来。

items.en: Cura meant 'care, concern, trouble', and also 'medical treatment' (the source of cure). To be free of cura is to have nothing to worry about.
items.cn: cura 意为“忧虑、关切、麻烦”，也指“治疗”（cure 的来源）。免于 cura，就是没有可操心的事。

items.en: Securus, from se- 'free from' + cura, meant of persons 'free from care, quiet, easy', and of things 'tranquil, free from danger, safe'. It could also mean 'careless, reckless', since not caring can go too far.
items.cn: securus 由 se-“免于”加 cura 构成，指人“无忧、平静、自在”，指物“安宁、无危险、安全”。它也可表示“漫不经心、鲁莽”，因为“不在意”也能走过头。

items.en: English borrowed the word early as sicor, which became Middle English siker. This older layer survives in the doublet sure, which came in through Old French.
items.cn: 英语很早就借入作 sicor，后变为中古英语 siker。这一更早的层次保留在双式词 sure 中，后者是经古法语传入的。

items.en: The modern form secure is recorded from the 1530s, meaning 'without care or fear, dreading no evil'. In early use it often suggested over-confidence, 'too sure'.
items.cn: 现代形式 secure 于 16 世纪 30 年代有记录，意为“无忧无惧、不怕灾祸”。早期用法常暗示过度自信，即“太有把握”。

items.en: By c. 1600 places were called secure when free from danger. The sense 'affording grounds for confidence' is 1580s, and the mechanical sense 'firmly fixed' is by 1841, extended from that confidence.
items.cn: 到 1600 年前后，地方被称为 secure 是指没有危险。“令人有理由放心”的义项在 16 世纪 80 年代，机械义“牢固固定”则在 1841 年由这种“放心”延伸而来。

items.en: The verb appears c. 1600 as 'make safe'. 'Seize and hold' is 1640s, 'guarantee' 1650s, 'get possession of' 1743. Telephone lines 'not wiretapped' are called secure by 1961, and digital security follows.
items.cn: 动词约在 1600 年出现，意为“使安全”。“抓住并持有”为 17 世纪 40 年代，“保证”为 17 世纪 50 年代，“取得占有”为 1743 年。电话线路“未被窃听”在 1961 年被称为 secure，数字安全义随后而来。

note.en: The look-alike group contains two genuine relatives (sure and security) that learners often treat as unrelated. The near-meaning group compares adjectives of safety and firmness.
note.cn: 形近组里有两个真正的亲属词（sure 与 security），学习者常误以为无关。近义组比较表示安全与牢固的形容词。

entries.definition: certain or reliable. It is the same Latin securus that reached English twice, once directly and once through French.
entries.definitionCN: 确定的；可靠的。它与 secure 同出拉丁语 securus，只是分两条路进入英语，一条直接、一条经法语。

entries.definition: the state of being safe, or the measures taken to protect something. It is the noun from secure, not a separate root.
entries.definitionCN: 安全的状态，或为保护某物采取的措施。它是 secure 派生的名词，不是独立词根。

entries.definition: in a safe or firmly fixed way. It modifies a verb and cannot stand where the adjective secure is needed.
entries.definitionCN: 安全地；牢固地。它修饰动词，不能用在需要形容词 secure 的位置。

entries.definition: not likely to be harmed, lost or damaged. It is narrower than secure because it says nothing about worry or firmness.
entries.definitionCN: 不太可能受到伤害、丢失或损坏。它比 secure 窄，因为不涉及“忧虑”或“牢固”。

entries.definition: shielded from harm by something or someone. It stresses an external guard rather than an inner state of ease.
entries.definitionCN: 受到某物或某人庇护而免于伤害。它强调外部的护卫，而不是内心的安定。

entries.definition: solid, steady and not likely to move or change. It overlaps with secure in the 'firmly fixed' sense only.
entries.definitionCN: 坚实、稳定，不易移动或改变。它只在“牢固固定”义上与 secure 重叠。

entries.definition: to get or gain something, often by effort or purchase. It matches secure only in the 'obtain' sense, without the idea of holding it safe.
entries.definitionCN: 通过努力或购买得到某物。它只在“获得”义上与 secure 对应，不含“牢牢持有”的意思。

normalIntro.en: Pictures: a locked vault, a tied boat, a steady salary, a guard at the door. Each picture anchors one group of senses.
normalIntro.cn: 画面：上锁的金库、系牢的船、稳定的薪水、门口的保安。每幅画锚定一组义项。

normal.en: Se- means 'free from', cura means 'care': secure is literally 'no worries'.
normal.cn: se- 意为“免于”，cura 意为“忧虑”：secure 字面就是“没有忧虑”。

normal.en: A vault door that is locked and bolted is secure twice: no danger can enter and no stranger can either.
normal.cn: 一扇锁好、闩好的金库门是双重 secure：危险进不来，陌生人也进不来。

normal.en: Tie the boat to the dock: now it is secure, because it cannot drift.
normal.cn: 把船系在码头上：它现在 secure 了，因为漂不走了。

normal.en: A secure job is one whose salary will not disappear next month.
normal.cn: secure 的工作，就是下个月薪水不会消失的工作。

normal.en: A goal in the last minute secures the win: the result can no longer be taken away.
normal.cn: 最后一分钟的进球锁定了胜局：结果再也拿不走了。

abstract.en: One schema: NO CARE → NO DANGER → NO MOVEMENT → NO ACCESS → NO DOUBT. Five kinds of freedom from worry.
abstract.cn: 一个图式：无忧 → 无险 → 不动 → 不可进入 → 无疑。五种“免于操心”。

abstract.en: Root check: secure = se- + cura. The doublet sure and the noun security come from the same securus.
abstract.cn: 词根检查：secure = se- + cura。双式词 sure 与名词 security 都出自同一个 securus。

abstract.en: Contrast: safe says no danger; secure says no danger and no worry; protected says someone is guarding you.
abstract.cn: 对照：safe 说没有危险；secure 说既无危险也无忧虑；protected 说有谁在护着你。

examples.en: Store the backup drive in a secure cabinet.
examples.cn: 把备份硬盘存放在安全的柜子里。

examples.en: She secured a place at the university after two attempts.
examples.cn: 两次尝试之后，她拿到了大学的一个名额。

examples.en: Secure the tent ropes before the wind rises.
examples.cn: 风变大之前把帐篷绳固定好。

dict_mnemonic.text: “细Q啊”——细（心）Q（锁）啊，锁上门就无忧 → secure 安全的、使安全

root: 源自拉丁语 securus，由 se-“免于”加 cura“忧虑”构成，字面是“无忧的”；英语早期借作 sicor，后经法语又得双式词 sure。核心是“不必操心”。

sensesIntro.en: Secure begins as 'free from care'. Remove care in five directions and you get the five adjective senses: no danger (safe), no movement (firmly fixed), no anxiety (confident), no intruder (protected access), no money worry (financially safe). The verb then does the removing: make safe, fasten down, obtain and hold, or guarantee an outcome.
sensesIntro.cn: secure 的起点是“免于忧虑”。向五个方向去除忧虑，就得到五个形容词义：无危险（安全）、不移动（牢固）、无焦虑（安心）、无闯入者（受保护）、无金钱之忧（经济有保障）。动词则是在执行“去除”：使安全、系牢、获得并保住、确保结果。

core.en: Free from care: a state in which nothing needs worrying about because nothing can harm, move, enter or be lost.
core.cn: 免于忧虑：一种不必操心的状态，因为没有东西能伤害、移动、闯入或失去。

branches.en: SAFETY: physical safety and financial safety, two kinds of 'nothing can hurt me'.
branches.cn: 安全：身体安全与经济安全，两种“没有东西能伤到我”。

branches.en: FIXEDNESS: the adjective 'firmly fixed' and the verb 'to fasten down'.
branches.cn: 牢固：形容词“固定牢靠”与动词“系牢”。

branches.en: CERTAINTY: inner confidence and the guaranteeing of an outcome.
branches.cn: 确定：内心的自信与对结果的确保。

branches.en: ACCESS CONTROL: protection from anyone not allowed in.
branches.cn: 访问控制：不让未经许可者进入。

branches.en: VERB ACTIONS: making something safe, and getting something then holding it.
branches.cn: 动词动作：使某物安全，以及得到某物并握住。

intro.en: Secure has two productive parts, se- and cura, plus a large English family built on security and the doublet sure.
intro.cn: secure 有两个能产成分 se- 与 cura，另有以 security 和双式词 sure 为基础的大词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin securus and securitas are the direct sources. Cura is the noun inside both, and it also gives cure.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 securus 与 securitas 是直接来源。cura 是两者内部的“忧虑”名词，也是 cure 的来源。

items.meaning: free from care; safe; to make safe
items.example: The house is secure when the alarm is on.
items.exampleCN: 警报开启时房子就是安全的。

items.meaningCN: 不安全的；缺乏安全感的
items.example: He felt insecure about the interview.
items.exampleCN: 他对面试感到没有把握。

items.meaning: the state of being secure; protection
items.example: Airport security checked every bag.
items.exampleCN: 机场安检检查了每个包。

items.example: The lid was securely fastened.
items.exampleCN: 盖子被牢牢固定。

items.structure: doublet of secure via Old French
items.example: Are you sure about the date?
items.exampleCN: 你确定日期吗？

items.example: I assure you the money is safe.
items.exampleCN: 我向你保证钱是安全的。

items.example: The doctor reassured the patient.
items.exampleCN: 医生让病人安心。

items.example: The medicine cured the infection.
items.exampleCN: 这药治好了感染。

items.meaning: one who cares for a collection
items.meaningCN: 策展人；馆长（照管藏品的人）
items.example: The curator arranged the exhibition.
items.exampleCN: 策展人安排了展览。

items.meaning: to turn assets into tradable securities
items.example: The bank securitized the mortgage pool.
items.exampleCN: 银行把抵押贷款池证券化。

latinEntries.structure: Middle English, from Old English sicor

definition_zh: 寻找；寻求；追求；请求；试图；前往；（磁盘）寻道
definition_en: to try to find, obtain or reach something, often by searching or asking
core_image: 猎犬低头循着气味一路追下去
scene: 山里天黑得很快，两个徒步者看见远处有灯光。They walked toward the light to seek shelter, and after an hour they found a small hut with a dry floor.
sceneCN: 这里 seek 是「寻找、寻求」（第 1、4 个义项：找东西、找栖身之处）；句意：他们朝着灯光去寻找栖身之处，走了一小时才找到一间地面干燥的小屋。图中可辨识物件：头灯、山路、远处小屋、地图。

pos.zh: 寻找；寻求；追求；请求；试图

senses.title: To look for something lost or hidden
senses.titleCN: 寻找丢失或藏起的东西
senses.definition: to try to find something or someone, especially by searching a place
senses.definitionCN: 试图找到某物或某人，尤指通过搜索某地
senses.example: Police are seeking the missing child.
senses.exampleCN: 警方正在寻找失踪的孩子。
senses.why: The Old English verb secan meant 'search for, pursue, chase'. Its deepest root *sag- means 'to track down', the work of a dog following a scent.
senses.whyCN: 古英语动词 secan 意为“搜寻、追捕、追赶”。其最深词根 *sag- 意为“追踪”，正是猎犬循着气味做的事。

senses.title: To try to obtain
senses.definition: to try to get something you want or need, such as help, money or permission
senses.definitionCN: 努力得到你想要或需要的东西，如帮助、金钱或许可
senses.example: She is seeking a loan to start the business.
senses.exampleCN: 她正在申请贷款来创业。
senses.why: The search is no longer for a lost object but for a thing not yet possessed. The trail leads toward a goal, and the goal is the object sought.
senses.whyCN: 这里的搜寻对象不再是丢失之物，而是尚未拥有的东西。踪迹通向一个目标，而目标就是所 sought 之物。

senses.title: To ask for something
senses.definition: to ask someone for advice, permission or an opinion
senses.definitionCN: 向某人征求建议、许可或意见
senses.example: You should seek legal advice before signing.
senses.exampleCN: 签字前你应该征求法律意见。
senses.why: By late Old English secan also meant 'ask a question'. The physical search for a person becomes a verbal search for their knowledge.
senses.whyCN: 到古英语晚期，secan 也有“提问”之义。对一个人身体的寻找，变成了对其知识的言语寻求。

senses.title: To look for a place of refuge
senses.definition: to go looking for a place that offers safety, rest or protection
senses.definitionCN: 去寻找能提供安全、休息或保护的地方
senses.example: The hikers sought shelter from the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 徒步者寻找躲避暴风雨的地方。
senses.why: A place is sought the way an object is sought: by moving through space until the right thing appears. Shelter is a location that ends the search.
senses.whyCN: 寻找一个地方和寻找一个物件一样：在空间中移动，直到合适的东西出现。栖身处就是终结这场寻找的地点。

senses.title: To strive after a goal
senses.definition: to try to achieve or win something over time, such as fame, peace or justice
senses.definitionCN: 长期努力达成或赢得某物，如名声、和平或正义
senses.example: The movement seeks equality for all citizens.
senses.exampleCN: 这场运动追求全体公民的平等。
senses.why: A goal lies far ahead, so the search stretches into a long pursuit. Seek here means the sustained direction of effort, not a single search.
senses.whyCN: 目标在远方，于是寻找拉长成长久的追求。此义的 seek 指持续的努力方向，而不是一次性的搜索。

senses.title: To try to do something
senses.definition: in the pattern seek to do, to attempt or aim to do something
senses.definitionCN: 用于 seek to do 结构，表示试图或旨在做某事
senses.example: The new law seeks to reduce waste.
senses.exampleCN: 新法律旨在减少浪费。
senses.why: If you are seeking an outcome, your first move is an attempt. Seek to do is the attempt viewed from the starting point, before success is known.
senses.whyCN: 如果你在寻求某个结果，第一步就是尝试。seek to do 是从起点看这次尝试，此时成败未知。

senses.title: To go to a person or place
senses.definition: in older English, to go to someone for help, advice or authority; now largely archaic
senses.definitionCN: 在早期英语中，指前往某人处求帮助、建议或权威；今大体废弃
senses.example: The villagers sought the lord for judgment.
senses.exampleCN: 村民前往领主处求裁断。
senses.why: This is the oldest physical sense kept whole: you do not send a request, you walk to the person. Modern English replaced it with go to or consult.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的实义完整保留：你不是发出请求，而是走到那个人面前。现代英语已用 go to 或 consult 取代它。

senses.title: To seek out: find by deliberate search
senses.definition: to find someone or something by searching deliberately, especially when it is not obvious
senses.definitionCN: 通过刻意的寻找发现某人或某物，尤指其并不显眼时
senses.example: She sought out the one expert who could help.
senses.exampleCN: 她特意找到了唯一能帮忙的专家。
senses.why: The particle out adds completion: the search does not merely continue, it ends with the thing brought out of hiding.
senses.whyCN: 小品词 out 加了“完成”：寻找不只是持续，而是以“把东西从隐藏处找出来”结束。

senses.title: To move a disk head: computing
senses.definition: of a disk drive, to move the read-write head to the track that holds the required data
senses.definitionCN: （磁盘驱动器）把读写头移动到存有所需数据的磁道
senses.example: The drive seeks the correct track before reading.
senses.exampleCN: 驱动器在读取前先寻道到正确的磁道。
senses.why: A head moving across a platter is literally searching for a location. Computing named the movement a seek, and seek time measures how long the search takes.
senses.whyCN: 读写头在盘片上移动，字面上就是在寻找一个位置。计算机领域把这一移动命名为 seek，而 seek time 衡量这次寻找花多久。

intro.en: Seek is a native English verb with Germanic roots; its irregular past sought preserves the Old English form. The core image is a tracker following a trail, which then stretches into asking and striving.
intro.cn: seek 是英语本族动词，词根属日耳曼语；不规则的过去式 sought 保留了古英语形式。核心意象是追踪者循着踪迹前行，这一意象后来延伸为请求与追求。

items.en: The reconstructed root *sag- meant 'to track down, seek out'. Latin sagire 'to perceive keenly' and sagus 'presaging' are cognates, not sources of the English word.
items.cn: 重构词根 *sag- 意为“追踪、找出”。拉丁语 sagire“敏锐感知”与 sagus“预言的”是同源词，而不是英语词的来源。

items.en: The Germanic verb *sokjanan 'to seek' produced Old Saxon sokian, Old High German suohhan, German suchen and Gothic sokjan.
items.cn: 日耳曼语动词 *sokjanan“寻找”产生了古撒克逊语 sokian、古高地德语 suohhan、德语 suchen 与哥特语 sokjan。

items.en: Old English secan meant 'search for; pursue, chase; long for, wish for; look for, expect from'. Its past tense was sohte, the direct ancestor of sought.
items.cn: 古英语 secan 意为“搜寻；追捕、追赶；渴望、盼望；期待”。其过去式 sohte 正是 sought 的直接祖先。

items.en: Old Norse soekja reinforced the English verb during the Viking age. Without that influence the modern form would have been seech, which survives inside beseech.
items.cn: 维京时代古诺尔斯语 soekja 强化了这个英语动词。若没有这层影响，现代形式本会是 seech，它保留在 beseech 里。

items.en: Middle English sechen kept the old senses and added 'ask a question' by late Old English. The past tense sohte became sought, and the -k- form replaced the older -ch-.
items.cn: 中古英语 sechen 保留旧义，并在古英语晚期增加“提问”义。过去式 sohte 变为 sought，-k- 形式取代了较早的 -ch-。

items.en: Modern English settles on 'try to find or obtain', with fixed phrases seek out, seek to do and sought-after (1881). The computing sense 'move the head' is a 20th-century transfer of the same search image; specific first dates vary by dictionary.
items.cn: 现代英语定型为“试图找到或获得”，并有固定短语 seek out、seek to do 与 sought-after（1881）。计算机义“移动磁头”是同一“寻找”意象在 20 世纪的转移；具体首见年代各词典不一。

note.en: The look-alike group includes one true relative (beseech) and two words that only resemble seek in form. The near-meaning group compares verbs of searching and asking.
note.cn: 形近组包含一个真正的亲属词（beseech）和两个只在形式上像 seek 的词。近义组比较表示寻找与请求的动词。

entries.definition: ill, unwell. It is unrelated to seek and comes from a different Germanic root meaning 'ill'.
entries.definitionCN: 生病的。它与 seek 无关，出自另一个意为“病”的日耳曼词根。

entries.definition: the past tense and past participle of seek. It is not a separate word, though sought-after is an adjective.
entries.definitionCN: seek 的过去式与过去分词。它不是独立单词，但 sought-after 是形容词。

entries.definition: to beg urgently. It is be- + the older form of seek, and preserves the -ch- that the simple verb lost.
entries.definitionCN: 急切恳求。它是 be- 加 seek 的较早形式，保留了简单动词失掉的那个 -ch-。

entries.definition: to look carefully through a place or thing for something. It stresses examining a space rather than pursuing a goal.
entries.definitionCN: 仔细检查一个地方或东西以找某物。它强调检查空间，而不是追求目标。

entries.definition: to chase and kill animals, or to search eagerly. It is more physical and often more aggressive than seek.
entries.definitionCN: 追猎动物，或急切搜寻。它比 seek 更具体，也常更具攻击性。

entries.definition: to follow someone or something in order to catch or achieve it. It emphasizes continuous following, not the initial search.
entries.definitionCN: 跟随某人或某物以抓住或达成。它强调持续追随，而不是起初的寻找。

entries.definition: to ask for something politely or formally. It matches seek only in the 'ask for' sense.
entries.definitionCN: 礼貌或正式地请求某物。它只在“请求”义上与 seek 对应。

normalIntro.en: Pictures: a bloodhound on a trail, a hand reaching for a goal, a knock on a door for advice, a disk head sliding to a track.
normalIntro.cn: 画面：循迹的猎犬、伸向目标的手、为求建议敲开的门、滑向磁道的磁盘读写头。

normal.en: A bloodhound follows a scent: that is the oldest seek, tracking something down.
normal.cn: 猎犬循着气味走：这就是最古老的 seek，追踪某物。

normal.en: Your hand reaches for a cup across the table: seek is the reach, not yet the grasp.
normal.cn: 你的手伸向桌子对面的杯子：seek 是伸手，还没握到。

normal.en: You knock on a professor's door to seek advice: the walk and the question are one search.
normal.cn: 你敲开教授的门去 seek advice：走过去和开口问是同一次寻找。

normal.en: Seek out means the search ends with the thing pulled out of hiding.
normal.cn: seek out 意味着寻找以“把东西从藏处拉出来”结束。

normal.en: A disk head slides to the right track: machinery still calls that movement a seek.
normal.cn: 读写头滑到正确的磁道：机器仍把这次移动叫作 seek。

abstract.en: One schema: TRACK → SEARCH → PURSUE → STRIVE → ASK. Each later sense is the earlier one applied to something less physical.
abstract.cn: 一个图式：追踪 → 搜索 → 追捕 → 力争 → 请求。后一个义项都是前一个被用于更不具体的东西。

abstract.en: Form check: seek → sought, like bring → brought. The -k- is native; beseech keeps the older -ch-.
abstract.cn: 形式检查：seek → sought，如同 bring → brought。 -k- 是本族形式；beseech 保留了更早的 -ch-。

abstract.en: Contrast: search examines a place; seek heads for a goal; pursue keeps following; request only asks.
abstract.cn: 对照：search 检查一个地方；seek 朝目标去；pursue 持续跟随；request 只是请求。

examples.en: The company is seeking new ways to cut costs.
examples.cn: 这家公司正在寻找削减成本的新办法。

examples.en: He sought out his old teacher to thank her.
examples.cn: 他特意找到当年的老师当面道谢。

examples.en: Better to seek permission than to ask forgiveness later.
examples.cn: 事先征求许可，胜过事后请求原谅。

dict_mnemonic.text: “细克”——细（细地）克（克服障碍往前找）→ seek 寻找、追求

root: 源自原始印欧语 *sag-“追踪、找出”，经原始日耳曼语 *sokjanan 到古英语 secan“搜寻、追捕”，并受古诺尔斯语 soekja 影响；过去式 sought 保留古英语 sohte 的形式。

sensesIntro.en: Seek starts as a tracker following a trail. The trail can lead to a lost object (find it), to something not yet owned (obtain it), to a person's knowledge (ask for it), to a safe place (shelter), to a distant goal (strive for it), or to an attempt. Older English also used it for walking to a person, and computing for moving a head to a track.
sensesIntro.cn: seek 的起点是追踪者循着踪迹前行。这条踪迹可以通向丢失的物件（找到）、尚未拥有的东西（获得）、某人的知识（求教）、安全之处（避难）、远方的目标（追求），也可以通向一次尝试。早期英语还用它表示走到某人面前，计算机领域则用它表示把读写头移到某条磁道。

core.en: Following a trail toward something that is not yet in hand.
core.cn: 循着踪迹，朝尚未到手的东西前行。

branches.en: LOOKING FOR: a lost thing, a refuge, or something deliberately sought out.
branches.cn: 寻找：丢失之物、避难之处，或特意找出的东西。

branches.en: STRIVING FOR: obtaining what one needs, and pursuing a long-term goal.
branches.cn: 力争：获得所需之物，以及追求长期目标。

branches.en: ASKING: seeking advice or an answer, and the old sense of going to a person.
branches.cn: 请求：求教或求答，以及古老的“前往某人处”。

branches.en: ATTEMPT: seek to do, the try that starts before success is known.
branches.cn: 尝试：seek to do，在成败未知时开始的努力。

branches.en: MACHINE SEARCH: a disk head moving to the track that holds the data.
branches.cn: 机器搜寻：磁盘读写头移向存有数据的磁道。

intro.en: Seek is a native verb, so its 'affixes' are mostly English prefixes and compounds rather than Latin pieces. The irregular past is listed because it behaves like a built form.
intro.cn: seek 是本族动词，其“词缀”多为英语前缀与复合形式，而不是拉丁成分。不规则的过去式也列出来，因为它的形态像构造形式。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin source here. The Latin words below are cognates from the same PIE root, useful for memory but not ancestors of seek.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁来源。下面的拉丁词是同出原始印欧语词根的同源词，便于记忆，但不是 seek 的祖先。

items.example: They seek a peaceful solution.
items.exampleCN: 他们寻求和平解决。

items.meaning: the act of searching; present participle
items.example: Job seeking takes time.
items.exampleCN: 找工作需要时间。

items.example: He is a seeker of truth.
items.exampleCN: 他是一个追求真理的人。

items.meaning: searched for; past tense and participle
items.meaningCN: 寻找过；过去式与过去分词
items.example: The answer was sought by many.
items.exampleCN: 许多人都寻找过答案。

items.example: They besought him to stay.
items.exampleCN: 他们恳求他留下。

items.meaning: acting only for one's own advantage
items.meaningCN: 自私自利的；只顾自己的
items.example: His self-seeking motives were obvious.
items.exampleCN: 他自私的动机很明显。

items.meaning: a children's game of hiding and searching
items.example: The children played hide-and-seek.
items.exampleCN: 孩子们玩捉迷藏。

items.example: She sought out the best mechanic in town.
items.exampleCN: 她特意找了城里最好的修理工。

items.meaning: not searched for; not asked for
items.meaningCN: 未经寻求的；未被请求的
items.example: Unsought advice is rarely welcome.
items.exampleCN: 未经请求的建议很少受欢迎。

items.example: The painting is a sought-after piece.
items.exampleCN: 这幅画是抢手的藏品。

definition_zh: 挑选；选拔；选择；精选的；优等的；专属的；被选出的人
definition_en: to choose one or more from a group, or chosen for special quality or a special purpose
core_image: 从一筐苹果里挑出最好的几个，单独放在另一个篮子里
scene: 果园里，工人把颜色最好、没有碰伤的苹果挑出来。Workers select the apples with the best colour and no bruises for the gift boxes, and the rest go to the juice press.

senses.title: Chosen for special quality
senses.titleCN: 因品质出众而被选出的
senses.definition: of goods, food or places, chosen because they are of especially good quality
senses.definitionCN: （商品、食物或场所）因品质特别好而被选出的
senses.example: The shop sells select wines from small vineyards.
senses.exampleCN: 这家店出售来自小酒庄的精选葡萄酒。
senses.why: Latin seligere is se- 'apart' + legere 'gather'. The good ones are gathered out and set apart from the rest, so 'select' comes to mean 'of the picked quality'.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 seligere 是 se-“分开”加 legere“收集”。好的被收集出来、与其余分开，于是 select 引申为“被挑出来的上等品质”。

senses.title: Restricted to a chosen few
senses.definition: open only to a small group of people considered special or privileged
senses.definitionCN: 只对被视为特别或享有特权的一小群人开放
senses.example: The lecture was for a select audience of invited guests.
senses.exampleCN: 那场讲座只对受邀的少数听众开放。
senses.why: If only the picked few are admitted, the place itself becomes exclusive. Select as an adjective carries the closed door inside it.
senses.whyCN: 如果只让被挑出的少数人进入，这个地方本身就变得排他。作形容词的 select 里藏着一扇关着的门。

senses.title: To choose from a number
senses.definition: to choose one or more things or people from a larger group
senses.definitionCN: 从较大的一群中选出一个或几个事物或人
senses.example: Please select three books from the list.
senses.exampleCN: 请从书单中选三本书。
senses.why: The verb is the act of gathering out: you look across the whole set, then take some and leave the rest.
senses.whyCN: 动词就是“收集出来”的动作：你扫过整个集合，然后取走一些、留下其余。

senses.title: To pick according to criteria
senses.definition: to choose someone or something after judging them against a standard or requirement
senses.definitionCN: 按照标准或要求评判之后选出某人或某物
senses.example: Candidates were selected on the basis of test scores.
senses.exampleCN: 候选人依据考试成绩被选出。
senses.why: Selection is not random grabbing. The prefix se- 'apart' implies a reason for separating: the criterion is what makes one thing belong in the chosen pile.
senses.whyCN: 挑选不是随手抓取。前缀 se-“分开”暗示分离有理由：标准决定了某物为什么该进入“被选”的那一堆。

senses.title: To highlight on a screen
senses.definition: in computing, to mark text, files or options so that an action will apply to them
senses.definitionCN: 在计算机操作中标记文本、文件或选项，使某一操作作用于它们
senses.example: Select the paragraph and press delete.
senses.exampleCN: 选中这段文字然后按删除键。
senses.why: Highlighting sets the chosen text apart from the rest of the page, exactly as the Latin prefix sets the chosen objects apart from the pile.
senses.whyCN: 高亮把选中的文字与页面其余部分分开，正如拉丁前缀把选中的对象与那一堆分开。

senses.title: The chosen ones: a literary noun
senses.titleCN: 被选中的一群：书面名词
senses.definition: a group of people or things that have been chosen, especially as a collective noun
senses.definitionCN: 被选出的一群人或物，尤作集合名词
senses.example: Only the select were allowed into the inner hall.
senses.exampleCN: 只有被选中的少数人获准进入内厅。
senses.why: English turned the adjective into a noun around 1600. The select are not a random crowd but the set that has been gathered out.
senses.whyCN: 英语在 1600 年前后把形容词用作名词。the select 不是随便一群人，而是被收集出来的那个集合。

senses.title: A specially chosen committee
senses.definition: in British politics, a committee of members chosen to examine a particular subject
senses.definitionCN: 英国政治中，为审查某一特定议题而选出的议员委员会
senses.example: The select committee published its report on housing.
senses.exampleCN: 特别委员会发布了关于住房的报告。
senses.why: The body is not the whole parliament but a part picked out for one task. Select marks the narrow purpose of the group.
senses.whyCN: 这个机构不是整个议会，而是为一项任务挑出来的一部分。select 标记了该群体的狭窄用途。

senses.title: To pick a player for a team
senses.definition: in sport, to choose a player to represent a team or country
senses.definitionCN: 在体育中，选出代表队伍或国家出赛的运动员
senses.example: She was selected for the national squad at seventeen.
senses.exampleCN: 她十七岁时入选国家队。
senses.why: A squad is a set gathered out from all available players. Being selected means being moved from the pool into the smaller, named group.
senses.whyCN: 队伍是从所有可用运动员中收集出来的集合。被 selected 意味着从大池子被移进那个更小、有名字的群体。

senses.title: To retrieve data: the SQL verb
senses.titleCN: 检索数据：SQL 中的 select
senses.definition: in database languages, to retrieve specified rows or columns from a table
senses.definitionCN: 在数据库语言中，从表中取出指定的行或列
senses.example: The query selects all records from last year.
senses.exampleCN: 该查询选出上一年度的所有记录。
senses.why: A query picks out exactly the rows that meet a condition and sets them apart from the rest of the table. The database verb repeats the original image at machine speed.
senses.whyCN: 查询精确挑出符合条件的行，并把它们与表中其余部分分开。数据库动词以机器速度重演了最初的意象。

intro.en: Select comes from Latin seligere, 'to choose out', built from se- 'apart' and legere 'to gather'. Choosing is literally gathering some things out of a larger set and setting them aside.
intro.cn: select 来自拉丁语 seligere“选出”，由 se-“分开”与 legere“收集”构成。挑选字面上就是把一些东西从更大的集合里收集出来、放到一边。

items.en: The root *leg- meant 'to collect, gather'. It also gives Latin legere 'to read' (reading as gathering letters) and English collect, elect and legible.
items.cn: 词根 *leg- 意为“收集、聚拢”。它也给出拉丁语 legere“读”（读即收集字母）以及英语 collect、elect、legible。

items.en: Legere meant 'to gather, collect; pick out; read'. In selection the gathering is deliberate: the hand goes through the pile and takes only some items.
items.cn: legere 意为“收集、聚拢；挑出；读”。在挑选中，收集是有意的：手穿过那一堆，只取走某些东西。

items.en: Seligere combined se- 'apart' with legere, giving 'to choose out, single out, separate, cull'. The past participle selectus is the direct source of English select.
items.cn: seligere 把 se-“分开”与 legere 结合，意为“选出、挑出、分离、剔除”。其过去分词 selectus 正是英语 select 的直接来源。

items.en: English records both the adjective and the verb in the 1560s. The adjective first meant 'chosen on account of special excellence'; the verb meant 'single out from a number of things of the same kind'.
items.cn: 英语在 16 世纪 60 年代同时记录形容词与动词。形容词最初指“因特别优秀而被选出”，动词指“从若干同类事物中挑出”。

items.en: By the 1580s the adjective also meant 'carefully picked, choice, of special excellence'. The noun 'a selected person or thing' appears c. 1600.
items.cn: 到 16 世纪 80 年代，形容词又指“精心挑选的、上等的、特别优秀的”。名词“被选出的人或物”约在 1600 年出现。

items.en: Selection (1620s) extends the family into biology: methodical selection in breeding is recorded by 1837, and Darwin's natural selection follows in 1857. Screen and database uses of select are 20th-century extensions.
items.cn: selection（17 世纪 20 年代）把词族扩展到生物学：育种中的“人工选择”于 1837 年有记录，达尔文的“自然选择”随后在 1857 年出现。屏幕与数据库中的 select 是 20 世纪的延伸。

note.en: The look-alike group is mostly the same family with different endings, plus collect, a genuine cousin from the same legere root. The near-meaning group compares verbs of choosing.
note.cn: 形近组多是以不同词尾构成的同族词，另加 collect，它同出 legere 词根，是真正的表亲。近义组比较表示“选”的动词。

entries.definition: the act of choosing, or the set of things chosen. It is the noun, not the verb.
entries.definitionCN: 选择的行为，或被选出的一组东西。它是名词，不是动词。

entries.definition: choosing carefully, or applying only to some cases. It describes a manner, not the act of choosing.
entries.definitionCN: 挑剔的；有选择性的。它描述方式，而不是选择动作本身。

entries.definition: to gather things together. It uses the same legere 'gather' but with com- 'together' instead of se- 'apart'.
entries.definitionCN: 把东西收集到一起。它同样用 legere“收集”，但前缀是 com-“一起”而不是 se-“分开”。

entries.definition: to decide between two or more possibilities. It is the everyday word and needs no criterion.
entries.definitionCN: 在两个或更多可能之间作决定。它是最日常的词，不要求标准。

entries.definition: to choose casually or by pointing to what one wants. It is less formal and less systematic than select.
entries.definitionCN: 随意选择，或指着想要的东西选。它比 select 更不正式，也更不系统。

entries.definition: to choose someone by voting. It is a formal, public kind of selection.
entries.definitionCN: 通过投票选出某人。它是一种正式、公开的挑选。

entries.definition: to select and remove unwanted animals or items from a group. It stresses taking away, not keeping.
entries.definitionCN: 从一群中挑出并移除不要的动物或物品。它强调拿走，而不是留下。

normalIntro.en: Pictures: a hand sorting apples, a velvet rope at a door, a highlighted line of text, a team sheet with names.
normalIntro.cn: 画面：分拣苹果的手、门口的丝绒绳、被高亮的一行字、写满名字的队员名单。

normal.en: Se- 'apart' + legere 'gather': select is to gather some out of the pile.
normal.cn: se-“分开” + legere“收集”：select 就是从一堆里收集出一些。

normal.en: The best apples go into a separate crate: the crate is select, and so are the apples.
normal.cn: 最好的苹果被放进另一个箱子：这箱是 select，苹果也是 select。

normal.en: A velvet rope admits only the chosen few: select as an adjective is that rope.
normal.cn: 丝绒绳只放被选中的少数人进去：作形容词的 select 就是那根绳。

normal.en: Highlight a line on screen: the blue block is the text that has been selected.
normal.cn: 在屏幕上高亮一行：那块蓝色就是被 selected 的文字。

normal.en: A team sheet has eleven names out of hundreds: those players were selected.
normal.cn: 队员名单从几百人里写下十一个名字：这些球员是被 selected 的。

abstract.en: One schema: GATHER → SET APART → CHOOSE → THE PICKED FEW. Every sense sits on this line.
abstract.cn: 一个图式：收集 → 分开 → 选择 → 被挑出的少数。每个义项都在这条线上。

abstract.en: Root family: select, collect and elect all use legere 'gather'; the prefixes se-, com- and ex- decide the direction.
abstract.cn: 词根家族：select、collect、elect 都用 legere“收集”；前缀 se-、com-、ex- 决定方向。

abstract.en: Contrast: choose is neutral; pick is casual; select is systematic; elect is by vote; cull is by removal.
abstract.cn: 对照：choose 中性；pick 随意；select 系统；elect 投票；cull 以移除方式选。

examples.en: The best entries were selected for the final exhibition.
examples.cn: 最好的参赛作品被选入最终展览。

examples.en: This is a select neighbourhood with very few shops.
examples.cn: 这是一个住户不多、店铺很少的高档社区。

examples.en: Select the row you want to edit, then click rename.
examples.cn: 选中你要编辑的那一行，然后点击重命名。

dict_mnemonic.text: “四莱克特”——四（处）来（挑）克（服）特（别好的）→ select 精选、挑选

root: 源自拉丁语 seligere“选出”，由 se-“分开”加 legere“收集”构成；过去分词 selectus 直接进入英语。核心是“从一堆里收集出一些、放到一边”。

sensesIntro.en: Select is the act of gathering some things out of a larger set. Choose from many, screen by criteria, mark text on a screen, retrieve rows from a table, pick a player, or form a special committee: all are the same se- 'apart' plus legere 'gather'. As an adjective it names the quality of the gathered few, and as a noun it names those few themselves.
sensesIntro.cn: select 就是把一些东西从更大的集合里收集出来。从多个中选、按标准筛选、在屏幕上标记文字、从表中取出行、选拔队员、组成特别委员会，都是同一个 se-“分开”加 legere“收集”。作形容词时，它指被收集出来的少数所具有的品质；作名词时，它指那少数人本身。

core.en: Gathering some out of a larger set and setting them apart.
core.cn: 从更大的集合中收集出一些，并把它们放到一边。

branches.en: CHOOSING: the plain act of taking some from a group.
branches.cn: 选择：从一群中取走一些的最普通动作。

branches.en: SCREENING: choosing by a standard, which is why the chosen pile has a reason.
branches.cn: 筛选：按标准选择，因此被选的那一堆有理由。

branches.en: THE CHOSEN FEW: quality, exclusiveness and the group itself.
branches.cn: 被选出的少数：品质、排他性，以及这群人本身。

branches.en: MACHINE SELECTION: highlighted text and retrieved rows, the same cut at digital speed.
branches.cn: 机器选择：高亮的文字与检索出的行，是同一刀以数字速度重演。

branches.en: INSTITUTIONAL SELECTION: a special committee and a national squad.
branches.cn: 制度性选拔：特别委员会与国家队伍。

intro.en: Select belongs to the legere 'gather' family. The prefix decides whether the gathering is together, apart or out.
intro.cn: select 属于 legere“收集”词族。前缀决定这次收集是“到一起”“分开”还是“出去”。

latinIntro.en: Latin legere and its compounds seligere, colligere and eligere are the backbone of this family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 legere 及其复合词 seligere、colligere、eligere 是这个词族的骨架。

items.example: She is selective about her friends.
