definition_zh: 顺序；次序；一连串；数列；序列；片段；按顺序排列
definition_en: a set of things or events that follow one another in a particular order, or the order itself
core_image: 一串珠子被线穿起来，一颗接一颗，先后不能乱
scene: 实验室里，研究员把一段碱基序列打印在纸上。The letters run down the page in a fixed sequence, and the researcher says that a single change in that order would change the result.
sceneCN: 这里 sequence 是「序列」（第 6 个义项：生物化学中的碱基排列）；句意：字母在纸上按固定顺序往下排，研究员说这个顺序里只要有一位改变，结果就会不同。图中可辨识物件：测序仪、碱基字母表、打印纸、移液枪。

pos.zh: 顺序；次序；一连串；数列；序列；片段
按顺序排列；测定……的序列

senses.title: The order in which things follow
senses.definition: the order in which a set of related events, actions or items follow one another
senses.definitionCN: 一组相关事件、动作或项目彼此接续的顺序
senses.example: The sequence of events that night is still unclear.
senses.exampleCN: 那天晚上事件的先后顺序仍不清楚。
senses.why: Latin sequi means 'to follow'. A sequence is not just a collection but a collection seen as one thing following another, so the order itself becomes the meaning.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 sequi 意为“跟随”。sequence 不只是集合，而是被看作“一个接一个”的集合，于是顺序本身成了词义。

senses.title: A connected series of things
senses.definition: a number of things of the same kind that come one after another
senses.definitionCN: 同类事物一个接一个地出现的一串
senses.example: The book is a sequence of short stories set in one town.
senses.exampleCN: 这本书是一连串发生在同一座小镇的短篇故事。
senses.why: Follow one thing with another and you get a chain. The word names the chain as a whole, not only the rule of its ordering.
senses.whyCN: 让一物跟着另一物，就得到一条链。这个词指整条链，而不只是排列规则。

senses.title: A fixed order that must be kept
senses.definition: a particular order that is correct or required, as in a procedure or code
senses.definitionCN: 正确或必需的特定顺序，如程序或密码中的顺序
senses.example: Enter the numbers in the correct sequence.
senses.exampleCN: 按正确顺序输入数字。
senses.why: Once following is required, reversing two steps breaks the whole. Sequence becomes a rule: the order matters, not just the items.
senses.whyCN: 一旦“跟随”成为要求，调换两步就会毁掉整体。sequence 变成规则：重要的不是项目，而是次序。

senses.title: A sung passage in the old liturgy
senses.definition: in church music, a hymn or chant sung after the Alleluia and before the Gospel
senses.definitionCN: 教会音乐中，在哈利路亚之后、福音之前唱的一首赞美诗或吟唱
senses.example: The choir sang the Easter sequence.
senses.exampleCN: 唱诗班唱了复活节续唱。
senses.why: This is the word's first English sense, late 14c. Medieval Latin sequentia meant 'a following', because the chant followed the Alleluia. The musical sense is the oldest recorded one.
senses.whyCN: 这是该词最早的英语义项，14 世纪晚期。中世纪拉丁语 sequentia 意为“跟随”，因为这首唱段跟随在哈利路亚之后。音乐义是最早有记录的义项。

senses.title: A run of cards
senses.definition: in card games, a set of three or more consecutive cards of the same suit
senses.definitionCN: 纸牌游戏中，同花色三张或以上连续的牌
senses.example: He laid down a sequence of hearts.
senses.exampleCN: 他打出了一串红桃顺子。
senses.why: Cards in a run follow one another by number. The 1570s recorded this sense alongside the general 'series of things', and both rest on following.
senses.whyCN: 顺子里的牌按点数彼此跟随。16 世纪 70 年代这一义项与一般“一连串”义同时有记录，两者都立足于“跟随”。

senses.title: The order of bases in DNA
senses.definition: in biochemistry, the order of nucleotides in a nucleic acid molecule
senses.definitionCN: 生物化学中，核酸分子里核苷酸的排列顺序
senses.example: The sequence of this gene differs by one base.
senses.exampleCN: 这个基因的序列有一个碱基不同。
senses.why: A genome is a text written in four letters, and the letters must follow in exactly the right order. Biochemistry borrowed sequence for that ordered string in 1959.
senses.whyCN: 基因组是用四个字母写成的文本，字母必须严格按正确顺序跟随。生物化学在 1959 年借用了 sequence 来指这条有序字符串。

senses.title: An ordered list in mathematics
senses.definition: in mathematics, an ordered list of numbers or terms, often following a rule
senses.definitionCN: 数学中按规则排列的一列数或项
senses.example: The sequence 2, 4, 8, 16 doubles each time.
senses.exampleCN: 数列 2、4、8、16 每次都翻倍。
senses.why: Mathematics makes the following explicit: each term is placed after the one before by a rule. The sequence is the list, and the rule is what keeps it in line.
senses.whyCN: 数学把“跟随”明确化：每一项按规则排在前一项之后。sequence 是这张列表，而规则让它保持队形。

senses.title: A passage of film
senses.definition: a series of related shots that form one continuous scene or unit in a film
senses.definitionCN: 构成影片中一个连续场景或单元的一组相关镜头
senses.example: The opening sequence lasts four minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 开场片段持续四分钟。
senses.why: Shots follow one another in time, and a group of them makes a larger unit that also follows the next. Film uses sequence for both the chain and the hand-off.
senses.whyCN: 镜头在时间上彼此跟随，一组镜头又构成更大单元，继续接向下一个。电影用 sequence 同时指链和链上的交接。

senses.title: To arrange or determine order
senses.definition: to arrange things in a particular order, or to determine the order of a molecule's units
senses.definitionCN: 把事物按特定顺序排列，或测定分子各单元的排列
senses.example: The lab sequenced the sample in two days.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室两天内测定了样本的序列。
senses.why: The verb turns the noun into work: either you impose the following (arrange), or you read it off (sequence a genome). Both are acts of ordering.
senses.whyCN: 动词把名词变成工作：要么你规定“跟随”（排列），要么你把它读出来（测序）。两者都是排序行为。

intro.en: Sequence comes from Latin sequi 'to follow', not from secare 'to cut'. The same root gives consequence, sequel and subsequent; the look-alike sec- family belongs to a different knife.
intro.cn: sequence 来自拉丁语 sequi“跟随”，不是 secare“切”。同一词根给出 consequence、sequel、subsequent；形近的 sec- 词族属于另一把刀。

items.en: The root *sekw- meant 'to follow'. It gives Latin sequi, Greek hepesthai, Sanskrit sacate and Old Irish sechim, and it underlies English sequence, sequel, second and society.
items.cn: 词根 *sekw- 意为“跟随”。它给出拉丁语 sequi、希腊语 hepesthai、梵语 sacate 与古爱尔兰语 sechim，也是英语 sequence、sequel、second、society 的底层词根。

items.en: Sequi meant 'to follow, come after'. Its present participle sequens 'following' produced the noun sequentia, 'a following, a succession'.
items.cn: sequi 意为“跟随、随后而来”。其现在分词 sequens“跟随的”造出名词 sequentia，意为“跟随、接续”。

items.en: In church use sequentia named the chant that followed the Alleluia. It was a partial loan-translation of Greek akolouthia 'a following', which had the same liturgical sense.
items.cn: 在教会用法中，sequentia 指跟随在哈利路亚之后的唱段。它是对希腊语 akolouthia“跟随”的部分仿译，后者也有同样的礼拜含义。

items.en: English first recorded sequence in late 14c. as the name of that liturgical chant, borrowed through Old French sequence 'answering verses'.
items.cn: 英语最早在 14 世纪晚期记录 sequence，指的就是这个礼拜唱段，经古法语 sequence“应答诗句”借入。

items.en: The general sense 'a series of things following in a certain order' is recorded by the 1570s, along with the card-game 'run'. 'Order of succession' appears in the 1580s.
items.cn: 一般义“按某种顺序接续的一串事物”于 16 世纪 70 年代有记录，牌戏“顺子”义同时出现。“继任顺序”义在 16 世纪 80 年代出现。

items.en: Biochemistry adopted sequence for nucleotide order by 1959. The verb 'arrange in a sequence' is recorded from 1954 in computing and in biochemistry by 1970.
items.cn: 生物化学在 1959 年用 sequence 指核苷酸顺序。动词“按顺序排列”于 1954 年在计算机领域有记录，1970 年进入生物化学。

note.en: The look-alike group is dominated by the sequ- 'follow' family. The near-meaning group compares words for ordered sets. Remember throughout: sequi, not secare.
note.cn: 形近组以 sequ-“跟随”词族为主。近义组比较表示有序集合的词。全程记住：是 sequi，不是 secare。

entries.definition: a result that follows from an action. It is con- 'together' + sequi, literally 'what follows with it'.
entries.definitionCN: 由某一行为引出的结果。它是 con-“一起”加 sequi，字面是“随之而来的东西”。

entries.definition: following in order, one after another. It describes the manner, while sequence names the thing.
entries.definitionCN: 按顺序一个接一个的。它描述方式，而 sequence 指事物本身。

entries.definition: following in time or order; subsequent. It is a formal adjective, not the noun.
entries.definitionCN: 在时间或顺序上随后的。它是正式形容词，不是名词。

entries.definition: a number of similar things arranged in a line or coming one after another. It comes from serere 'join', not sequi.
entries.definitionCN: 排成一行或接连出现的同类事物。它出自 serere“连接”，不是 sequi。

entries.definition: the arrangement of things according to a rule or plan. It is broader than sequence and can be spatial as well as temporal.
entries.definitionCN: 按规则或计划对事物的安排。它比 sequence 宽，可指空间也可指时间。

entries.definition: a number of people or things following one another, especially in office or inheritance. It stresses taking another's place.
entries.definitionCN: 一个接一个的人或物，尤指职位或继承。它强调接替他人的位置。

entries.definition: the process of moving forward step by step. It stresses development rather than mere listing.
entries.definitionCN: 一步一步向前的过程。它强调发展，而不只是罗列。

normalIntro.en: Pictures: beads on a string, a queue at a door, a DNA readout, numbered steps in a recipe.
normalIntro.cn: 画面：串起来的珠子、门口排队的人、DNA 测序读数、菜谱里编号的步骤。

normal.en: Beads on one string: each bead follows the one before, and the whole string is the sequence.
normal.cn: 一根线上的珠子：每颗都跟着前一颗，整根线就是 sequence。

normal.en: A queue only works if everyone follows the person ahead: sequence is that rule.
normal.cn: 队伍只有在每个人都跟着前一个人时才成立：sequence 就是这条规则。

normal.en: A recipe numbers its steps: step 2 follows step 1, and swapping them ruins the dish.
normal.cn: 菜谱给步骤编号：第 2 步跟着第 1 步，调换就毁了这道菜。

normal.en: A DNA readout is a string of letters in exact order: that string is a sequence.
normal.cn: DNA 读数是严格按顺序排列的一串字母：这串就是 sequence。

normal.en: A film's opening sequence is a chain of shots that hands off to the next chain.
normal.cn: 电影的开场 sequence 是一串镜头，再交接给下一串。

abstract.en: One schema: FOLLOW → A FOLLOWING → SUCCESSION → FIXED ORDER → SERIES → ARRANGEMENT.
abstract.cn: 一个图式：跟随 → 一次接续 → 连续 → 固定次序 → 系列 → 排列。

abstract.en: Root check: sequence, sequel, second, consequence all follow sequi. Section and sector cut with secare. Never mix the two.
abstract.cn: 词根检查：sequence、sequel、second、consequence 都跟随 sequi。section 与 sector 用 secare 切。两者绝不能混。

abstract.en: Contrast: sequence is ordered following; series is joined similars; order is any arrangement; progression is forward development.
abstract.cn: 对照：sequence 是有序跟随；series 是连接起来的同类；order 是任何排列；progression 是向前发展。

examples.en: The film's final sequence ties every story together.
examples.cn: 影片的最后一段把所有线索串了起来。

examples.en: The software runs the steps in a fixed sequence.
examples.cn: 软件按固定顺序执行这些步骤。

examples.en: Scientists sequenced the virus within a week.
examples.cn: 科学家在一周内测定了该病毒的序列。

dict_mnemonic.text: “西宽斯”——西（边）宽（宽地）斯（跟着）排开 → sequence 顺序、序列

root: 源自拉丁语 sequi“跟随”，经 sequentia“接续”进入英语；与 secare“切”无关。同根词有 consequence、sequel、subsequent、second。

sensesIntro.en: Sequence is following made into a thing. Events follow in time, cards follow by number, bases follow along a DNA strand, numbers follow a rule, shots follow in a film, and steps follow in a procedure. The oldest sense is liturgical: a chant that follows the Alleluia. The verb either imposes the order or reads it off.
sensesIntro.cn: sequence 是把“跟随”变成一样东西。事件在时间上跟随，牌按点数跟随，碱基沿 DNA 链跟随，数字按规则跟随，镜头在影片中跟随，步骤在流程中跟随。最古老的义项是礼拜性的：跟随在哈利路亚之后的唱段。动词则要么规定顺序，要么把顺序读出来。

core.en: A chain in which each item follows the one before, and the order itself matters.
core.cn: 一条链，其中每一项都跟着前一项，而顺序本身很重要。

branches.en: ORDER IN TIME: the sequence of events and a required order that cannot be swapped.
branches.cn: 时间中的顺序：事件序列，以及不可调换的规定次序。

branches.en: ORDERED SETS: a connected series of things, and a mathematical list ruled by a pattern.
branches.cn: 有序集合：一串相关事物，以及按规律排列的数列。

branches.en: HISTORICAL AND PLAY FORMS: the liturgical chant and the card run.
branches.cn: 历史与游戏形式：礼拜唱段与牌局顺子。

branches.en: BIOCHEMISTRY: the base order of DNA and the act of determining or arranging it.
branches.cn: 生物化学：DNA 的碱基顺序，以及测定或排列它的动作。

branches.en: FILM: a chain of shots that forms one unit and hands off to the next.
branches.cn: 电影：构成一个单元并交接给下一单元的一串镜头。

intro.en: Sequence sits in the large sequ- 'follow' family. The items below show the family and keep the root separate from sec- 'cut'.
intro.cn: sequence 属于庞大的 sequ-“跟随”词族。下列条目展示这个词族，并把词根与 sec-“切”分开。

latinIntro.en: Latin sequi 'follow' and sequentia 'a following' are the sources. Secare 'cut' is a different root and must not be attached here.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 sequi“跟随”与 sequentia“接续”是来源。secare“切”是另一个词根，不可挂到这里。

items.example: The sequence of steps is fixed.
items.exampleCN: 步骤的顺序是固定的。

items.example: The tasks are sequential, not parallel.
items.exampleCN: 这些任务按顺序进行，不是并行。

items.example: The sequel was better than the first film.
items.exampleCN: 续集比第一部电影更好。

items.example: He accepted the consequences.
items.exampleCN: 他承担了后果。

items.example: It rained; consequently, the match was cancelled.
items.exampleCN: 下雨了，比赛因此取消。

items.example: Subsequent tests confirmed the result.
items.exampleCN: 后续测试证实了结果。

items.example: Genome sequencing is now routine.
items.exampleCN: 基因组测序如今已很常规。

items.meaning: a device that arranges or reads out a sequence
items.example: The sequencer reads the order of bases.
items.exampleCN: 测序仪读出碱基的顺序。

items.meaning: an unbroken transition from one thing to another
items.example: She segued from the report into questions.
items.exampleCN: 她从报告无缝转入了提问环节。

items.meaning: following another's wishes too eagerly; servile
items.example: The waiter was almost obsequious.
items.exampleCN: 那名服务员几乎有些谄媚。

definition_zh: 系列；一连串；丛书；电视连续剧；系列赛；级数；串联；地层系列
definition_en: a number of similar things joined or arranged one after another, or a set issued or happening in order
core_image: 把一颗颗珠子用线穿成一串，珠子还在，线把它们连起来
scene: 书店架上摆着一整套同一封面的小说，从第一册排到第十册。店员说：This is the whole series.
sceneCN: 这里 series 是「丛书、系列出版物」（第 3 个义项：成套发行的同类作品）；句意：这是一整套。图中可辨识物件：统一封面的书、编号书脊、书架、价签。

pos.zh: 系列；一连串；丛书；连续剧；系列赛；级数

collocations.zh: 世界大赛（棒球总冠军系列赛）

senses.title: A row of similar things
senses.definition: a number of things of the same kind that come one after another, often arranged in a line
senses.definitionCN: 同类事物一个接一个出现，常排成一行
senses.example: The lab ran a series of tests on the sample.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室对样本做了一系列测试。
senses.why: Latin serere means 'to join, link, arrange in a row'. A series is not a random pile but things linked into a line, each joined to the next.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 serere 意为“连接、串起、排成行”。series 不是随便一堆，而是被连成一条线的事物，每一个都与下一个相连。

senses.title: A chain of events
senses.definition: a set of related events or actions that follow one another over time
senses.definitionCN: 在时间上一个接一个发生的一组相关事件或行动
senses.example: A series of storms hit the coast last winter.
senses.exampleCN: 去年冬天一连串风暴袭击了海岸。
senses.why: Events can be linked in time the way beads are linked on a string. The word treats them as one connected run rather than separate happenings.
senses.whyCN: 事件可以像线上的珠子那样在时间中被串起来。这个词把它们看作一段连起来的连续过程，而不是彼此分离的事情。

senses.title: A set of published works
senses.definition: a set of books, articles or other works published one after another with something in common
senses.definitionCN: 一本接一本出版、具有共同点的一套书、文章或其他作品
senses.example: The publisher reissued the whole series in new covers.
senses.exampleCN: 出版社以新封面重版了整套丛书。
senses.why: Publishing joined separate volumes into one commercial line. The 1711 sense names the set, while each volume remains a separate bead.
senses.whyCN: 出版业把分开的各卷连成一条商业线。1711 年的义项指整套，而每一卷仍是独立的一颗珠子。

senses.title: A television or radio run
senses.definition: a set of programmes with the same characters, setting or theme, broadcast in order
senses.definitionCN: 具有相同人物、背景或主题、按顺序播出的一组节目
senses.example: The series has run for six seasons.
senses.exampleCN: 这部连续剧已播出六季。
senses.why: Each episode follows the last, yet the whole run is one unit. Broadcasters took the publishing sense and attached it to time rather than paper.
senses.whyCN: 每一集跟着上一集，而整轮播出又是一个单元。广播业借用了出版义，把它从纸张移到了时间。

senses.title: A set of games between the same teams
senses.titleCN: 同一两队之间的系列赛
senses.definition: in sport, a set of games played between the same opponents on consecutive or scheduled days
senses.definitionCN: 体育中，同一对手在连续或约定日期进行的一组比赛
senses.example: They won the three-game series two to one.
senses.exampleCN: 他们以二比一赢下了三场系列赛。
senses.why: Separate games are joined into a larger contest, and the winner of the series is the winner of the linked set. Baseball recorded this sense in 1862.
senses.whyCN: 一场场比赛被连成更大的较量，系列赛的赢家就是这组连接起来的比赛的赢家。棒球在 1862 年记录了这一义项。

senses.title: A sum of terms: mathematical series
senses.definition: in mathematics, the sum of the terms of a sequence
senses.definitionCN: 数学中，一个数列各项之和
senses.example: The infinite series converges to two.
senses.exampleCN: 这个无穷级数收敛于二。
senses.why: Mathematics links terms with plus signs. A sequence is the list; a series is the linked total, which is why the two words are often confused.
senses.whyCN: 数学用加号把各项连起来。sequence 是列表，series 是连起来的总和，这也是两个词常被混淆的原因。

senses.title: A series circuit
senses.definition: in electronics, a circuit in which components are connected one after another so the same current passes through each
senses.definitionCN: 电子学中，元件一个接一个连接、同一电流依次通过每个元件的电路
senses.example: If one bulb fails in a series circuit, the whole string goes dark.
senses.exampleCN: 串联电路中若一个灯泡坏了，整串都会熄灭。
senses.why: The components are joined end to end like beads. One break stops the chain, which is exactly what 'joined in a row' predicts.
senses.whyCN: 元件像珠子一样首尾相连。一处断开就终止整条链，这正是“连成一排”所预示的结果。

senses.title: A set of stamps or notes issued together
senses.titleCN: 成套发行的邮票或纸币
senses.definition: a set of coins, stamps or banknotes issued together as one design family
senses.definitionCN: 作为同一设计家族一起发行的一套硬币、邮票或纸币
senses.example: The new series of notes features local birds.
senses.exampleCN: 新一版纸币以本地鸟类为图案。
senses.why: Issuers release a family of items at once, each different but linked by design. Collectors call the linked family a series.
senses.whyCN: 发行方一次推出一组物件，彼此不同却由设计连在一起。收藏者把这组连起来的家族称为 series。

senses.title: A layer in geology
senses.definition: in geology, a group of rock strata formed during one period and treated as a unit
senses.definitionCN: 地质学中，在一个时期内形成并作为一个单元处理的一组岩层
senses.example: The cliff exposes a series of sandstone layers.
senses.exampleCN: 悬崖露出了一系列砂岩层。
senses.why: Strata are laid down one after another and joined in a vertical line. Geology borrowed the 'linked row' for layers stacked in time.
senses.whyCN: 岩层一层接一层沉积，在垂直方向上连成一线。地质学借用“连成一排”来指按时间堆叠的层。

intro.en: Series comes from Latin serere 'to join, link, arrange in a row', not from sequi 'to follow'. A series is a row of things fastened together; a sequence is things following in order. The roots are different and the words are not interchangeable.
intro.cn: series 来自拉丁语 serere“连接、串起、排成行”，不是 sequi“跟随”。series 是被连在一起的一排东西；sequence 是按顺序跟随的事物。词根不同，两者不能互换。

items.en: The root *ser- meant 'to line up, arrange in a row'. It underlies Latin serere and English series, serial, insert, assert and desert.
items.cn: 词根 *ser- 意为“排成行、排列”。它是拉丁语 serere 以及英语 series、serial、insert、assert、desert 的底层词根。

items.en: Serere meant 'to join, link, bind together, arrange, attach, put; join in speech'. The image is physical: things are fastened into a chain or row.
items.cn: serere 意为“连接、串起、绑在一起、排列、附着、放置；连起来讲”。意象是具体的：东西被系成链或排成行。

items.en: The noun series meant 'row, chain, series, sequence, succession'. Latin already used it for both a physical row and an order of things.
items.cn: 名词 series 意为“排、链、系列、连续、接续”。拉丁语已同时用它指实物的一排和事物的次序。

items.en: English first had serie in late 14c., meaning a 'sequence of thoughts, discussion of a subject'. The Latin-shaped series replaced it in the 17th century.
items.cn: 英语最早在 14 世纪晚期有 serie，意为“思路的顺序、对某主题的论述”。17 世纪时，拉丁形的 series 取代了它。

items.en: Series is recorded from the 1610s as 'a number or set of things of one kind arranged in a line, a continued succession of similar things'. The publishing sense follows in 1711.
items.cn: series 于 17 世纪 10 年代有记录，意为“同类事物排成一行的一组，类似事物的连续接续”。出版义在 1711 年跟进。

items.en: Radio or television series is recorded from 1949; the baseball series from 1862. Mathematical and electrical uses are 19th-century specializations of the same linked row.
items.cn: 广播或电视连续剧义于 1949 年有记录，棒球系列赛义于 1862 年。数学与电学用法是同一“连成一排”在 19 世纪的专业化。

note.en: The look-alike group contains serious (pure spelling danger), serial (same root) and sequence (a different root with a similar meaning). Read the notes carefully.
note.cn: 形近组包含 serious（纯拼写陷阱）、serial（同根）与 sequence（词根不同但意思相近）。请细读说明。

entries.definition: important, severe or not joking. It is unrelated to series and comes from Latin serius 'weighty'.
entries.definitionCN: 重要的、严重的或不玩笑的。它与 series 无关，出自拉丁语 serius“沉重的”。

entries.definition: of or forming a series; a story told in parts. It is the adjective and noun built on series.
entries.definitionCN: 系列的；连载的；连载故事。它是由 series 构成的形容词与名词。

entries.definition: an order of things following one another. It comes from sequi 'to follow', while series comes from serere 'to join'.
entries.definitionCN: 事物一个接一个的顺序。它出自 sequi“跟随”，而 series 出自 serere“连接”。

entries.definition: a set of things following in a particular order. It stresses the rule of following, while series stresses the linked row.
entries.definitionCN: 按特定顺序接续的一组事物。它强调跟随的规则，而 series 强调连成一排。

entries.definition: a number of things or people following one another, especially in office. It is more formal than series.
entries.definitionCN: 一个接一个的事物或人，尤指职位接替。它比 series 更正式。

entries.definition: a continuous period or sequence of similar events. It is informal and often used of successes or performances.
entries.definitionCN: 一段连续时期或一连串类似事件。它较口语，常用于成功或演出。

entries.definition: a group of things that belong together. It stresses membership in one group rather than the order of a row.
entries.definitionCN: 属于一起的一组东西。它强调同属一组，而不是排成行的次序。

normalIntro.en: Pictures: beads on a string, books in one cover design, episodes in order, bulbs in a chain.
normalIntro.cn: 画面：串起的珠子、同一封面设计的书、按序播放的剧集、连成一串的灯泡。

normal.en: Serere means 'join': a series is beads joined on one string, not beads that merely follow.
normal.cn: serere 意为“连接”：series 是串在一根线上的珠子，而不只是彼此跟随。

normal.en: Ten books with one cover design stand in a row: that row is a series.
normal.cn: 十本同一封面设计的书排成一行：这一排就是 series。

normal.en: A TV series is a row of episodes joined by the same characters.
normal.cn: 电视 series 是由同样人物连起来的一排剧集。

normal.en: Bulbs in a series circuit are joined end to end; one break darkens the whole string.
normal.cn: 串联电路里的灯泡首尾相连；断一处，整串都黑。

normal.en: A series of stamps is a family issued together, each different but linked by design.
normal.cn: 一套邮票是一起发行的家族，每张不同，却由设计连在一起。

abstract.en: One schema: JOIN → ROW → LINKED SET → PUBLISHED RUN → TECHNICAL ORDER.
abstract.cn: 一个图式：连接 → 一排 → 连成的集合 → 出版连载 → 技术序列。

abstract.en: Root check: series = serere 'join'. sequence = sequi 'follow'. Do not write 'series of events follow sequi'.
abstract.cn: 词根检查：series = serere“连接”。sequence = sequi“跟随”。不要写成 series 来自 sequi。

abstract.en: Contrast: a series is joined similars; a sequence is ordered followers; a set is members of one group.
abstract.cn: 对照：series 是连接起来的同类；sequence 是有序的跟随者；set 是同属一组的成员。

examples.en: The museum is hosting a series of talks on climate.
examples.cn: 博物馆正在举办一系列气候讲座。

examples.en: This is the third book in the series.
examples.cn: 这是该系列的第三本书。

examples.en: The two teams meet for a three-game series this weekend.
examples.cn: 两队本周末进行三场系列赛。

dict_mnemonic.text: “西瑞斯”——西（边）瑞（雪）斯（串）连成一排 → series 系列、丛书

root: 源自拉丁语 serere“连接、串起、排成行”，名词 series 意为“排、链、连续”。与 sequi“跟随”无关：series 强调连成一排，sequence 强调按顺序跟随。

sensesIntro.en: Series is a row of things joined together. Tests, storms, books, episodes, games, numbers, circuit parts, stamps and rock layers can all be linked into such a row. Each sense keeps the same picture: separate items, one connecting line. The word is not sequence: series joins, sequence follows.
sensesIntro.cn: series 是被连起来的一排东西。测试、风暴、书、剧集、比赛、数字、电路元件、邮票与岩层，都能被连成这样一排。每个义项都保留同一幅画面：各自独立的项目，一条连接的线。它不是 sequence：series 讲连接，sequence 讲跟随。

core.en: Separate similar items joined into one row or run.
core.cn: 彼此独立的同类项目，被连成一行或一段连续过程。

branches.en: ROW AND CHAIN: things arranged in a line, and events linked over time.
branches.cn: 一排与一条链：排成一行的事物，以及在时间中连起来的事件。

branches.en: PUBLISHING AND BROADCAST: a set of volumes, and a run of episodes.
branches.cn: 出版与广播：一套书，以及一轮剧集。

branches.en: COLLECTED SETS: games between the same teams, and stamps or notes issued together.
branches.cn: 成套收藏：同一两队之间的比赛，以及一起发行的邮票或纸币。

branches.en: TECHNICAL LINKING: a summed mathematical series, and components joined end to end.
branches.cn: 技术连接：求和的数学级数，以及首尾相连的电路元件。

branches.en: GEOLOGY: strata laid down one after another and treated as one unit.
branches.cn: 地质：一层接一层沉积、作为一个单元处理的岩层。

intro.en: Series belongs to the serere 'join' family. Note how many common English words hide this 'join' inside them.
intro.cn: series 属于 serere“连接”词族。注意有多少常用英语词把“连接”藏在里面。

latinIntro.en: Latin serere 'join' and its participle sertus are the sources. English insert, assert and desert all descend from the same verb.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 serere“连接”及其分词 sertus 是来源。英语 insert、assert、desert 都出自同一个动词。

items.exampleCN: 一系列实验证实了这一点。

items.example: The novel first appeared in serial form.
items.exampleCN: 这部小说最初以连载形式发表。

items.meaning: to publish or convert into a series
items.example: The story was serialized in a magazine.
items.exampleCN: 这个故事在杂志上连载。

items.example: The units are connected serially.
items.exampleCN: 这些单元是串联的。

items.example: The leaves are seriate along the stem.
items.exampleCN: 叶子沿茎成系列排列。

items.example: Seriation helps date the pottery.
items.exampleCN: 排序法有助于给陶器断代。

items.meaning: to put something into something else
items.example: Insert the card into the slot.
items.exampleCN: 把卡插入槽中。

items.meaning: to state firmly; literally to join a claim to oneself
items.meaningCN: 断言；坚称（字面“把主张接到自己身上”）
items.example: She asserted that the plan would work.
items.exampleCN: 她断言该计划可行。

items.meaning: to abandon; literally to unjoin oneself
items.meaningCN: 抛弃；遗弃（字面“把自己从连接中解开”）
items.example: He deserted his post.
items.exampleCN: 他擅离岗位。

items.meaning: a circuit joined end to end
items.example: A series circuit shares one current path.
items.exampleCN: 串联电路共用一条电流路径。

definition_zh: 移动；改变；转移；轮班；换挡；Shift 键；转变；宽松内衣
definition_en: to move or change something from one position, state or owner to another; also a period of work or a change itself
core_image: 把箱子从左边搬到右边：东西没变，位置变了
scene: 护士站的白板上写着早班、中班、夜班三行。护士长说：You are on the night shift tonight.
sceneCN: 这里 shift 是「轮班」（第 3 个义项：一段工作时间）；句意：你今晚值夜班。图中可辨识物件：排班白板、时钟、护士帽、值班表。

pos.zh: 移动；改变；转移；换挡
转变；轮班；换挡装置；Shift 键

senses.title: To move something to another place
senses.definition: to move something from one position or place to another
senses.definitionCN: 把某物从一个位置或地方移到另一个
senses.example: Shift the table closer to the window.
senses.exampleCN: 把桌子移得离窗户近一点。
senses.why: Old English sciftan meant 'arrange, place, put in order'. Rearranging is already a kind of moving, and the modern sense keeps the physical displacement.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 sciftan 意为“安排、放置、整理”。重新安排本身就是一种移动，现代义保留了这种物理位移。

senses.title: To change focus or opinion
senses.definition: to change the subject, emphasis or direction of attention
senses.definitionCN: 改变主题、重点或注意力的方向
senses.example: The debate shifted to the cost of housing.
senses.exampleCN: 辩论转向了住房成本问题。
senses.why: Attention can be moved the way an object is moved. What changes is not the topic itself but where the collective gaze is placed.
senses.whyCN: 注意力可以像物体一样被移动。改变的不是话题本身，而是众人的目光落在哪里。

senses.title: A period of work
senses.definition: a fixed period during which one group of workers works, followed by another group
senses.definitionCN: 一组工人工作的固定时段，随后由另一组接替
senses.example: She works the night shift at the hospital.
senses.exampleCN: 她在医院上夜班。
senses.why: Workers are arranged in relays, one group replacing another. The meaning is recorded from 1809 in mining, where crews literally changed places at the seam.
senses.whyCN: 工人被排成接力班次，一组替换另一组。该义 1809 年见于矿业，矿工在矿层处真正换位。

senses.title: A gear change
senses.definition: the lever or mechanism that changes the gear of a vehicle, or the act of changing gear
senses.definitionCN: 改变车辆挡位的杆或机构，或换挡的动作
senses.example: He shifted into third gear on the hill.
senses.exampleCN: 他在上坡时换到了三挡。
senses.why: A gearbox arranges ratios in order; shifting moves the engine from one ratio to the next. The mechanical sense (1910) is arrangement made visible.
senses.whyCN: 变速箱把各种传动比排成序列；换挡就是把发动机从一个比位移到下一个。这一机械义（1910）是“安排”的可见化。

senses.title: The keyboard shift key
senses.definition: the key that temporarily changes the character produced by another key, usually to a capital letter
senses.definitionCN: 临时改变另一键所产生字符（通常转为大写）的按键
senses.example: Hold shift to type a capital letter.
senses.exampleCN: 按住 Shift 键输入大写字母。
senses.why: The typewriter's shift key (1893) physically moved the type basket so a different set of characters sat under the typebar. It shifted a mechanism, hence the name.
senses.whyCN: 打字机的 shift 键（1893）会物理移动字模篮，让另一组字符来到打字杆下。它移动的是机构，因此得名。

senses.title: To transfer blame or cost
senses.definition: to move responsibility, blame or cost from one person or group to another
senses.definitionCN: 把责任、责备或成本从一个人或群体转移到另一个
senses.example: The company shifted the cost onto customers.
senses.exampleCN: 公司把成本转嫁给了顾客。
senses.why: An abstract burden is treated as a physical load: it can be picked up from one shoulder and placed on another. Transfer is displacement without change of content.
senses.whyCN: 抽象的负担被当作实物重量：可以从一个肩膀拿起，放到另一个肩膀。转移就是内容不变的位置移动。

senses.title: To manage by oneself
senses.definition: in older English, to manage or cope without help, as in shift for oneself
senses.definitionCN: 在早期英语中，指无人帮助而自己应付，如 shift for oneself
senses.example: Out here you must shift for yourself.
senses.exampleCN: 在这种地方，你得自己想办法。
senses.why: The Middle English sense 'take care of oneself, make out a livelihood' survives in this phrase. To shift is to rearrange your resources until they work.
senses.whyCN: 中古英语义“照顾自己、谋生”保留在这个短语里。to shift 就是不断重新安排手头资源，直到能用。

senses.title: A loose undergarment
senses.definition: a woman's loose undergarment or chemise, used from the 1590s and now historical
senses.definitionCN: 一种宽松的女式内衣或衬衣，16 世纪 90 年代起使用，今为历史词
senses.example: The costume includes a linen shift.
senses.exampleCN: 这套服装包括一件亚麻内衬衣。
senses.why: The garment sense came from 'a change of clothes': a shift was the item you changed into next to the skin. The name remembers the change, not the cloth.
senses.whyCN: 衣物义来自“换衣服”：shift 是贴身穿换的那一件。名字记住的是“更换”，而不是布料。

senses.title: A change or turn
senses.definition: a change in state, direction or tendency, especially a noticeable one
senses.definitionCN: 状态、方向或趋势上的改变，尤指明显的改变
senses.example: There has been a shift in public opinion.
senses.exampleCN: 公众舆论出现了转变。
senses.why: The noun sense 'change, alteration' is recorded from the 1560s. A shift is what happens when the moved thing stays moved: the new position becomes the new state.
senses.whyCN: 名词“改变、变更”义自 16 世纪 60 年代有记录。shift 就是被移动的东西留在新位置后发生的事：新位置变成了新状态。

intro.en: Shift is a native Germanic word. Its oldest English sense is 'arrange, divide, distribute', and the modern ideas of moving, changing and working in relays all come from rearranging people or things.
intro.cn: shift 是本族日耳曼词。它最早的英语义是“安排、划分、分配”，现代的移动、改变与轮班等义都来自对人或物的重新安排。

items.en: The deeper Indo-European source is not established. The Germanic verb is connected to the source of Old English sceadan 'divide, separate' (modern shed), but the reconstruction is marked as uncertain.
items.cn: 更深的印欧来源尚未确立。该日耳曼动词被认为与古英语 sceadan“分开、分离”（现代 shed）的来源有关，但这一重构被标为不确定。

items.en: The verb *skiftan meant 'to divide, arrange, distribute'. It produced Old Norse skipta, Dutch schiften, German schichten 'to classify' and Schicht 'a layer, a shift'.
items.cn: 动词 *skiftan 意为“划分、安排、分配”。它产生古诺尔斯语 skipta、荷兰语 schiften、德语 schichten“分类”与 Schicht“层、班次”。

items.en: Old English sciftan meant 'arrange, place, put in order', also 'divide, separate, partition; distribute, allot, share'. The dividing and the arranging were one act.
items.cn: 古英语 sciftan 意为“安排、放置、整理”，也指“划分、分开、分隔；分配、分派、共享”。划分与安排在当时是同一个动作。

items.en: By c. 1200 shift meant 'dispose, make ready, set in order, control', and also 'take care of oneself'. By mid-13c. it meant 'alter, change'; by c. 1300 'go, move, depart', and also 'change one's clothes'.
items.cn: 约 1200 年，shift 意为“处置、备好、整理、控制”，也指“照顾自己”。到 13 世纪中期意为“改变、变更”；到 1300 年前后意为“走、移动、离开”，也指“换衣服”。

items.en: The noun begins c. 1300 as 'a movement, a beginning'; by mid-15c. 'an attempt, expedient'; by the 1560s 'a change'. The work-period sense is recorded from 1809, originally in mining, perhaps from an older 'relay of horses' (1708).
items.cn: 名词约 1300 年出现，意为“移动、开端”；到 15 世纪中期指“尝试、权宜手段”；到 16 世纪 60 年代指“改变”。工作时段义自 1809 年有记录，最初用于矿业，可能来自更早的“换马接力”（1708）。

items.en: The typewriter shift key is named by 1893, the gearshift by 1910 (noun 1914), and 'shift gears' in the figurative sense by 1961. The undergarment sense dates from the 1590s.
items.cn: 打字机 Shift 键于 1893 年得名，换挡机构于 1910 年（名词 1914），比喻义的 shift gears 于 1961 年。内衣义始于 16 世纪 90 年代。

note.en: The look-alike group is mostly other English words in shift- or -ift. The near-meaning group compares verbs of movement and change.
note.cn: 形近组多为 shift- 或 -ift 的其他英语词。近义组比较表示移动与改变的动词。

entries.definition: a long narrow passage or a rotating rod. It is unrelated to shift and comes from a different Germanic root.
entries.definitionCN: 狭长的通道或旋转的轴。它与 shift 无关，出自另一个日耳曼词根。

entries.definition: to sieve or separate fine particles. It shares the idea of separating but is a different word with a different root.
entries.definitionCN: 筛分；把细颗粒分开。它共享“分离”的概念，但词根不同，是另一个词。

entries.definition: lacking resourcefulness or ambition. It is shift + -less, literally 'having no shifts or expedients'.
entries.definitionCN: 懒惰、无进取心的。它是 shift + -less，字面是“没有招数、没有权宜手段”。

entries.definition: to change place or position. It is the broadest word and carries no idea of arrangement.
entries.definitionCN: 改变地方或位置。它是最宽泛的词，不含“安排”的意思。

entries.definition: to make or become different. It covers state as well as position, while shift often implies a move from one slot to another.
entries.definitionCN: 使或变得不同。它涵盖状态与位置，而 shift 常暗示从一个位置移到另一个。

entries.definition: to move something from one person, place or account to another. It is more formal than shift and often institutional.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物从一人、一地或一账户移到另一处。它比 shift 正式，常用于机构语境。

entries.definition: to change something in part without replacing it. It stresses modification rather than relocation.
entries.definitionCN: 部分地改变某物而不替换它。它强调修改，而不是位置移动。

normalIntro.en: Pictures: moving a box, a relay of nurses, a gear lever, a typewriter key. Each picture holds a cluster of senses.
normalIntro.cn: 画面：搬箱子、护士接力、换挡杆、打字机按键。每幅画托住一组义项。

normal.en: Lift the box from left to right: the box is the same, only its slot has shifted.
normal.cn: 把箱子从左搬到右：箱子没变，只是它的位置 shift 了。

normal.en: Three shifts of nurses replace one another at the desk: a shift is a relay of people.
normal.cn: 三班护士在护士站彼此替换：一个 shift 就是一轮人。

normal.en: Push the gear lever from second to third: you have shifted the gearbox's arrangement.
normal.cn: 把挡杆从二挡推到三挡：你改变了变速箱的排列。

normal.en: The typewriter's shift key physically moves the type basket: the key is named for the movement.
normal.cn: 打字机的 Shift 键会物理移动字模篮：这个键因移动而得名。

normal.en: Blame is a load you can pick up and put on someone else: that is shifting it.
normal.cn: 责任是一件可以拿起、放到别人身上的重物：这就是 shift 它。

abstract.en: One schema: DIVIDE → ARRANGE → CHANGE → MOVE → TRANSFER → RELAY.
abstract.cn: 一个图式：划分 → 安排 → 改变 → 移动 → 转移 → 接力。

abstract.en: Noun and verb pair up: to shift (move) produces a shift (a change); to work a shift is to take one turn in a relay.
abstract.cn: 名动配对：to shift（移动）产生 a shift（改变）；to work a shift 是在接力中值一轮。

abstract.en: Contrast: move is neutral; shift implies a slot or arrangement; transfer is formal hand-off; alter is partial modification.
abstract.cn: 对照：move 中性；shift 暗示位置或安排；transfer 是正式交接；alter 是部分修改。

examples.en: The wind shifted to the north just before the storm.
examples.cn: 暴风雨来临前，风向转到了北。

examples.en: The factory runs three shifts a day.
examples.cn: 这家工厂每天三班倒。

examples.en: Public attention has shifted away from the scandal.
examples.cn: 公众的注意力已经从这桩丑闻移开了。

dict_mnemonic.text: “谁福特”——谁（把）福（特）搬走？位置一换 → shift 移动、轮班

root: 源自原始日耳曼语 *skiftan“划分、安排、分配”，经古英语 sciftan“整理、划分”进入现代英语；更深印欧来源未确立。核心是“重新安排位置”。

sensesIntro.en: Shift is rearrangement. Move a box, move your attention, move a gear, move a typewriter's type basket, move blame onto someone else, or move yourself into a work relay: each is a displacement of something from one slot to another. The noun then names the displacement itself, the relay period, and the changed state that remains after the move.
sensesIntro.cn: shift 就是重新安排。搬箱子、移注意力、换挡、移动打字机字模篮、把责任推到别人身上、把自己排进一轮班次，都是把某物从一个位置移到另一个。名词则指这次位移本身、接力的一段时间，以及移动后留下的新状态。

core.en: Rearranging: something keeps its identity but changes its slot, state or owner.
core.cn: 重新安排：某物保持自身，却改变了位置、状态或归属。

branches.en: DISPLACEMENT: moving an object, and moving attention or emphasis.
branches.cn: 位移：移动物体，以及移动注意力或重点。

branches.en: THE RESULTING CHANGE: the noun for an alteration that stays in place.
branches.cn: 由此产生的改变：指留在新位置上的变更。

branches.en: RELAYS AND MECHANISMS: work shifts, gear shifts and the typewriter's shift key.
branches.cn: 接力与机构：工作班次、换挡，以及打字机的 Shift 键。

branches.en: BURDENS AND SELF-RELIANCE: transferring blame or cost, and shifting for oneself.
branches.cn: 负担与自立：转移责任或成本，以及自己设法应付。

branches.en: THE GARMENT: a change of clothes, now a historical sense.
branches.cn: 衣物：一次换衣，今为历史义。

intro.en: Shift is a native root with English suffixes and compounds. The items below keep the 'rearrange' idea visible.
intro.cn: shift 是本族词根，搭配英语后缀与复合形式。下列条目让“重新安排”这一概念保持可见。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin source for shift. The Latin words below are semantic parallels, listed for contrast, not for etymology.
latinIntro.cn: shift 没有拉丁来源。下面的拉丁词是语义对照，只为比较而列，不构成词源。

items.meaning: to move or change; a change; a work period
items.example: They shift the boxes every morning.
items.exampleCN: 他们每天早上搬箱子。

items.meaning: moving or changing; the act of moving
items.meaningCN: 移动的、变化的；移动行为
items.example: Shifting sands bury the road each year.
items.exampleCN: 流沙每年埋住这条路。

items.example: He gave a shifty answer.
items.exampleCN: 他回答得躲躲闪闪。

items.example: They called him shiftless and lazy.
items.exampleCN: 他们说他懒惰无能。

items.meaning: one who shifts; a gear lever
items.example: The shifter stuck in second gear.
items.exampleCN: 换挡杆卡在二挡。

items.example: He has worked the night shift for years.
items.exampleCN: 他上夜班已经多年。

items.meaning: a system of working in relays
items.example: Shift work can disturb sleep.
items.exampleCN: 轮班工作会扰乱睡眠。

items.meaningCN: 临时替代品；凑合的办法
items.example: They built a makeshift bridge.
items.exampleCN: 他们搭了一座临时桥。

items.meaning: a lever or mechanism for changing gears
items.example: The gearshift is on the floor.
items.exampleCN: 换挡杆在地板上。

items.meaning: the key that changes character case
items.meaningCN: Shift 键（切换字符大小写）
items.example: Press shift key and the letter becomes capital.
items.exampleCN: 按 Shift 键，字母变成大写。

definition_zh: 有意义的；重要的；显著的；意味深长的；有效数字的；统计显著的
definition_en: carrying meaning, or large or important enough to be noticed and to matter
core_image: 一个记号被刻在石头上：它不只是痕迹，还指着某件事
scene: 统计课上，教授指着两组数据说：The difference is small but statistically significant.
sceneCN: 这里 significant 是「统计上显著的」（第 3 个义项：差异大到不太可能由偶然造成）；句意：差异虽小，但统计上显著。图中可辨识物件：散点图、p 值、置信区间、投影仪。

pos.zh: 有意义的；重要的；显著的；意味深长的

forms.label: 比较级（更多用 more 构成）
最高级（更多用 most 构成）

derivatives.zh: 有表示作用的；示意性的

senses.title: Carrying meaning
senses.definition: having a meaning, especially one that can be understood or interpreted
senses.definitionCN: 具有意义，尤指可被理解或解释的意义
senses.example: Every word in the code is significant.
senses.exampleCN: 代码中的每个词都有意义。
senses.why: Significare is signum 'sign' + facere 'make'. Something significant makes a sign: it points beyond itself to a meaning.
senses.whyCN: significare 是 signum“记号”加 facere“做”。significant 的东西会“做出记号”：它指向自身之外的意义。

senses.title: Important enough to matter
senses.definition: large or important enough to have an effect or to deserve attention
senses.definitionCN: 足够大或足够重要，能产生影响或值得关注
senses.example: The new policy marks a significant change in direction.
senses.exampleCN: 新政策标志着方向上的重大转变。
senses.why: A sign that points to a large consequence is itself large in importance. From 'full of meaning' the word moves to 'full of consequence'.
senses.whyCN: 一个指向重大后果的记号，本身也就分量很重。词义从“充满意义”滑向“充满后果”。

senses.title: Unlikely to be chance: statistical significance
senses.titleCN: 不太可能出于偶然：统计显著
senses.definition: in statistics, of a result, unlikely to have occurred by chance under the stated assumptions
senses.definitionCN: 在统计中，指结果在既定假设下不太可能由偶然产生
senses.example: The two groups differed significantly at the 5% level.
senses.exampleCN: 两组在 5% 水平上差异显著。
senses.why: A result is statistically significant when it carries information rather than noise. The word's 'meaning' becomes a technical test: does this difference mean something?
senses.whyCN: 当结果承载的是信息而不是噪声，它在统计上就是显著的。这里的“意义”变成一项技术检验：这个差异到底说明问题吗？

senses.title: Large enough to be noticed
senses.definition: of an amount, effect or number, large enough to be noticed or to matter in practice
senses.definitionCN: 指数量、效果或数字大到引人注意或在实践中起作用
senses.example: A significant number of readers cancelled their subscriptions.
senses.exampleCN: 有相当多的读者取消了订阅。
senses.why: A quantity becomes significant when it is big enough to be read as a message: the size itself tells you something about the situation.
senses.whyCN: 当数量大到可以被读成一条信息时，它就 significant：大小本身就在告诉你局势如何。

senses.title: Full of unspoken meaning
senses.definition: of a look, gesture or silence, expressing something more than is actually said
senses.definitionCN: 指目光、手势或沉默表达了言外之意
senses.example: She gave him a significant glance across the table.
senses.exampleCN: 她在桌子对面意味深长地看了他一眼。
senses.why: A glance that makes a sign is doing exactly what significare means: it indicates something without naming it.
senses.whyCN: 一个“做出记号”的眼神，正是在做 significare 的事：它指出某事，却不把它说出来。

senses.title: Significant figures: meaningful digits
senses.definition: in measurement, the digits of a number that carry reliable information about precision
senses.definitionCN: 测量中，一个数里承载可靠精度信息的数字
senses.example: Round the answer to three significant figures.
senses.exampleCN: 把答案保留三位有效数字。
senses.why: In a measured number only some digits carry meaning; the rest are zeros or placeholders. The significant digits are precisely the 'meaningful' ones.
senses.whyCN: 在测量数值中，只有部分数字承载意义，其余是零或占位符。significant figures 正是那些“有意义”的数字。

senses.title: Significant other: the person who matters
senses.definition: a person's spouse or romantic partner, named as the person of special importance in their life
senses.definitionCN: 某人的配偶或恋爱伴侣，被称作其生活中特别重要的人
senses.example: Employees may bring their significant other to the dinner.
senses.exampleCN: 员工可以带伴侣参加晚宴。
senses.why: The phrase keeps the 'important' sense and makes it social: the person is significant because their presence changes the meaning of the evening.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语保留了“重要”义，并把它社会化：这个人 significant，因为他的出现改变了这个夜晚的意义。

senses.title: Indicative of something
senses.definition: in formal usage, significant of something, serving as a sign that it exists or is true
senses.definitionCN: 正式用法中，significant of 某事物，指作为其存在或为真的标志
senses.example: The silence was significant of their disapproval.
senses.exampleCN: 那片沉默说明他们并不赞成。
senses.why: The preposition of names what the sign points to. The word returns to its root sense: a sign that makes another thing known.
senses.whyCN: 介词 of 引出记号所指的东西。这个词回到词根本义：一个让他物被知晓的记号。

senses.title: Signifying in language and semiotics
senses.titleCN: 语言学与符号学中的“表意”
senses.definition: in linguistics and semiotics, having a signifying function; carrying a signified meaning
senses.definitionCN: 在语言学与符号学中，具有表意功能；承载被表示的意义
senses.example: The study asks which features of the image are significant.
senses.exampleCN: 该研究追问图像中哪些特征是表意的。
senses.why: Semiotics splits the sign into signifier and signified. 'Significant' names the side that does the pointing, the mark that carries meaning rather than the meaning carried.
senses.whyCN: 符号学把符号分为能指与所指。significant 指做“指向”的那一侧，即承载意义的记号，而不是被承载的意义。

intro.en: Significant is built from Latin signum 'sign' and facere 'to make': it literally 'makes a sign'. The movement from 'meaning something' to 'important' is the story of the word.
intro.cn: significant 由拉丁语 signum“记号”与 facere“做”构成，字面就是“做出记号”。从“有意义”到“重要”，正是这个词的故事。

items.en: Signum meant 'a mark, token, sign, signal, standard'. Its deeper origin is uncertain, so the chain stops here rather than inventing a PIE root.
items.cn: signum 意为“记号、标记、标志、信号、军旗”。其更深来源不确定，因此词链到此为止，不编造原始印欧语词根。

items.en: Significare meant 'to make known, show by signs, indicate, mean'. It joined signum with the root of facere 'to make, do'.
items.cn: significare 意为“使知晓、用记号表示、指示、意味着”。它把 signum 与 facere“做、造”的词根结合起来。

items.en: The present participle significans 'making a sign, meaning' became the adjective. English took it as significant, so the word begins as 'that which signifies'.
items.cn: 现在分词 significans“做记号、表意的”变成了形容词。英语取作 significant，因此这个词最初就是“在表意的那个”。

items.en: Significant is recorded from the 1570s meaning 'having a meaning, expressive', first of words and signs rather than of events.
items.cn: significant 于 16 世纪 70 年代有记录，意为“有意义的、表达意义的”，最初用于词语与记号，而不是事件。

items.en: The sense 'of consequence, important' appears in the 18th century (c. 1747). A sign that points to a great consequence comes to be called great itself.
items.cn: “有后果的、重要的”义在 18 世纪出现（约 1747）。一个指向重大后果的记号，本身也就被称为重大。

items.en: Statistics adopted 'statistically significant' in the 20th century, and 'significant figures' comes from measurement. 'Significant other' is recorded in the 20th century as a social phrase.
items.cn: 统计学在 20 世纪采用 statistically significant，significant figures 来自测量学。significant other 作为社会用语也在 20 世纪出现。

note.en: The look-alike group is the sign- family; the near-meaning group compares words for importance and meaning. Watch the noun/adjective endings.
note.cn: 形近组是 sign- 词族；近义组比较表示重要与有意义的词。注意名词与形容词词尾。

entries.definition: the meaning or importance of something. It is the noun, while significant is the adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 某事物的意义或重要性。它是名词，而 significant 是形容词。

entries.definition: to be a sign of; to mean. It is the verb that names the act of making a sign.
entries.definitionCN: 是……的标志；表示。它是表示“做记号”这一动作的动词。

entries.definition: a mark, notice or gesture that conveys information. It is the noun inside significare.
entries.definitionCN: 传达信息的记号、告示或手势。它是 significare 内部的那个名词。

entries.definition: having great effect or value. It is the everyday word for significance as weight.
entries.definitionCN: 有重大影响或价值。它是表示“分量重”的日常词。

entries.definition: having a serious, useful or personal meaning. It stresses felt meaning rather than statistical or social weight.
entries.definitionCN: 具有严肃、有用或个人的意义。它强调被感受到的意义，而不是统计或社会分量。

entries.definition: large in amount or degree. It matches significant only in the 'large enough to notice' sense.
entries.definitionCN: 数量或程度上很大。它只在“大到值得注意”义上与 significant 对应。

entries.definition: deserving attention because of a special quality. It stresses being noticed rather than carrying meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 因特殊品质而值得注意。它强调被注意到，而不是承载意义。

normalIntro.en: Pictures: a carved sign, a raised eyebrow, a p-value on a screen, a number rounded to three digits.
normalIntro.cn: 画面：刻下的记号、扬起的眉毛、屏幕上的 p 值、保留三位的数字。

normal.en: Signum + facere: to be significant is to make a sign that points somewhere.
normal.cn: signum + facere：significant 就是做出一个指向某处的记号。

normal.en: A raised eyebrow across the table is a sign with no words: that is a significant glance.
normal.cn: 桌对面扬起眉毛，是一个不用词的记号：这就是 significant glance。

normal.en: A p-value says the difference is probably not noise: statistically significant.
normal.cn: p 值说明这个差异大概不是噪声：statistically significant。

normal.en: Only some digits in a measurement carry meaning; those are the significant figures.
normal.cn: 测量中只有部分数字承载意义；那些就是 significant figures。

normal.en: A significant other is the person whose presence changes the meaning of your day.
normal.cn: significant other 就是那个出现后会改变你一天意义的人。

abstract.en: One schema: SIGN → MEAN → EXPRESS → MATTER → MEASURE. Meaning first, importance second, technique third.
abstract.cn: 一个图式：记号 → 表意 → 表达 → 要紧 → 测量。先有意义，再有重要性，最后是技术化。

abstract.en: Word-family check: sign (noun) → signify (verb) → significant (adj.) → significance (noun) → significantly (adv.).
abstract.cn: 词族检查：sign（名）→ signify（动）→ significant（形）→ significance（名）→ significantly（副）。

abstract.en: Contrast: meaningful is felt meaning; important is weight; considerable is size; notable is visibility.
abstract.cn: 对照：meaningful 是被感受到的意义；important 是分量；considerable 是数量；notable 是显眼。

examples.en: There is a significant difference between the two treatments.
examples.cn: 两种疗法之间存在显著差异。

examples.en: She gave a significant nod, as if to say yes.
examples.cn: 她意味深长地点了点头，像是在说“好”。

examples.en: Report the result to two significant figures.
examples.cn: 把结果保留两位有效数字报告。

dict_mnemonic.text: “西哥尼菲肯特”——西（边）哥（哥）尼（尼）菲（非）肯（肯定）特（别重要）→ significant 重要的、有意义的

root: 源自拉丁语 significare“用记号表示、意味着”，由 signum“记号”加 facere“做”构成；现在分词 significans 进入英语。核心是“做出记号、指向意义”。

sensesIntro.en: Significant begins with a sign that makes meaning. A word or code has meaning; a glance carries unspoken meaning; a semiotic feature signifies. Then the word measures: an amount large enough to matter, an event important enough to change direction, a statistical result unlikely to be noise, a measured digit that carries precision. The social phrase significant other keeps the old idea that a person can change the meaning of a situation.
sensesIntro.cn: significant 的起点是一个“做出意义”的记号。词或代码有意义；一个眼神承载未说出的意义；符号学特征在表意。随后这个词开始度量：大到起作用的数量、重要到能改变方向的事件、不太可能是噪声的统计结果、承载精度的测量数字。social phrase significant other 则保留旧意：一个人的存在能改变局面的意义。

core.en: Making a sign: carrying or pointing to a meaning, and therefore mattering.
core.cn: 做出记号：承载或指向某种意义，因此也就有分量。

branches.en: MEANING: plain sense, unspoken implication, and the semiotic signifying function.
branches.cn: 意义：字面意义、未说出的含义，以及符号学上的表意功能。

branches.en: CONSEQUENCE: importance that changes direction, and size large enough to notice.
branches.cn: 后果：能改变方向的重要性，以及大到值得注意的规模。

branches.en: MEASUREMENT: statistical significance and significant figures, meaning made numerical.
branches.cn: 测量：统计显著性与有效数字，把“意义”变成数字。

branches.en: SOCIAL PHRASE: the significant other, a person whose presence carries weight.
branches.cn: 社会短语：significant other，其存在自带分量的人。

branches.en: INDICATION: significant of something, the sign pointing at what it reveals.
branches.cn: 指示：significant of 某物，记号指向它所揭示的东西。

intro.en: Significant belongs to the sign- family, built on signum plus facere. The items below trace the family from noun to adverb.
intro.cn: significant 属于 sign- 词族，建立在 signum 加 facere 之上。下列条目从名词追到副词。

latinIntro.en: Latin signum 'sign' and significare 'make a sign' are the two load-bearing forms. Significans is the participle that became the English adjective.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 signum“记号”与 significare“做记号”是两个承重形式。significans 是变成英语形容词的那个分词。

items.example: This is a significant moment for the team.
items.exampleCN: 这对团队来说是一个重要时刻。

items.example: Few saw the significance of the letter.
items.exampleCN: 很少有人看出这封信的意义。

items.meaning: to be a sign of; mean
items.example: A red light signifies danger.
items.exampleCN: 红灯表示危险。

items.example: There was no sign of rain.
items.exampleCN: 没有下雨的迹象。

items.meaning: a sign that conveys a message
items.example: The radio signal was weak.
items.exampleCN: 无线电信号很弱。

items.meaning: a person's name written as a mark
items.example: The contract needs your signature.
items.exampleCN: 合同需要你的签名。

items.example: Sales improved significantly.
items.exampleCN: 销售额显著提高。

items.example: The error was insignificant.
items.exampleCN: 这个误差微不足道。

items.example: The word's signification changed over time.
items.exampleCN: 这个词的意义随时间改变。

items.meaningCN: 有表示作用的；示意性的
items.example: The gesture was significative of consent.
items.exampleCN: 这个手势表示同意。

definition_zh: 相似的；类似的；同类的；[几何]相似的
definition_en: alike in appearance, nature or amount, without being exactly the same
core_image: 两张大小不同的地图叠在一起：轮廓一模一样，只是尺寸变了
scene: 几何课上，老师把两个三角形叠在黑板上：These two triangles are similar, but not congruent.
sceneCN: 这里 similar 是「几何上相似的」（第 2 个义项：形状相同、大小可以不同，对应角相等、对应边成比例）；句意：这两个三角形相似，但不全等。图中可辨识物件：两个三角形、量角器、比例标注、黑板。

pos.zh: 相似的；类似的；同类的
[几何] 相似的（形状相同、大小可不同）

forms.label: 比较级（更多用 more 构成）
最高级（更多用 most 构成）

senses.title: Like, but not the same
senses.definition: alike in appearance, sound or nature, while remaining two distinct things
senses.definitionCN: 在外观、声音或性质上相像，但仍然是两个不同的事物
senses.example: The two sisters have similar voices.
senses.exampleCN: 这两个姐妹嗓音相似。
senses.why: Latin similis means 'like, resembling'. The word marks likeness that stops short of identity: the two things are put side by side and their outlines match, but they do not merge.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 similis 意为“相像的”。这个词标记的相似止步于“同一”：两样东西被并排放在一起，轮廓对得上，但并没有合并成一个。

senses.title: Same shape, different size: geometry
senses.titleCN: 形状相同、大小不同：几何相似
senses.definition: of geometric figures, having the same shape with corresponding angles equal and corresponding sides in proportion
senses.definitionCN: 指几何图形形状相同，对应角相等、对应边成比例
senses.example: These two triangles are similar, but not congruent.
senses.exampleCN: 这两个三角形相似，但不全等。
senses.why: In geometry the everyday likeness is made exact: angles are copied, sides are scaled. Similarity is likeness with a fixed ratio, so the shape survives while the size changes.
senses.whyCN: 在几何中，日常的“像”被精确化：角被复制，边按比例缩放。相似就是带固定比例的相像，所以形状保留下来，而大小可以改变。

senses.title: Of the same kind or nature
senses.definition: belonging to the same category or sharing the same basic nature
senses.definitionCN: 属于同一类别，或具有相同的基本性质
senses.example: The two countries face similar problems.
senses.exampleCN: 这两个国家面临类似的问题。
senses.why: Likeness can sit in the kind rather than in the individual: two problems are similar because they belong to one family of problems, not because they are the same problem.
senses.whyCN: 相似可以落在“类别”上而不是“个体”上：两个问题之所以相似，是因为它们属于同一类问题，而不是因为它们是同一个问题。

senses.title: Nearly the same in amount
senses.definition: of numbers, ages, prices or levels, close to one another without being equal
senses.definitionCN: 指数字、年龄、价格或水平彼此接近，但并不相等
senses.example: The two cities have similar populations.
senses.exampleCN: 这两座城市人口相近。
senses.why: The same outline can be read on a scale: two values are similar when they sit close together on the axis, near enough to be compared but not identical.
senses.whyCN: 同一条轮廓也可以放在刻度上读：两个数值在数轴上靠得很近时就是 similar，近到可以比较，但并非完全相同。

senses.title: Similar to: the comparison frame
senses.definition: used with 'to' to name the second thing that the first is being measured against
senses.definitionCN: 与 to 连用，引出用来衡量第一个事物的参照物
senses.example: Her response was similar to mine.
senses.exampleCN: 她的回答和我的相似。
senses.why: The preposition to points at the reference object. Similarity is not a property held alone; it needs a second term standing beside the first, and 'to' supplies that second term.
senses.whyCN: 介词 to 指向参照物。相似不是孤立拥有的属性，它需要有第二个项站在第一个项旁边，而 to 提供的正是这第二个项。

senses.title: Similar forms in language
senses.definition: of words, sounds or structures, nearly identical in form but distinct in meaning or origin
senses.definitionCN: 指词语、语音或结构形式接近，但意义或来源不同
senses.example: Learners often confuse similar-sounding words.
senses.exampleCN: 学习者常常混淆发音相似的词。
senses.why: Here the likeness is purely formal: the shapes echo each other while the meanings diverge. This is the sense that produces warnings about 'similar-looking words' in dictionaries.
senses.whyCN: 这里的相似纯粹是形式上的：外形彼此呼应，而意义分道扬镳。词典里“形近词”的提醒，就是从这个义项来的。

senses.title: Comparable conditions in science
senses.definition: of experimental conditions or structures, close enough to allow a controlled comparison
senses.definitionCN: 指实验条件或结构足够接近，可以进行受控比较
senses.example: The reaction was tested under similar conditions.
senses.exampleCN: 该反应在类似条件下进行了测试。
senses.why: A scientist needs two setups that differ only in the variable under study. 'Similar conditions' means the likeness has been made precise enough that the remaining difference can be trusted.
senses.whyCN: 科学家需要两个装置只在被研究的变量上不同。“类似条件”意味着相似已被精确到足以让人信任剩下的那点差异。

senses.title: Measured likeness: similarity
senses.definition: the derived noun similarity names how much two things resemble each other, often expressed as a score or index
senses.definitionCN: 派生名词 similarity 指两事物相像的程度，常以分数或指数表示
senses.example: The software calculates the similarity between the two texts.
senses.exampleCN: 该软件计算两段文本之间的相似度。
senses.why: Once likeness can be scored, it becomes a quantity. The noun turns 'they look alike' into 'they are 87% alike', moving the word from perception to measurement.
senses.whyCN: 一旦相像可以被打分，它就变成一种量。名词把“它们看起来像”变成“它们相似度 87%”，词义从知觉走向测量。

senses.title: Similarly: parallel reasoning
senses.definition: the adverb similarly introduces a second case that follows the same pattern as the first
senses.definitionCN: 副词 similarly 引出与前一例遵循同一模式的第二个例子
senses.example: Similarly, the second group improved after training.
senses.exampleCN: 同样地，第二组在训练后也有所提高。
senses.why: The -ly suffix turns likeness into a way of proceeding. In an argument, two cases are laid side by side and the same step is applied to both: that is arguing similarly.
senses.whyCN: -ly 后缀把“相像”变成一种推进方式。在论证中，两个案例被并排放置，同一个步骤被施加于两者：这就是 similarly 地论证。

intro.en: Similar goes back to Latin similis 'like, resembling', whose older relative semol meant 'together, at the same time'. French passed the learned form similaire to English, where similar is recorded from the 1610s.
intro.cn: similar 追溯到拉丁语 similis“相像的”，它的更早亲属 semol 意为“一起、同时”。法语把学术形式 similaire 传给英语，similar 在 17 世纪 10 年代见于记录。

items.en: Similis was a third-declension adjective meaning 'like, resembling, of the same kind'. It could describe people, things and appearances, and it took the dative: similis patri, 'like his father'.
items.cn: similis 是第三变格法形容词，意为“相像的、类似的、同类的”。它可以形容人、物和外观，并支配与格：similis patri，“像他父亲”。

items.en: The older form semol meant 'together, at the same time', from PIE *sem- 'one, together'. The same root underlies Latin semel 'once' and simul 'at the same time', and is cognate with English same.
items.cn: 更早的形式 semol 意为“一起、同时”，来自原始印欧语 *sem-“一、一起”。同一词根也支撑拉丁语 semel“一次”和 simul“同时”，并与英语 same 同源。

items.en: Old and Middle French took the Latin adjective as a learned borrowing, similaire. English acquired the word through this French channel rather than directly from Latin.
items.cn: 古法语和中古法语把这一拉丁形容词作为学术借词吸收进来，作 similaire。英语是通过这条法语渠道而不是直接从拉丁语获得这个词的。

items.en: The earlier form similary is recorded in the 1560s; the modern spelling similar appears in the 1610s. Both kept the Latin sense 'like, of the same kind'.
items.cn: 较早的形式 similary 见于 16 世纪 60 年代；现代拼写 similar 出现于 17 世纪 10 年代。两者都保留拉丁语“相像的、同类的”之义。

items.en: Geometry gave the word its exact technical sense: similar figures have equal angles and proportional sides. Logic and rhetoric extended it to similar cases and similar arguments.
items.cn: 几何学赋予这个词精确的技术义：相似图形对应角相等、对应边成比例。逻辑学与修辞学又把它扩展到相似案例与相似论证。

items.en: Modern usage adds measured likeness (similarity index, similarity score), statistical use (similar distributions) and the discourse adverb similarly. The core idea stays 'like, but not the same'.
items.cn: 现代用法增加了可度量的相似（similarity index、similarity score）、统计学用法（similar distributions）以及语篇副词 similarly。核心观念始终是“像，但不是同一个”。

note.en: The look-alike group is the simil- family; the near-meaning group compares words for likeness. Watch the difference between a state (similar) and an act (simulate).
note.cn: 形近组是 simil- 词族；近义组比较表示“相像”的词。注意状态（similar）与动作（simulate）的区别。

entries.definition: the state or degree of being similar. It is the noun built on similar.
entries.definitionCN: 相似的状态或程度。它是建立在 similar 之上的名词。

entries.definition: a figure of speech that compares two things using 'like' or 'as'. It comes from the neuter of similis.
entries.definitionCN: 用 like 或 as 比较两事物的修辞手法。它来自 similis 的中性形式。

entries.definition: to imitate the appearance or conditions of something. It is an action, not a state.
entries.definitionCN: 模仿某物的外观或条件。它是动作，不是状态。

entries.definition: looking or being the same in some way. It is more general and often predicative: they look alike.
entries.definitionCN: 在某方面看起来或实际上是相同的。它更宽泛，常作表语：they look alike。

entries.definition: similar enough to be measured or judged against each other. It stresses the act of comparison.
entries.definitionCN: 相似到足以相互衡量或评判。它强调比较这一动作。

entries.definition: similar in structure or function though not in origin. It is used for parallels across different systems.
entries.definitionCN: 结构或功能上相似，但来源不同。它用于跨不同系统的对应关系。

entries.definition: similar by nature or origin, as if belonging to the same family. It stresses shared descent.
entries.definitionCN: 性质或来源上相似，仿佛同属一族。它强调共同来源。

normalIntro.en: Pictures: two maps of different sizes, two triangles on a board, two sisters' voices, two values close on an axis.
normalIntro.cn: 画面：两张大小不同的地图、黑板上的两个三角形、两个姐妹的嗓音、数轴上靠近的两个值。

normal.en: Similis means 'like': put two things side by side, and if the outlines match without merging, they are similar.
normal.cn: similis 就是“像”：把两样东西并排放，轮廓对得上却又没有合并，它们就是 similar。

normal.en: In geometry, similar figures keep the shape and change the size; congruent figures keep both.
normal.cn: 几何里，相似图形保留形状、改变大小；全等图形则两者都保留。

normal.en: The fixed phrase is similar to, not similar with: 'to' points at the thing you are comparing against.
normal.cn: 固定搭配是 similar to，不是 similar with：to 指向你拿来比较的那个参照物。

normal.en: Similarly introduces a parallel case: first this group improved, similarly the second group improved.
normal.cn: similarly 引出并列的第二个案例：第一组进步了，同样地第二组也进步了。

normal.en: Do not mix similar (a state of likeness) with simulate (the act of imitating or pretending).
normal.cn: 不要把 similar（相像的状态）和 simulate（模仿或假装的动作）混在一起。

abstract.en: One schema: LIKE → SAME SHAPE → SAME KIND → SAME DEGREE → COMPARISON → PARALLEL CASE.
abstract.cn: 一个图式：像 → 同形 → 同类 → 同程度 → 比较 → 并列案例。

abstract.en: Word-family check: similis (Latin) → similar (adj.) → similarity (n.) → similarly (adv.); opposite dissimilar.
abstract.cn: 词族检查：similis（拉丁）→ similar（形）→ similarity（名）→ similarly（副）；反义 dissimilar。

abstract.en: Contrast: alike is everyday, comparable stresses measurement, analogous stresses structural parallel, akin stresses shared origin.
abstract.cn: 对照：alike 最日常，comparable 强调可测量，analogous 强调结构对应，akin 强调共同来源。

examples.en: The two paintings are similar in style but not in subject.
examples.cn: 这两幅画风格相似，但题材不同。

examples.en: Her response was similar to mine.
examples.cn: 她的回答和我的相似。

examples.en: The two countries face similar problems.
examples.cn: 这两个国家面临类似的问题。

dict_mnemonic.text: “西米勒”——西（瓜）米（粒）勒（在一起）→ 摆在一起看着都像 → similar 相似的

root: 源自拉丁语 similis“相像的”，更早与古拉丁语 semol“一起”同源，可追溯到原始印欧语 *sem-“一、一起”；经法语 similaire 于 17 世纪进入英语。核心是“彼此相像、可以并排比较”。

sensesIntro.en: Similar begins with plain likeness: two things whose outlines match without being one. Geometry makes that likeness exact, with equal angles and proportional sides. From there the word spreads along two lines: likeness of kind, and likeness of degree. It also supplies the frame 'similar to', the measured noun similarity, and the discourse adverb similarly, which lays two cases side by side in an argument.
sensesIntro.cn: similar 的起点是朴素的相似：两样东西轮廓对得上，却并不是同一个。几何学把这种相似精确化，要求对应角相等、对应边成比例。从这里词义沿两条线展开：类别上的相似，与程度上的接近。它还提供比较框架 similar to、可度量的名词 similarity，以及在论证中把两个案例并排放置的语篇副词 similarly。

core.en: Like, but not the same: shape, kind and degree that can be set side by side.
core.cn: 像，但不相同：形状、类别与程度可以被并排比较。

branches.en: RESEMBLANCE: everyday likeness, and values that sit close on a scale.
branches.cn: 相像：日常的相似，以及刻度上彼此接近的数值。

branches.en: STRUCTURE: geometric similarity and comparable scientific conditions.
branches.cn: 结构：几何相似，以及可比的科学条件。

branches.en: KIND AND FORM: the same category of thing, and similar-looking language forms.
branches.cn: 类别与形式：同一类别的事物，以及外形相近的语言形式。

branches.en: COMPARISON: the 'similar to' frame, and similarity as a measured score.
branches.cn: 比较：similar to 框架，以及作为可度量分数的相似度。

branches.en: PARALLEL REASONING: similarly, applying one pattern to a second case.
branches.cn: 并列推理：similarly，把同一模式套用到第二个案例。

intro.en: Similar belongs to the simil- family, built on Latin similis 'like'. The items below follow the family from the root adjective to verbs and abstract nouns.
intro.cn: similar 属于 simil- 词族，建立在拉丁语 similis“像”之上。下列条目从词根形容词一路追到动词与抽象名词。

latinIntro.en: Latin similis 'like' and its older relative semol 'together' carry the core idea. Simile is the neuter of similis turned into a noun, and similitudo supplies the abstract noun.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 similis“像”及其更早的亲属 semol“一起”承载核心观念。simile 是 similis 的中性形式名词化，similitudo 则提供抽象名词。

items.example: The two designs are similar.
items.exampleCN: 这两个设计很相似。

items.meaning: the state or degree of being alike
items.example: There is a strong similarity between the two cases.
items.exampleCN: 这两个案例之间有很强的相似性。

items.example: The second group improved similarly.
items.exampleCN: 第二组也同样有所提高。

items.example: The two samples are chemically dissimilar.
items.exampleCN: 这两个样品在化学上并不相似。

items.example: The study lists three dissimilarities.
items.exampleCN: 这项研究列出了三处不同。

items.meaning: a comparison using like or as
items.meaningCN: 明喻（用 like 或 as 的比较）
items.example: 'Her smile was like sunlight' is a simile.
items.exampleCN: “她的微笑像阳光”是一个明喻。

items.meaning: likeness; an image or likeness of something
items.example: The poem speaks in similitudes.
items.exampleCN: 这首诗以比喻的方式言说。

items.meaning: to make alike; to absorb into a group
items.example: Newcomers gradually assimilate into the community.
items.exampleCN: 新来者逐渐融入社区。

items.example: The program simulates ocean currents.
items.exampleCN: 该程序模拟洋流。

items.meaning: appearing to be true or real
items.example: The detail makes the story verisimilar.
items.exampleCN: 这个细节让故事显得逼真。

latinEntries.structure: Old Latin adverb, from PIE *sem- 'one, together'
neuter of similis, used as a noun

definition_en: to imitate the appearance or conditions of something, sometimes in order to deceive
core_image: 飞行模拟舱里，仪表和真飞机一样转动，但窗外只是一块屏幕
scene: 飞行训练中心，学员在模拟舱里练习迫降。教官说：The simulator can simulate an engine failure at 30,000 feet.
sceneCN: 这里 simulate 是「模拟、仿真」（第 2、4 个义项：用模型重现真实条件）；句意：模拟器可以模拟三万英尺高空的发动机失效。图中可辨识物件：模拟舱、仪表盘、球形屏幕、教员座椅。

pos.zh: 模拟；仿真；模仿
假装；装作

senses.title: To pretend: putting on a false front
senses.titleCN: 假装：摆出不真实的样子
senses.definition: to pretend to have a feeling, illness or quality that one does not really have
senses.definitionCN: 假装拥有某种实际并不存在的情感、疾病或品质
senses.example: He simulated illness to avoid the exam.
senses.exampleCN: 他装病以逃避考试。
senses.why: Latin simulare could mean both 'to make like' and 'to feign'. The second sense survives: the outer surface is copied, while the inner state is missing. Simulation is a likeness with no substance behind it.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 simulare 既可表示“使相像”，也可表示“假装”。第二个义项活了下来：外层表面被复制，而内在状态缺席。假装是一种背后没有实质的相似。

senses.title: To reproduce real conditions
senses.definition: to create conditions that copy the important features of a real situation, usually for study or training
senses.definitionCN: 创造复制了真实情境重要特征的条件，通常用于研究或训练
senses.example: The chamber simulates the pressure at high altitude.
senses.exampleCN: 这个舱室模拟高海拔的气压。
senses.why: Here the copy is honest: the aim is not to deceive but to reproduce. Engineers keep the variables that matter and drop the rest, so the model can be tested safely.
senses.whyCN: 这里的复制是诚实的：目的不是欺骗，而是重现。工程师保留真正重要的变量，舍弃其余部分，从而能安全地测试模型。

senses.title: To imitate an appearance or sound
senses.definition: to copy the look, sound or manner of something so that it resembles the original
senses.definitionCN: 复制某物的外观、声音或举止，使其像原物
senses.example: The actor simulated the old man's walk.
senses.exampleCN: 演员模仿了那位老人的步态。
senses.why: The Latin verb was used for making a copy of a thing. In this sense the imitation is visible and often skilful, and the question of deceit does not arise.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁动词本就用于“给某物做一个复本”。在这个义项里，模仿是可见的、常常很技巧性，是否欺骗的问题并不出现。

senses.title: Computer simulation
senses.definition: to run a model on a computer so that it reproduces the behaviour of a real system
senses.definitionCN: 在计算机上运行模型，使其重现真实系统的行为
senses.example: The program simulates how heat spreads through the wall.
senses.exampleCN: 该程序模拟热量如何在墙体中传导。
senses.why: A computer can carry a model through thousands of steps that would be too slow or too dangerous to run in reality. Simulation here means letting a formal description act out the process.
senses.whyCN: 计算机能把模型推进成千上万步，而在现实中跑这些步骤要么太慢、要么太危险。这里的仿真，就是让一份形式化描述“演”出整个过程。

senses.title: Training by simulated practice
senses.definition: to let a learner practise in an artificial setting that reproduces the pressures of the real task
senses.definitionCN: 让学习者在复现真实任务压力的人造环境中练习
senses.example: Pilots train on simulators before flying real aircraft.
senses.exampleCN: 飞行员在驾驶真飞机之前先在模拟器上训练。
senses.why: The point of simulated flight is that mistakes are cheap. The copy is close enough to transfer skill, yet detached enough to absorb failure.
senses.whyCN: 模拟飞行的意义在于犯错的代价很低。这个复本足够接近真实，使技能可以迁移；又足够脱离真实，使失败可以被吸收。

senses.title: To feign an attitude
senses.definition: to display an emotion or interest that one does not feel, usually for social reasons
senses.definitionCN: 表现出并未真正感受到的情绪或兴趣，通常出于社交原因
senses.example: She simulated interest in the lecture.
senses.exampleCN: 她假装对讲座感兴趣。
senses.why: Social life often requires the surface of an emotion without its substance. The word marks exactly that gap: the visible sign is produced, the inner state is not.
senses.whyCN: 社交生活常常需要情绪的表面，而不需要它的实质。这个词标记的正是那道缝隙：可见的信号被制造出来，内在状态却不存在。

senses.title: To model an outcome
senses.definition: to use a model to work out what would happen under given conditions, before the event occurs
senses.definitionCN: 用模型推算出在给定条件下会发生什么，且发生在事件之前
senses.example: Economists simulated the effect of the tax cut.
senses.exampleCN: 经济学家模拟了减税的效果。
senses.why: The model is a stand-in that can be pushed ahead of reality. Simulating an outcome is a way of trying the future at low cost.
senses.whyCN: 模型是现实的替身，可以被推到现实之前。模拟结果，就是用低成本的方式先“试一遍”未来。

senses.title: Simulating biological conditions
senses.definition: in biology and medicine, to reproduce the chemical or physical conditions of a living system
senses.definitionCN: 在生物学与医学中，重现生命系统的化学或物理条件
senses.example: The device simulates the acidity of the stomach.
senses.exampleCN: 该装置模拟胃部的酸度。
senses.why: Living systems are hard to open and hard to control. A simulated environment keeps the relevant parameters while removing the complexity that would confound the experiment.
senses.whyCN: 生命系统难以打开、也难以控制。模拟环境保留相关参数，同时去掉会干扰实验的复杂性。

senses.title: Simulated: the adjective of the artificial
senses.definition: the past participle works as an adjective meaning 'made to resemble something real, and not real itself'
senses.definitionCN: 过去分词作形容词，意为“被做成像真的、但本身并非真的”
senses.example: The aircraft landed on a simulated runway.
senses.exampleCN: 飞机降落在一条模拟跑道上。
senses.why: Once the participle becomes an adjective, the 'as if' is packed into a single word: simulated leather, simulated flavour, simulated emergency. The likeness is the point, and the absence of the original is understood.
senses.whyCN: 当分词变成形容词，“仿佛”就被压缩进一个词里：simulated leather、simulated flavour、simulated emergency。相似本身就是重点，而原物的缺席则是不言自明的。

intro.en: Simulate comes from Latin simulare 'to make like, imitate, represent', built on similis 'like'. English first used it in the 1620s for pretending; the technical sense 'reproduce conditions with a model' is a 20th-century development.
intro.cn: simulate 来自拉丁语 simulare“使相像、模仿、再现”，建立在 similis“像”之上。英语在 17 世纪 20 年代最早用它表示“假装”；“用模型重现条件”的技术义则是 20 世纪的发展。

items.en: Similis meant 'like, resembling'. It is the adjective behind the whole family, and its older relative semol 'together' points to PIE *sem- 'one, together'.
items.cn: similis 意为“相像的”。它是整个词族背后的形容词，其更早的亲属 semol“一起”指向原始印欧语 *sem-“一、一起”。

items.en: Simulare meant 'to make like, copy, imitate, represent', and also 'to pretend'. The verb could describe an artist copying a face or a person faking a feeling.
items.cn: simulare 意为“使相像、复制、模仿、再现”，也可表示“假装”。这个动词既能描述画家复制一张脸，也能描述一个人伪造一种情感。

items.en: The past participle simulatus 'made like, imitated, feigned' supplied the stem for the English verb. The Latin supine form simulatum also underlies the noun simulation.
items.cn: 过去分词 simulatus“被弄得相像的、被模仿的、被假装的”为英语动词提供了词干。拉丁语动名词形式 simulatum 也是名词 simulation 的基础。

items.en: English simulate is first recorded in the 1620s with the sense 'to feign, pretend'. It was either a back-formation from simulation or a direct borrowing of the Latin participle.
items.cn: 英语 simulate 最早记录于 17 世纪 20 年代，意为“假装、装作”。它要么是从 simulation 逆构而来，要么是直接借用了拉丁语分词。

items.en: The modern technical sense 'to imitate the working of a system, especially with a model or computer' is recorded from the mid-20th century (c. 1947), alongside the growth of simulators.
items.cn: 现代技术义“模仿某一系统的运作，尤指用模型或计算机”记录于 20 世纪中期（约 1947），与模拟器的兴起同步。

items.en: Simulation, simulator and simulated now cover engineering, medicine, economics and games. The old polarity survives: the copy may be offered as a tool, or offered as a deception.
items.cn: simulation、simulator、simulated 如今覆盖工程、医学、经济学与游戏。旧的二元性仍然存在：这个复本既可以作为工具提供，也可以作为骗局提供。

note.en: The look-alike group is the simul- family; the near-meaning group compares verbs of copying and pretending. Watch the difference between an honest model and a deliberate lie.
note.cn: 形近组是 simul- 词族；近义组比较表示复制与假装的动词。注意“诚实的模型”与“有意的谎言”之间的差别。

entries.definition: the act or result of simulating; a model that reproduces a real process. It is the noun of simulate.
entries.definitionCN: 模拟的行为或结果；重现真实过程的模型。它是 simulate 的名词。

entries.definition: a device or program that simulates conditions for training or study. It is the thing that does the simulating.
entries.definitionCN: 为训练或研究而模拟条件的装置或程序。它是执行模拟的那个东西。

entries.definition: to hide one's real feelings by pretending the opposite. The prefix dis- reverses the direction of the pretence.
entries.definitionCN: 通过装作相反的样子来掩盖真实情感。前缀 dis- 反转了伪装的方向。

entries.definition: to copy someone's actions or manner, often to learn or to entertain. It does not imply deception.
entries.definitionCN: 复制他人的行为或举止，常用于学习或娱乐。它不暗示欺骗。

entries.definition: to copy the sound or movement of something, often in a playful or exaggerated way.
entries.definitionCN: 复制某物的声音或动作，常带有戏仿或夸张。

entries.definition: to pretend to have a feeling or condition. It is close to the oldest sense of simulate.
entries.definitionCN: 假装拥有某种情感或状况。它接近 simulate 最古老的义项。

entries.definition: to try to equal or surpass someone by imitating their success. It adds striving, not pretence.
entries.definitionCN: 通过模仿他人的成功来试图赶上或超越。它增加了努力，而不是伪装。

normalIntro.en: Pictures: a flight simulator, a fake cough, a computer model of heat, a simulated runway.
normalIntro.cn: 画面：飞行模拟器、假装的咳嗽、热的计算机模型、模拟跑道。

normal.en: Similis is 'like': to simulate is to make something look or behave like the real thing.
normal.cn: similis 就是“像”：simulate 就是让某物看起来或表现得像真的。

normal.en: A flight simulator copies the cockpit but not the sky: the relevant parts are real, the danger is not.
normal.cn: 飞行模拟器复制了驾驶舱，却没有复制天空：相关部分是真实的，危险则不是。

normal.en: Simulate an illness is to fake it; simulate a climate is to model it. One deceives, the other studies.
normal.cn: simulate an illness 是装病；simulate a climate 是建模。前者骗人，后者研究。

normal.en: The noun pair: simulation is the process, simulator is the machine.
normal.cn: 名词配对：simulation 是过程，simulator 是机器。

normal.en: Simulated leather, simulated flavour: the adjective tells you the real material is absent.

examples.en: The program simulates how the virus spreads through a city.

examples.en: He simulated a headache to leave the meeting early.

examples.en: The astronauts trained in a simulated weightless environment.

root: 源自拉丁语 simulare“使相像、模仿、假装”，由 similis“相像的”派生；过去分词 simulatus 进入英语。核心是“做出一个像真的复本”，既可用于诚实的建模，也可用于欺骗性的假装。

sensesIntro.en: Simulate starts from a copy. The oldest sense is pretence: a person fakes an illness or an interest. The same act becomes respectable when the copy is meant to teach or to predict: an altitude chamber reproduces pressure, a computer runs a model, a pilot practises on a simulator, an economist tries the future before it arrives. The adjective simulated then carries the whole idea in one word: made to resemble something real, and not real itself.
sensesIntro.cn: simulate 的起点是一个复本。最古老的义项是伪装：一个人装病、装感兴趣。当复本被用来教学或预测时，同一个动作就变得正当：高压舱重现气压，计算机跑模型，飞行员在模拟器上练习，经济学家在未来到来之前先试一遍。形容词 simulated 则用一个词承载整个观念：被做成像真的，而本身并非真的。

core.en: Making a likeness: copying a surface, a condition or a process, with or without intent to deceive.
core.cn: 制造相似：复制表面、条件或过程，可能有意欺骗，也可能没有。

branches.en: PRETENCE: faking an illness, and faking an attitude, where the inner state is missing.
branches.cn: 伪装：装病与装态度，内在状态缺席。

branches.en: IMITATION: copying a walk, a voice or a manner for display.
branches.cn: 模仿：为展示而复制步态、声音或举止。

branches.en: REPRODUCTION: recreating real physical or biological conditions for study.
branches.cn: 重现：为研究而再造真实的物理或生理条件。

branches.en: MODELLING: running a system or an outcome through a model, often on a computer.
branches.cn: 建模：用模型推演系统或结果，常在计算机上运行。

branches.en: TRAINING AND ARTIFICE: simulated practice, and the adjective for things that only resemble the real.
branches.cn: 训练与人造：模拟练习，以及表示“只是像真的”的形容词。

intro.en: Simulate sits in the simil-/simul- family. The items below move from the Latin verb through the modern technical nouns to the adjective of artifice.
intro.cn: simulate 位于 simil-/simul- 词族中。下列条目从拉丁动词出发，经过现代技术名词，到达表示“人造”的形容词。

latinIntro.en: Latin similis 'like' gives simulare 'make like', whose participle simulatus supplies English simulate. Simulacrum adds the idea of a mere image or shadow.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 similis“像”派生出 simulare“使相像”，其分词 simulatus 提供英语 simulate。simulacrum 则加入“仅是影像或影子”的意思。

items.meaning: a device or program that simulates

items.example: They tested the material in simulated sunlight.
items.exampleCN: 他们在模拟阳光下测试该材料。

items.meaningCN: 模拟性的；有模仿作用的

items.example: The two cases are similar.

items.example: The parable works by similitude.
items.exampleCN: 这个寓言通过比喻起作用。

items.meaning: an image or imitation that lacks substance
items.meaningCN: 影像；幻影；徒有其表的东西
items.example: The town was a simulacrum of a real city.
items.exampleCN: 这座小镇只是一座真实城市的仿像。

definition_zh: 地点；场所；网站；遗址；工地
definition_en: a place where something is, happens, or is built
core_image: 地图上一个被图钉按住的小点：所有事都发生在这一点上
scene: 考古队在黄土坡上拉好网格，队长指着图纸说：This is the site of the ancient city.
sceneCN: 这里 site 是「遗址、考古现场」（第 3 个义项：过去某事发生并留下痕迹的地点）；句意：这里就是古城的遗址。图中可辨识物件：探方网格、刷子、标尺、图纸。
