senses.title: A place on the ground
senses.definition: a particular place where something is located or where an event takes place
senses.definitionCN: 某物所在或某事发生的特定地点
senses.example: The site was chosen for its flat ground.
senses.exampleCN: 这块地点因地面平坦而被选中。
senses.why: Latin situs means 'place, position', literally 'the place where something has been left'. The word starts as a point on the ground, fixed and locatable.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 situs 意为“地点、位置”，字面是“某物被放置之处”。这个词的起点就是地面上一个固定、可定位的点。

senses.title: A place under construction
senses.definition: an area of ground where a building or other structure is being put up
senses.definitionCN: 正在建造建筑物或其他结构的场地
senses.example: Safety helmets are required on the building site.
senses.exampleCN: 在建筑工地上必须戴安全帽。
senses.why: A site becomes a building site when work begins. The word shifts from 'where something is' to 'where something is being made', and the ground becomes a workspace.
senses.whyCN: 当施工开始，一块地点就成了 building site。词义从“某物所在之处”滑向“某物正在被制造之处”，地面变成了工作空间。

senses.title: A place that remembers: the historic site
senses.definition: a place where an ancient building, event or culture is preserved or studied
senses.definitionCN: 保存或研究古代建筑、事件或文化的地点
senses.example: The site has yielded thousands of fossils.
senses.exampleCN: 这处遗址已出土了数千件化石。
senses.why: In archaeology the place itself is the document. What happened there left traces in the ground, so the site is both a location and a record.
senses.whyCN: 在考古学里，地点本身就是文献。那里发生过的事在地层里留下痕迹，因此遗址既是位置，也是记录。

senses.title: The virtual site: website
senses.definition: a location on the internet where a set of pages or services is hosted
senses.definitionCN: 互联网上托管一组页面或服务的位置
senses.example: The company moved its site to a new server.
senses.exampleCN: 公司把网站迁到了新服务器。
senses.why: The internet borrowed the spatial word: a website is a 'place' you visit, with an address and pages. The metaphor treats the network as territory.
senses.whyCN: 互联网借用了这个空间词：网站是一个你可以“访问”的地方，有地址、有页面。这个隐喻把网络当成一片领土。

senses.title: The site of an event
senses.definition: the place where an accident, crime or important event happened
senses.definitionCN: 事故、犯罪或重大事件发生的地点
senses.example: Police sealed off the site of the explosion.
senses.exampleCN: 警方封锁了爆炸现场。
senses.why: An event leaves a place behind as its footprint. Saying 'the site of the accident' is a way of pointing at that footprint and treating the ground as evidence.
senses.whyCN: 事件会在身后留下一个地点作为脚印。“the site of the accident”这种说法就是在指认那个脚印，并把地面当作证据。

senses.title: A site on the body
senses.definition: in medicine, a particular point on or in the body where something occurs or is applied
senses.definitionCN: 在医学中，指身体上或体内某事发生或施术的特定位点
senses.example: The injection site was slightly swollen.
senses.exampleCN: 注射部位略有肿胀。
senses.why: The body is treated as a map with points on it. The site of infection or of injection is a location inside this small territory, precise enough to be named.
senses.whyCN: 身体被当成一张带点的地图。感染部位或注射部位就是这片小领土内部的一个位置，精确到可以被命名。

senses.title: A site in computing
senses.definition: in computing, a location that hosts data, software or services, often used in compounds such as site licence
senses.definitionCN: 在计算领域，托管数据、软件或服务的位置，常用于 site licence 等复合词
senses.example: The university has a site licence for the software.
senses.exampleCN: 该大学拥有这款软件的站点许可。
senses.why: When a whole organisation is treated as one 'place', a licence can be granted per site. The spatial metaphor again turns an abstract arrangement into a location.
senses.whyCN: 当整个机构被当成一个“地点”，许可就可以按 site 授予。空间隐喻再次把抽象的安排变成一个位置。

senses.title: To site: choosing the place
senses.definition: to place a building, facility or object at a particular location
senses.definitionCN: 把建筑物、设施或物体安置在特定位置
senses.example: They sited the new library near the station.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把新图书馆选址在车站附近。
senses.why: The noun turns into a verb when someone must decide the point on the map. To site something is to fix it at a place, which is the original meaning of situs made active.
senses.whyCN: 当人必须决定地图上的那个点时，名词就变成了动词。to site something 就是把它固定在某个地点，这正是 situs 原义的动作化。

senses.title: On-site and off-site
senses.definition: the compounds on-site and off-site describe work done at the place itself or somewhere else
senses.definitionCN: 复合词 on-site 与 off-site 分别指在本地现场或以外地点进行的工作
senses.example: The team provides both on-site and off-site support.
senses.exampleCN: 该团队既提供现场支持，也提供远程支持。
senses.why: Adding on or off to site creates a contrast of presence and absence. The place remains the reference point: work is either at it or away from it.
senses.whyCN: 在 site 前加 on 或 off，就造出“在场”与“不在场”的对照。地点仍是参照点：工作要么在它那里，要么离它而去。

intro.en: Site comes from Latin situs 'place, position', the past participle of sinere 'to let, leave'. It entered English through Anglo-French in the late 14th century with the plain sense 'place, ground'.
intro.cn: site 来自拉丁语 situs“地点、位置”，是 sinere“让、留下”的过去分词。它经盎格鲁-法语于 14 世纪晚期进入英语，最初就是“地点、地面”的意思。

items.en: Situs meant 'place, position, site', and also 'a leaving, a setting down'. It was the past participle of sinere, so a situs was literally 'something left or set down' in a spot.
items.cn: situs 意为“地点、位置、场所”，也有“放置、留下”之意。它是 sinere 的过去分词，所以 situs 字面上就是“被留在或放置在某个点上的东西”。

items.en: Sinere 'to let, allow, leave' supplied the participle. The verb describes permitting something to remain where it is, and its participle came to name the place where it remained.
items.cn: sinere“让、允许、留下”提供了这个分词。该动词描述允许某物留在原处，其分词后来就用来命名它留下的那个地点。

items.en: The deeper origin is uncertain. A connection with PIE *tkei- 'to settle, dwell' has been proposed, which would link situs to the idea of settling on land, but it is not firmly established.
items.cn: 更深的来源不确定。有说法把它与原始印欧语 *tkei-“定居、居住”联系起来，这样 situs 就与“在土地上安顿下来”的观念相关，但这一联系并未牢固确立。

items.en: Anglo-French carried site into English in the late 14th century. The earliest uses are concrete: a place, a piece of ground, the spot where a building stands.
items.cn: 盎格鲁-法语在 14 世纪晚期把 site 带进英语。最早的用法是具体的：一个地点、一块地面、建筑物所在的那块地。

items.en: The word widened from a building plot to the ground of a battle, an event or a ruin. By the 19th century 'the site of' was a standard way to point at a place charged with history.
items.cn: 这个词从建筑地块扩展到战役、事件或废墟所在的地面。到 19 世纪，“the site of”已成为指认一处承载历史的地点的标准说法。

items.en: The 20th century added the abstract and technical uses: construction site, archaeological site, medical site, and finally website in the 1990s, when the network was imagined as a set of places.
items.cn: 20 世纪增加了抽象与技术用法：construction site、archaeological site、医学上的 site，最后是 20 世纪 90 年代的 website——当时人们把网络想象成一组地点。

note.en: The look-alike group is the cit-/sight/situ- cluster, which is easy to confuse in spelling and sound; the near-meaning group compares words for place.
note.cn: 形近组是 cit-/sight/situ- 这一簇，拼写与读音都容易混淆；近义组比较表示“地点”的词。

entries.definitionCN: 引用或提及某一来源。它与 site 同音，但意义毫无关联。

entries.definition: the ability to see, or something worth seeing. It is another unrelated homophone.
entries.definitionCN: 视力，或值得一看的景物。它是另一个无关的同音词。

entries.definition: to place something in a particular position. It is the verb built on Latin situs.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物安置在特定位置。它是建立在拉丁语 situs 之上的动词。

entries.definition: a place or position, especially one identified by coordinates or features. It is more neutral than site.
entries.definitionCN: 地点或位置，尤指可用坐标或特征确定的位置。它比 site 更中性。

entries.definition: a general word for any area or point. It is the broadest member of the group.
entries.definitionCN: 表示任何区域或点的通用词。它是这一组里最宽泛的词。

entries.definition: the place where an organised event is held. It is used for concerts, conferences and matches.
entries.definitionCN: 举办有组织活动的地点。它用于音乐会、会议和比赛。

entries.definition: the place of something relative to other things. It stresses relations rather than the ground itself.
entries.definitionCN: 某物相对于其他事物的位置。它强调关系，而不是地面本身。

root: 源自拉丁语 situs“地点、位置”，为 sinere“让、留下”的过去分词；经盎格鲁-法语于 14 世纪晚期进入英语。核心是“某物被放置下来的那个点”，由此扩展到工地、遗址、身体部位与网站。

sensesIntro.en: Site begins as a pin on the ground: the place where a thing has been set down. From that point it grows outward. Work turns the place into a construction site; history turns it into an archaeological site; an accident turns it into the site of an event; medicine maps sites onto the body; computing maps them onto the network as websites and site licences. The verb then reverses the direction: instead of naming where something is, it chooses where something will be.
sensesIntro.cn: site 的起点是地面上的一枚图钉：某物被放置下来的那个点。从这里向外生长：施工把地点变成建筑工地，历史把它变成考古遗址，事故把它变成事件现场，医学把位点画到身体上，计算把位点画到网络上，成为 website 与 site licence。动词则反过来：不再命名某物在哪里，而是决定某物将要在哪里。

core.en: A fixed point on the ground where something is, happens or is built.
core.cn: 地面上一个固定的点：某物所在、某事发生或某物被建造之处。

branches.en: PHYSICAL PLACE: a located spot, and ground under construction.
branches.cn: 物理地点：可定位的一点，以及施工中的地面。

branches.en: HISTORY AND EVIDENCE: the archaeological site and the scene of an event.
branches.cn: 历史与证据：考古遗址与事件现场。

branches.en: BODY: a precise point on or in the body, such as an injection site.
branches.cn: 身体：身体表面或内部的精确位点，如注射部位。

branches.en: NETWORK: the website and the site licence, the place metaphor applied to computing.
branches.cn: 网络：网站与站点许可，把“地点”隐喻用于计算。

branches.en: ACTION AND RELATION: to site something, and the on-site/off-site contrast.
branches.cn: 动作与关系：为某物选址，以及 on-site/off-site 的对照。

intro.en: Site is a small family with a large reach. The items below follow Latin situs into English nouns, verbs and compounds, including the modern website.
intro.cn: site 是一个小而覆盖广的词族。下列条目从拉丁语 situs 追到英语名词、动词与复合词，包括现代的 website。

latinIntro.en: Latin situs 'place' comes from sinere 'to let, leave'. Late Latin situare 'to place' gave English situate, and the abstract noun situation followed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 situs“地点”来自 sinere“让、留下”。晚期拉丁语 situare“放置”给出英语 situate，抽象名词 situation 随之而来。

forms.label: 形容词（绝对形容词，无比较级）

senses.title: One and only
senses.definition: being the only one of its kind in a given situation
senses.definitionCN: 在特定情形下是同类中唯一的一个
senses.example: The sole reason for the delay was bad weather.
senses.exampleCN: 延误的唯一原因是天气恶劣。
senses.why: Latin solus means 'alone, single'. The adjective counts to one and stops: there is no second item to compare with, so the word often carries the force of 'and nothing else'.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 solus 意为“独自的、单一的”。这个形容词数到一就停下：没有第二个项可以比较，因此常带“再无其他”的力量。

senses.title: Exclusive: belonging to one party only
senses.definition: held by one person or group to the exclusion of all others
senses.definitionCN: 由一个人或一个群体持有，排除其他所有人
senses.example: The company has sole rights to the drug.
senses.exampleCN: 该公司拥有该药物的独家权利。
senses.why: Alone becomes exclusive when a right is involved. If only one party holds it, all others are shut out; the numerical 'one' turns into a legal boundary.
senses.whyCN: 当涉及权利时，“独自”就变成“独占”。如果只有一方持有，其他各方都被挡在门外；数量上的“一”变成了法律上的边界。

senses.title: The bottom of the foot
senses.definition: the under-surface of the foot, the part that rests on the ground
senses.definitionCN: 脚的底面，即接触地面的那一面
senses.example: She felt a sharp pain in the sole of her foot.
senses.exampleCN: 她感到脚底一阵刺痛。
senses.why: This sense has a different source: Latin solea 'sandal, sole', from solum 'bottom, ground'. The foot's sole is literally its 'ground' side, the surface that meets the earth.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项来源不同：拉丁语 solea“凉鞋、鞋底”，出自 solum“底部、地面”。脚底字面上就是脚的“地面”那一面，与大地相接的表面。

senses.title: The bottom of a shoe
senses.definition: the layer of material under a shoe that touches the ground
senses.definitionCN: 鞋底下接触地面的那层材料
senses.example: These boots have thick rubber soles.
senses.exampleCN: 这双靴子有厚实的橡胶鞋底。
senses.why: The shoe repeats the foot: whatever meets the ground is its sole. The word moved from the body to the object worn on the body, keeping the same spatial role.
senses.whyCN: 鞋子重复了脚的结构：凡是接触地面的那一层就是它的 sole。词从身体移到穿在身体上的物件，保留着同一个空间角色。

senses.title: The flatfish called sole
senses.definition: a flatfish with a flattened body, named for its resemblance to the sole of a shoe
senses.definitionCN: 一种身体扁平的比目鱼，因形似鞋底而得名
senses.example: The restaurant serves grilled sole with lemon.
senses.exampleCN: 这家餐厅供应柠檬烤鳎鱼。
senses.why: This is a third, independent word. The fish was named in the Middle Ages for its flat, sole-shaped body, so the naming is a comparison rather than a derivation.
senses.whyCN: 这是第三个独立的词。这种鱼在中世纪因扁平、形似鞋底的身体而得名，所以这是比喻性命名，而不是词源派生。

senses.title: Alone: the literary sense
senses.definition: in literary or archaic use, being without companions; lone
senses.definitionCN: 在文学或古旧用法中，指没有同伴的；孤身一人的
senses.example: He was the sole survivor of the shipwreck.
senses.exampleCN: 他是这场海难唯一的幸存者。
senses.why: The original Latin sense was simply 'alone'. Modern English keeps a trace of it in phrases like sole survivor, where the person is both the only one left and entirely without company.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语原义就是“独自的”。现代英语在 sole survivor 一类短语里保留了它的痕迹：这个人既是唯一剩下的，也完全无人作伴。

senses.title: Sole proprietor: one person owns it
senses.definition: in business and law, describing an owner who has no partners and bears the whole liability
senses.definitionCN: 在商业与法律中，指没有合伙人、承担全部责任的业主
senses.example: She runs the shop as a sole proprietor.
senses.exampleCN: 她以独资经营者的身份经营这家店。
senses.why: The legal phrase makes the 'one' explicit: one owner, one set of responsibilities, no division. Sole here means both 'single' and 'undivided'.
senses.whyCN: 这个法律短语把“一”说得很明白：一个业主、一套责任、没有分摊。这里的 sole 既是“单一”，也是“不可分割”。

senses.title: To sole a shoe
senses.definition: to put a new sole on a shoe or boot
senses.definitionCN: 给鞋或靴子装上新底
senses.example: The cobbler soled the boots while I waited.
senses.exampleCN: 鞋匠在我等候时给靴子换了底。
senses.why: The noun becomes a verb: to give a thing its ground-contact layer. The action is narrow and concrete, and it keeps the image of the sole as the part that meets the earth.
senses.whyCN: 名词变成动词：给某物装上接触地面的那一层。这个动作范围窄而具体，仍保留“鞋底是与大地相接的那一层”这一意象。

senses.title: Solely: nothing but that
senses.definition: the adverb solely means 'only, and for no other reason or by no other means'
senses.definitionCN: 副词 solely 意为“仅仅，且不为其他理由、不靠其他手段”
senses.example: The decision was based solely on the evidence.
senses.exampleCN: 这个决定完全基于证据。
senses.why: Adding -ly turns 'one' into a limitation on a whole action: nothing else entered into it. The adverb is the numerical core of sole applied to causes and means.
senses.whyCN: 加 -ly 把“一”变成对整个动作的限制：没有别的因素进入其中。这个副词就是 sole 的数量核心，被应用到原因与手段上。

intro.en: Sole is really three words that look alike. The adjective comes from Latin solus 'alone'. The foot and shoe sense comes from Latin solea 'sandal, sole', from solum 'bottom, ground'. The fish was named after the shoe sole. None of them is related to sol 'sun'.
intro.cn: sole 实际上是三个外形相同的词。形容词来自拉丁语 solus“独自的”。脚底与鞋底义来自拉丁语 solea“凉鞋、鞋底”，出自 solum“底部、地面”。鱼名则是照着鞋底的样子起的。三者都与表示“太阳”的 sol 无关。

items.en: Solus meant 'alone, single, only'. Its own origin is uncertain: it has been connected with se 'oneself' and with the reflexive PIE root *swo-, but no derivation is firmly established.
items.cn: solus 意为“独自的、单一的、唯一的”。它自身的来源不确定：有说法把它与 se“自己”以及反身代词性的原始印欧语词根 *swo- 联系起来，但没有任何派生关系被牢固确立。

items.en: Old French soul carried Latin solus into English in the late 14th century. The adjective kept the sense 'single, alone', and from it grew the legal sense 'exclusive'.
items.cn: 古法语 soul 在 14 世纪晚期把拉丁语 solus 带进英语。这个形容词保留“单一的、独自的”之义，并从中生长出法律上的“独占”义。

items.en: The foot and shoe sense is a separate line: solea 'sandal, sole' came from solum 'bottom, ground, soil'. Solum's own origin is uncertain; de Vaan suggests a possible PIE *se/ol-o- 'place, habitation'.
items.cn: 脚底与鞋底义是另一条线：solea“凉鞋、鞋底”出自 solum“底部、地面、土壤”。solum 自身的来源不确定；de Vaan 提出可能与原始印欧语 *se/ol-o-“地点、居所”有关。

items.en: The flatfish called sole is recorded from the mid-13th century. It was named for its flat, sole-shaped body, so the fish sense is a comparison with the shoe part, not a development from it.
items.cn: 名为 sole 的比目鱼记录于 13 世纪中期。它因扁平、形似鞋底的身体而得名，所以鱼义是与鞋底部件的比喻关系，而不是从鞋底义发展来的。

items.en: The verb 'to furnish a shoe with a sole' is recorded from the 1560s. English commonly turns a concrete noun into a verb this way: the object names the part being supplied.
items.cn: 动词“给鞋装底”记录于 16 世纪 60 年代。英语常这样把具体名词变成动词：宾语命名了被提供的那一部分。

items.en: Latin sol 'sun' (as in solar, solstice) is a different word with a different origin. Sole 'alone', sole 'shoe bottom' and sole 'fish' do not come from it, and the resemblance is accidental.
items.cn: 拉丁语 sol“太阳”（见于 solar、solstice）是另一个来源不同的词。sole“独自”、sole“鞋底”与 sole“鱼”都不来自它，外形相似纯属偶然。

note.en: The look-alike group is the sound-alike cluster soul/solar/solo; the near-meaning group compares words for being the only one.
note.cn: 形近组是 soul/solar/solo 这一簇同音或形近词；近义组比较表示“唯一”的词。

entries.definition: the spiritual part of a person. It sounds exactly like sole but has no connection in meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 人的精神部分。它与 sole 读音完全相同，但意义毫无关联。

entries.definition: relating to the sun, from Latin sol 'sun'. It is often wrongly linked to sole.
entries.definitionCN: 与太阳有关的，来自拉丁语 sol“太阳”。它常被误认为与 sole 有关。

entries.definition: performed by one person alone. It comes from Latin solus through Italian.
entries.definitionCN: 由一人独自表演的。它经意大利语来自拉丁语 solus。

entries.definition: the single one and no other. It is the most everyday word for the numerical sense of sole.
entries.definitionCN: 唯一的一个，没有别的。它是表示 sole 数量义最日常的词。

entries.definition: consisting of one part or one person. It stresses the count rather than exclusivity.
entries.definitionCN: 由一个部分或一个人组成的。它强调数量，而不是排他性。

entries.definition: restricted to one person or group. It matches the legal sense of sole.
entries.definitionCN: 仅限于一人或一个群体。它与 sole 的法律义对应。

entries.definition: alone, with no companions. It matches the literary sense of sole, not the legal one.
entries.definitionCN: 独自一人，没有同伴。它与 sole 的书面义对应，而不是法律义。

normalIntro.en: Pictures: one footprint on a turned-up shoe, a contract held by one company, a flatfish on a plate.
normalIntro.cn: 画面：翻过来的鞋上只有一个脚印、一家公司独占的合同、盘子里的一条鳎鱼。

normal.en: Solus means 'alone': the sole reason is the one reason with no others beside it.
normal.cn: solus 就是“独自”：the sole reason 就是唯一的原因，旁边没有别的。

normal.en: Foot sole and shoe sole come from solea/solum, a different line from solus; they are not the same word.
normal.cn: 脚底与鞋底来自 solea/solum，与 solus 是另一条线；它们不是同一个词。

normal.en: The fish is called sole because it is flat like a shoe sole, not because it is lonely.
normal.cn: 这种鱼叫 sole，是因为它扁得像鞋底，不是因为它孤独。

sensesIntro.en: Sole is a word that happens to have three bodies. The adjective counts to one: one reason, one owner, one survivor. The noun sole is the ground-contact layer, first of the foot and then of the shoe, and a flatfish borrowed the name because it looks like that layer. The verb is the smallest step of all: to give a shoe its sole. Keep the sources apart, and the many senses fall into three clear families.
sensesIntro.cn: sole 是一个恰好有三个身体的词。形容词数到一：一个原因、一个业主、一个幸存者。名词 sole 是接触地面的那一层，先是脚底，再是鞋底，而一种扁平的鱼因为像这一层而借用了这个名字。动词是最小的一步：给鞋装上底。把来源分清，众多义项就落进三个清晰的家族。

core.en: One, and the one surface that meets the ground: two different Latin sources that share an English spelling.

branches.en: SINGLE AND EXCLUSIVE: from the number one to a right held by one party alone.

branches.en: GROUND-CONTACT LAYER: the sole of the foot and of the shoe, from solea and solum.
branches.cn: 接触地面的层：脚底与鞋底，来自 solea 与 solum。

branches.en: FISH: the flatfish named after the shape of a shoe sole.
branches.cn: 鱼：因形似鞋底而得名的鳎鱼。

branches.en: ALONE AND UNDIVIDED: the literary lone survivor and the legal sole proprietor.
branches.cn: 独自与不可分：文学中的孤身幸存者与法律上的独资业主。

branches.en: ACTION AND LIMIT: to sole a shoe, and solely as a restriction to one cause.
branches.cn: 动作与限制：给鞋换底，以及 solely 把范围限制到唯一原因。

intro.en: Sole has two families behind one spelling: solus 'alone' and solea/solum 'bottom'. The items below mark which family each word belongs to.

latinIntro.en: Latin solus 'alone' gives sole, solely, solo, solitude and solitary. Latin solea 'sandal' and solum 'bottom' give the foot and shoe senses. Latin sol 'sun' is a separate word and is listed only to mark the contrast.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 solus“独自”给出 sole、solely、solo、solitude、solitary。拉丁语 solea“凉鞋”与 solum“底部”给出脚底与鞋底义。拉丁语 sol“太阳”是另一个词，列出它只为标明对照。

senses.title: A little, but not very
senses.definition: to a small or moderate degree, placed before an adjective or adverb
senses.definitionCN: 达到较小或中等程度，置于形容词或副词之前
senses.example: The room was somewhat cold.
senses.exampleCN: 房间里有点冷。
senses.why: Some means 'a certain part', and what means 'which thing'. Together they name an unspecified portion of a quality: not none, not all, but a measurable slice.
senses.whyCN: some 意为“某一部分”，what 意为“哪一个东西”。两者合起来命名一种性质中未被指明的那一部分：不是没有，也不是全部，而是一片可度量的份额。

senses.title: In some measure: hedging a judgement
senses.titleCN: 在某种程度上：给判断留余地
senses.definition: used to soften a statement so that it is true only in part
senses.definitionCN: 用于缓和陈述，使其只在部分意义上成立
senses.example: The results were somewhat disappointing.
senses.exampleCN: 结果有点令人失望。
senses.why: The word is a hedge. It lets a speaker say that a quality is present without committing to how strongly, which is exactly what 'a certain part' allows.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是一种模糊限制语。它让说话人承认某种性质存在，却不必承诺它有多强，而“某一部分”恰好允许这种保留。

senses.title: Before a comparative: a step, not a leap
senses.titleCN: 修饰比较级：一小步，不是一大步
senses.definition: used before a comparative to mean 'a little more' or 'a little less'
senses.definitionCN: 用于比较级之前，表示“稍多一点”或“稍少一点”
senses.example: This version is somewhat easier to read.
senses.exampleCN: 这个版本读起来稍微容易一些。
senses.why: A comparative already marks a direction; somewhat sets the size of the step. The two together say 'the difference is real, but modest'.
senses.whyCN: 比较级已经标出方向；somewhat 则规定这一步的大小。两者合起来表示“差异确实存在，但不大”。

senses.title: Somewhat of a: partly one kind of thing
senses.definition: in the phrase 'somewhat of a + noun', describing someone or something as partly, but not fully, that thing
senses.definitionCN: 在 somewhat of a + 名词 的结构中，表示某人或某物部分地、而非完全地属于那一类
senses.example: He is somewhat of a poet.
senses.exampleCN: 他有点诗人的气质。
senses.why: The 'of' phrase measures a portion of an identity. Calling a person somewhat of a poet says they have a poet's part without claiming the whole title.
senses.whyCN: of 短语衡量的是一种身份中的份额。说某人是 somewhat of a poet，是说他们身上有诗人的那一部分，却不宣称拥有完整的头衔。

senses.title: The old noun: a certain something
senses.definition: in older usage, an unspecified thing or an indefinite amount
senses.definitionCN: 在较古的用法中，指未指明的事物或不确定的数量
senses.example: There is somewhat in his story that troubles me.
senses.exampleCN: 他的叙述里有些东西让我不安。
senses.why: The noun sense is older: some + what literally names 'a certain thing'. Modern English has largely handed this job to something, leaving somewhat to the degree adverb.
senses.whyCN: 名词义更古老：some 加 what 字面上就是“某个东西”。现代英语基本把这个任务交给了 something，只把 somewhat 留作程度副词。

senses.title: A formal register
senses.definition: in writing and careful speech, a more formal alternative to 'a bit' or 'kind of'
senses.definitionCN: 在书面语与正式口语中，作为 a bit 或 kind of 的更正式替代
senses.example: The proposal is somewhat controversial among members.
senses.exampleCN: 该提案在成员中颇有争议。
senses.why: Because the word names only a portion and does not exaggerate, it suits reports and academic prose. It signals care rather than casualness.
senses.whyCN: 因为这个词只命名一部分、也不夸张，它适合报告与学术文体。它传递的是谨慎，而不是随便。

senses.title: The middle of the scale
senses.titleCN: 程度刻度上的中间位置
senses.definition: occupying a position between 'a little' and 'quite', neither minimal nor strong
senses.definitionCN: 处在“一点儿”与“相当”之间，既不是极小也不是强烈
senses.example: The two colours are somewhat similar.
senses.exampleCN: 这两种颜色有些相似。
senses.why: Degree words form a scale. Somewhat sits low on that scale: above 'slightly' in some uses, below 'quite' and 'very', and it refuses to specify an exact value.
senses.whyCN: 程度词构成一个刻度。somewhat 位于这个刻度的低段：在某些用法中高于 slightly，低于 quite 与 very，并且拒绝给出精确值。

senses.title: Compared with nearby degree words
senses.definition: distinguished from slightly, rather, fairly and quite by its blend of modesty and formality
senses.definitionCN: 以谦抑与正式的混合色彩，区别于 slightly、rather、fairly 与 quite
senses.example: It is somewhat unusual, rather than slightly unusual or quite unusual.
senses.exampleCN: 它是有几分不寻常，而不是略微不寻常或相当不寻常。
senses.why: Each degree word has its own flavour. Slightly is minimal and neutral; rather is subjective and often evaluative; fairly is moderate; quite is stronger. Somewhat is the detached, report-like member of the set.
senses.whyCN: 每个程度词都有自己的味道。slightly 极小且中性；rather 主观、常带评价；fairly 中等；quite 更强。somewhat 则是这一组里超然而像报告的那一个。

senses.title: A transparent compound
senses.definition: a native English compound of 'some' and 'what', whose parts still show through the whole
senses.definitionCN: 由 some 与 what 构成的英语本族复合词，其组成部分在整体中仍然可见
senses.example: The word is written as one unit: somewhat, not some what.
senses.exampleCN: 这个词写作一个单位 somewhat，而不是 some what。
senses.why: English builds many such compounds with some-: something, sometime, sometimes, somewhere, somehow. Somewhat is the one that turned into a degree word, but its two parts are still readable.
senses.whyCN: 英语用 some- 造了许多这类复合词：something、sometime、sometimes、somewhere、somehow。somewhat 是其中变成程度词的那一个，但它的两个部分仍然读得出来。

intro.en: Somewhat is a native English compound, not a Latin borrowing: Old English sum 'some' plus hwæt 'what'. It appears around 1200 as an adverb and soon after as a noun, and has no Latin source.
intro.cn: somewhat 是英语本族复合词，不是拉丁语借词：古英语 sum“某个”加 hwæt“什么”。它约在 1200 年作为副词出现，不久后也作名词使用，没有拉丁语来源。

items.en: The two parts are Old English sum 'some, a certain' and hwæt 'what'. Both are native Germanic words, so the compound was built inside English rather than borrowed.
items.cn: 两个组成部分是古英语 sum“某个、某一”与 hwæt“什么”。两者都是本族日耳曼词，所以这个复合词是在英语内部造出来的，而不是借来的。

items.en: The adverb is recorded around 1200 with the sense 'to some extent, in some measure'. The written forms include somwhat and sumwhat.
items.cn: 副词形式约在 1200 年见于记录，意为“在某种程度上、在某种程度上”。书写形式包括 somwhat 与 sumwhat。

items.en: A noun use appears in the early 13th century meaning 'something, a certain thing'. This sense is now archaic, having been taken over by something.
items.cn: 名词用法在 13 世纪早期出现，意为“某物、某个东西”。这个义项现已古旧，其功能已被 something 接管。

items.en: The new compound largely replaced the older Old English phrases sumdæl and sume dæle 'in some part', which expressed the same partial quantity.
items.cn: 这个新复合词在很大程度上取代了更早的古英语短语 sumdæl 与 sume dæle“在某一部分”，后者表达同样的部分数量。

items.en: Middle English shows somwhat, sumwhat and other variants before the spelling settled as somewhat. The two parts were sometimes still written apart.
items.cn: 中古英语中出现 somwhat、sumwhat 等变体，后来拼写才固定为 somewhat。两个部分有时仍分开书写。

items.en: Modern English keeps the degree adverb and the phrase somewhat of a. The word remains a native compound; it has no Latin or Greek ancestry, so no Latin entries are listed for it.
items.cn: 现代英语保留程度副词用法以及 somewhat of a 短语。这个词始终是本族复合词，没有拉丁或希腊语祖先，因此不为它列出拉丁语条目。

note.en: The look-alike group is the some- compound family; the near-meaning group compares degree words. Watch register: somewhat is more formal than a bit.
note.cn: 形近组是 some- 复合词家族；近义组比较程度词。注意语体：somewhat 比 a bit 更正式。

entries.definition: in or to some place. It is the place member of the some- family.
entries.definitionCN: 在某处或到某处。它是 some- 家族中表示地点的成员。

entries.definition: in some way, or for some unknown reason. It is the manner member of the family.
entries.definitionCN: 以某种方式，或由于某种未知原因。它是家族中表示方式的成员。

entries.definition: a thing that is not specified. It took over the old noun sense of somewhat.
entries.definitionCN: 未被指明的事物。它接管了 somewhat 古老的名词义。

entries.definition: to a very small degree. It is smaller and more neutral than somewhat.
entries.definitionCN: 达到极小的程度。它比 somewhat 更小、更中性。

entries.definition: to a noticeable degree, often with the speaker's judgement attached.
entries.definitionCN: 达到明显程度，常带有说话人的评价。

entries.definition: to a moderate degree, more strongly than slightly but less than very.
entries.definitionCN: 达到中等程度，强于 slightly，弱于 very。

entries.definition: a little; the everyday spoken equivalent of somewhat.
entries.definitionCN: 一点儿；somewhat 的日常口语对应说法。

normalIntro.en: Pictures: a thermometer stopped one mark above neutral, a résumé on a desk, a scale running from slightly to very.
normalIntro.cn: 画面：停在刻度上方一格温度计、桌上的简历、从 slightly 排到 very 的刻度。

normal.en: Some + what: a certain part of 'what' — that is, a certain degree of a quality.
normal.cn: some 加 what：某个“什么”的一部分——也就是某种性质的一定程度。

normal.en: Somewhat cold is colder than 'slightly cold' and warmer than 'quite cold'.
normal.cn: somewhat cold 比 slightly cold 更冷，比 quite cold 更暖。

normal.en: Somewhat of a poet means you have a poet's part, not the whole title.
normal.cn: somewhat of a poet 意思是身上有诗人的那一部分，而不是完整的头衔。

normal.en: The degree ladder: a little < somewhat < fairly < quite < very.
normal.cn: 程度阶梯：a little < somewhat < fairly < quite < very。

normal.en: Do not put somewhat at the end of a clause; it sits right before the word it limits.
normal.cn: 不要把 somewhat 放到句末；它紧贴在所修饰的词前面。

abstract.en: One schema: SOME → PART → DEGREE → HEDGE → COMPARISON → REGISTER.
abstract.cn: 一个图式：某个 → 部分 → 程度 → 模糊限制 → 比较 → 语体。

abstract.en: Word-building check: some + what = somewhat; the same prefix builds something, somewhere and somehow.
abstract.cn: 构词检查：some + what = somewhat；同一前缀还造出 something、somewhere、somehow。

abstract.en: Contrast: slightly is minimal, rather is subjective, fairly is moderate, a bit is colloquial, somewhat is formal and detached.
abstract.cn: 对照：slightly 极小，rather 主观，fairly 中等，a bit 口语，somewhat 正式而超然。

examples.en: The instructions were somewhat unclear.
examples.cn: 这些说明有点不清楚。

examples.en: He is somewhat of a mystery to his colleagues.
examples.cn: 对同事们来说，他有点神秘。

examples.en: Prices have risen somewhat since last year.
examples.cn: 自去年以来价格略有上涨。

dict_mnemonic.text: “萨姆沃特”——萨姆（Sam）喝（what）了一（点）水 → somewhat 有点、稍微

root: 英语本族复合词：古英语 sum“某个”加 hwæt“什么”，约 1200 年固定为副词，表示“在某种程度上”。它没有拉丁语或希腊语来源，其组成部分在现代英语中仍清晰可见。

sensesIntro.en: Somewhat names a part of a quality. It began as 'some' plus 'what', an unspecified portion of a thing, and settled into a degree adverb: somewhat cold, somewhat surprising. It is the detached, formal member of the degree scale, useful for hedging a judgement, for softening a comparison, and for the phrase somewhat of a, which grants someone a part of an identity without the whole title. Its old noun sense has been taken over by something.
sensesIntro.cn: somewhat 命名的是某种性质中的一部分。它起初是 some 加 what，指事物中未被指明的一份，后来固定为程度副词：somewhat cold、somewhat surprising。它是程度刻度上超然而正式的一员，适合给判断留余地、缓和比较，也适合 somewhat of a 这一短语——它给人某种身份的一部分，而不给完整的头衔。它古老的名词义已被 something 接管。

core.en: A certain part of a quality: not none, not all, but an unnamed moderate degree.
core.cn: 某种性质中的某一份额：不是没有，不是全部，而是未指明的中等程度。

branches.en: DEGREE: a little but not very, and the middle position on the scale.
branches.cn: 程度：有点但不算很，以及刻度上的中间位置。

branches.en: HEDGING AND REGISTER: softening a judgement, and the formal tone of reports.
branches.cn: 模糊限制与语体：缓和判断，以及报告体的正式语气。

branches.en: COMPARISON: a modest step before a comparative, contrasted with other degree words.
branches.cn: 比较：比较级前的温和一步，并与其他程度词形成对照。

branches.en: PARTIAL IDENTITY: somewhat of a, granting a part of a title rather than the whole.
branches.cn: 部分身份：somewhat of a，给出头衔的一部分而非全部。

branches.en: WORD HISTORY: the archaic noun 'something', and the transparent some- compound.
branches.cn: 词史：古老的名词义“某物”，以及构词透明的 some- 复合词。

intro.en: Somewhat is a native compound, so its 'affixes' are really its parts and the compounds built with the same prefix. The items below show the some- family and its transparent structure.
intro.cn: somewhat 是本族复合词，所以它的“词缀”实际上是它的组成部分以及用同一前缀造出的复合词。下列条目展示 some- 家族及其透明的结构。

latinIntro.en: There are no Latin entries for somewhat: it is an Old English compound of sum and hwæt, with no Latin or Greek ancestor. The list is left empty on purpose.
latinIntro.cn: somewhat 没有拉丁语条目：它是古英语 sum 与 hwæt 的复合词，没有拉丁或希腊语祖先。清单按设计留空。

items.meaning: to some degree; a certain part
items.example: The task is somewhat difficult.
items.exampleCN: 这项任务有点难。

items.meaning: an unspecified amount or particular one
items.example: Some students stayed behind.
items.exampleCN: 一些学生留了下来。

items.example: What do you mean?
items.exampleCN: 你是什么意思？

items.example: Something moved in the dark.
items.exampleCN: 黑暗中有东西动了。

items.example: Let's meet sometime next week.
items.exampleCN: 我们下周找个时间见吧。

items.example: Sometimes the bus is late.
items.exampleCN: 公交车有时会晚点。

items.example: I left my keys somewhere.
items.exampleCN: 我把钥匙落在某处了。

items.meaningCN: 以某种方式；不知怎么地
items.example: Somehow she finished on time.
items.exampleCN: 不知怎么的，她按时完成了。

items.example: Someone is knocking at the door.
items.exampleCN: 有人在敲门。

items.meaning: partly, but not fully, a certain kind of person or thing
items.example: She is somewhat of a legend here.
items.exampleCN: 她在这里算得上是个传奇人物。
